- Groups are placement groups that define where database replicas live; databases belong to a group
- Database connection via libsql protocol: `libsql://dbname-orgname.turso.io`
- Per-database auth tokens generated via `POST /v1/organizations/{org}/databases/{name}/auth/tokens`
- Connection string format for the SQL driver: `libsql://host?authToken=TOKEN` — the libsql driver parses the authToken from the query parameter
- `resourceSqlDriver` declared on `turso-database` with driver `"libsql"` and `connectionStringOutputKey: "connectionString"`
- SQL node driver (`./driver`) uses `@libsql/client` — registered in `drivers.ts` as `libsql`
- Supports create/delete for both groups and databases
- Database status: sleeping→degraded, active→healthy
- Resource ID format: `{accountId}:{typeId}:{dbName}` or `{accountId}:{typeId}:{groupName}`
- 30+ edge locations available for group placement (3-letter IATA codes: iad, fra, nrt, etc.)

### PlanetScale (`@infrawrench/plugin-planetscale`)

- Auth: Service token — `Authorization: {serviceTokenId}:{serviceTokenSecret}` against `https://api.planetscale.com/v1`
- Credentials: `serviceTokenId`, `serviceTokenSecret` (sensitive), `organizationName` (org slug)
- Resource types: `ps-database`, `ps-branch` + `ps-deploy-request` (children of ps-database), `ps-password` + `ps-backup` (children of ps-branch)
- PlanetScale is MySQL-compatible (built on Vitess); branches are isolated schema environments with their own connection endpoints
- Branch connection: `POST /v1/organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{branch}/passwords` creates a password, then builds `mysql://user:pass@host/database`
- SQL node driver (`./driver`) is `mysql-planetscale` — wraps mysql2 with TLS forced on (PlanetScale requires encrypted connections); registered in `drivers.ts`
- `resourceSqlDriver` declared on `ps-branch` with driver `"mysql-planetscale"` and `connectionStringOutputKey: "connectionString"`
- Supports create/delete for both databases and branches
- Database state mapping: ready→healthy, awaiting_import→provisioning, else→error
- Branch status: ready→healthy, else→provisioning
- Resource ID format: `{accountId}:ps-database:{databaseName}` or `{accountId}:ps-branch:{databaseName}/{branchName}`
- Regions: AWS regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west, eu-central, ap-south, ap-southeast, ap-northeast, sa-east, ap-southeast-2)

### Cloudflare (`@infrawrench/plugin-cloudflare`)

- Auth: API Token (scoped, created at dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens), passed as `Bearer` token to `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4`
- **The `cloudflare` SDK is held at `~6.4.0` on purpose** (in plugin-cloudflare, web, poller and github-watcher — keep the four in lockstep). `6.5.0` silently deleted `emailRouting.rules.list`, which `listAllEmailRoutingRules` needs; the REST endpoint and every sibling method (`create`/`update`/`delete`/`get`) still exist, so it's a codegen regression, not an API removal. Tracked upstream in [cloudflare-typescript#2790](https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-typescript/issues/2790) (still open, and still missing on the 7.x line). Don't widen the range back to `^6.5.0` until that lands — typecheck is the only thing that catches it.
- Account ID is lazy-resolved from the first zone's `account.id` field and cached for the session
- 41 resource types: `zone`, `dns-record` (child of zone), `worker`, `r2-bucket`, `kv-namespace`, `d1-database`, `queue`, `tunnel`, `ssl-certificate` (child of zone), `page-rule` (child of zone), `firewall-rule` (child of zone), `access-application`, `access-policy` (child of access-application), `load-balancer` (child of zone), `worker-route` (child of zone), `custom-hostname` (child of zone), `hyperdrive`, `email-routing-rule` (child of zone), `waiting-room` (child of zone), `spectrum-application` (child of zone), `logpush-job` (child of zone), `workers-ai-model`, `rate-limit-rule` (child of zone), `redirect-rule` (child of zone), `cache-rule` (child of zone), `ip-access-rule` (child of zone), `turnstile-widget` (account), `healthcheck` (child of zone), `notification-policy` (account), `vectorize-index` (account), `durable-object-namespace` (account, list-only), `ai-gateway`, `ai-search`, `workflow` (account; no create/edit, since Cloudflare's update endpoint is the deploy path and needs a step-limit setting the read endpoint never returns), `secrets-store-secret` (account; creates `default_secrets_store` when the account has none). Pages types were removed in 257ef387. Basin (GA 2026-10-01, the rename of Pipelines / R2 Data Catalog / R2 SQL with unchanged APIs) adds `basin-stream`, `basin-sink`, `basin-pipeline`, `basin-catalog`, `basin-table`, and Workers Analytics Engine adds `analytics-engine-dataset`; see the Basin note below.
- **updateResource / edit panels:** 17 types are editable (`supportsUpdate: true`): `dns-record`, `tunnel` (ingress only), and the batch wired through `updateResourceImpl` — `rate-limit-rule`/`redirect-rule`/`cache-rule` (reuse `editPhaseRule` + `RulePhaseSpec.buildBody` with an `enabled` toggle), `firewall-rule` (`editFirewallRule`), `ip-access-rule`, `waiting-room`, `load-balancer`, `hyperdrive` (name + caching only — origin needs the never-returned password), `custom-hostname` (SSL method only), `email-routing-rule` (name+enabled; matchers/actions preserved via a `get`), `spectrum-application`, `logpush-job`, `access-application`, `access-policy` (name/decision/precedence; include/exclude/require preserved via `get`), `page-rule` (status/priority; targets/actions preserved via `get`), `turnstile-widget`, `healthcheck`, `notification-policy`. **Key mechanism:** the host only sends changed keys, so `updateResourceImpl` calls `mergeCurrentFields` (fetch current resource, stringify fields, overlay the changed keys) before dispatching — every builder sees a complete field set, which matters for CF's full-replace PUTs and required-field PATCHes. Read-only/identity fields are marked `editable: false` on the resource type so they don't appear in the edit form.
- **Turnstile / Health Checks / Notifications** (`clients/turnstile-client.ts`, `healthcheck-client.ts`, `notification-policy-client.ts`): `turnstile-widget` (account, `turnstile.widgets.*`; externalId = sitekey; `siteKey` output + sensitive `secretKey` resolved on demand via `getWidgetSecret` → `widgets.get().secret`; `secretExportTemplates` for `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`/`TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`). `healthcheck` (child of zone, `healthchecks.*`; HTTP/HTTPS build an `http_config`; `edit` is PATCH). `notification-policy` (account, `alerting.policies.*`; create models the email-delivery `mechanisms` case, `summarizeMechanisms` flattens for display, edit is PATCH). `turnstile-widget` and `notification-policy`/`healthcheck`: `turnstile-widget` wires metrics via `fetchTurnstileMetricSeries` (`turnstileAdaptiveGroups`, filter `siteKey`, `count` by `datetimeFifteenMinutes`); healthcheck/notification-policy have no useful time-series dataset so they omit metrics.
- **Vectorize / Durable Objects** (`clients/vectorize-client.ts`, `durable-object-namespace-client.ts`): `vectorize-index` (account, `vectorize.indexes.*` v2; externalId = name; create takes `config:{dimensions,metric}`; `indexName` output + export template; no update — Vectorize indexes are immutable). `durable-object-namespace` (account, `durableObjects.namespaces.list` — **list-only**, declared by deploying a Worker class; `namespaceId` output; wires metrics via `fetchDurableObjectMetricSeries` → `durableObjectsInvocationsAdaptiveGroups`, filter `namespaceId`, sum `{requests, responseBodySize}`). Token scopes added: `vectorize` (edit); DO listing reuses the existing `workers_scripts` scope. Vectorize has no metrics wired — `vectorizeQueriesAdaptiveGroups` exists but its dimensions/metrics couldn't be verified (schema mirror truncates), so it was left off rather than ship an unverified query.
- **Rules engine** (`clients/rules-engine-client.ts`): a generic ruleset-phase client (`listAllPhaseRules`/`createPhaseRule`/`deletePhaseRule`) parameterized by `RulePhaseSpec`, shared by `rate-limit-rule` (phase `http_ratelimit`), `redirect-rule` (`http_request_dynamic_redirect`), and `cache-rule` (`http_request_cache_settings`). Each rule's externalId is `<zoneId>/<rulesetId>/<ruleId>`. `firewall-rule` (WAF custom rules, `http_request_firewall_custom`) predates this and has its own client. `ip-access-rule` uses `firewall.accessRules.*` (externalId `<zoneId>/<ruleId>`). All hang off the zone's "Rules & WAF" customTab; create forms start with a zone picker.
- **invokeAction** (zone header `plugin-action` ActionNodes, returns `Promise<void>`): "Purge Everything" → `cache.purge({purge_everything:true})`; "Enable/Disable DNSSEC" → `zone-client.setDnssec` → `dns.dnssec.edit({status})`.
- DNS records use shared `@infrawrench/plugin-base` DNS helpers (`dnsRecordBadgeColor`, `formatDnsTtl`, `renderDnsRecordDetail`, `renderDnsRecordSidebar`) — same helpers used by DigitalOcean and GCP
- Paginated fetch uses Cloudflare's `page` + `per_page` + `result_info.total_pages` pattern
- Resource ID formats: `{accountId}:zone:{zoneId}`, `{accountId}:dns-record:{zoneId}/{recordId}`, `{accountId}:r2-bucket:{bucketName}`, etc.
- Zone-scoped resources (DNS records, SSL certs, page rules, firewall rules, load balancers, worker routes, custom hostnames, email routing rules, waiting rooms) iterate all zones to list
- Account-scoped resources (Workers, R2, Pages, KV, D1, Queues, Tunnels, Access Apps, Hyperdrive) use the resolved `cfAccountId`
- Create supported for: zones, DNS records, R2 buckets, KV namespaces, D1 databases, queues, hyperdrive configs
- Delete supported for: zones, DNS records, R2 buckets, KV namespaces, D1 databases, queues, hyperdrive configs, workers
- R2 buckets declare `supportsStorageBrowser: true` — host renders the file browser via `listStorageObjects()`, `uploadStorageObject()`, `makeStorageFolder()`, `deleteStorageObject()`, `fetchStorageStats()`
- R2 storage browser uses `GET /accounts/{cfAccountId}/r2/buckets/{bucket}/objects?prefix=...&delimiter=/`; uploads via `PUT .../objects/{key}`
- D1 databases declare `resourceSqlDriver: { driver: "d1", connectionStringOutputKey: "databaseId" }` — REST-based SQL execution via `POST /accounts/{cfAccountId}/d1/database/{dbId}/query`
- D1 `executeQuery()` and `introspectResource()` implemented — introspection uses `sqlite_master` + `PRAGMA table_info` to populate SQL editor autocomplete with tables, columns, and primary keys
- Firewall rules are fetched from WAF custom rulesets (`phase: http_request_firewall_custom`) via the Rulesets API
- `CREATE_TOKEN_SCOPES` (in `plugin.ts`) builds the dash "create token" deep link; includes `cache_purge` (purge), `cache_settings` (edit), `transform_rules` (edit), `health_checks` (edit), `turnstile` (edit), and `notifications` (edit) alongside the originals
- The `detail-renderers.ts` barrel uses explicit named re-export blocks (NOT `export *`) — a new renderer must be added to the matching block or it won't surface (caused a "renderX is not a function" failure during the rules-engine work)
- Tunnels exclude soft-deleted entries (filters out records where `deleted_at` is set)
- Pages deployments are capped at 5 per project to avoid excessive API calls
- Tunnel tokens resolved via `GET /accounts/{cfAccountId}/cfd_tunnel/{tunnelId}/token`
- Access Policies are children of Access Applications — listed by iterating all apps and fetching per-app policies
- Hyperdrive configs include origin connection details (host, port, scheme, database, user) and caching state
- Email Routing Rules parse matchers and actions into human-readable strings
- Workers AND zones both declare `settingsEditor` — a settings _form_ (the generic `SettingsEditorView`), not a raw JSON editor. `getManifest()` returns `{ settings: SettingDescriptor[] }`; the form's Apply sends a JSON array of changed `{id,value}` to `applyManifest`.
- Zone settings (`clients/zone-settings-meta.ts`): descriptors built by `buildZoneSettingDescriptors` (curated label/control/options map + inference fallback) from `GET /zones/{zoneId}/settings`; `applyManifest` coerces per setting via `coerceZoneSettingValue` and PATCHes each.
- Worker settings (`clients/worker-settings-meta.ts`): `getWorkerManifest` gathers from three endpoints — `scriptAndVersionSettings.get` (rich read: usage model, compatibility date/flags, placement, limits, bindings count, tail consumers — surfaced read-only), `subdomain.get` (workers.dev toggle), `schedules.get` (cron) — and `buildWorkerSettingDescriptors` returns the rows. `applyWorkerManifest` routes changes back: editable script fields (logpush, observability enabled+head_sampling_rate, tags) via `settings.edit`; the workers.dev toggle via `subdomain.create`; cron via `schedules.update`. The deploy-time fields are read-only because the simple settings PATCH can't set them.
- **Settings editor capability (generic):** `settingsEditor?: SettingsEditorCapability` on `DetailViewSchema` renders `SettingsEditorView` (toggles/selects/numbers/text + dirty tracking) backed by the existing `getManifest`/`applyManifest` transport — `getManifest` returns `{settings: SettingDescriptor[]}`, Apply posts changed `[{id,value}]`. Reuses the manifest host wiring (web + desktop, cloud + local); the manifest/settings tab gate now also checks `settingsEditor`.
- **Error formatting:** `clients/shared.ts` exports `formatCloudflareError` (pulls `errors[].message` → e.g. "Zone not entitled to this functionality (code 1034)", parsing both the SDK error object and a JSON body embedded in the message) and `withCloudflareErrors(fn)` which rethrows the clean message (original kept as `cause`). `withAuthErrorHint` reuses it on its non-auth path. `createResource`/`updateResource`/`deleteResource`/`publishMessage` are wrapped so create/edit/delete modals show the readable message instead of a raw `403 {…}` blob; auth (401/403/code 10000/9109) still maps to the friendly scope hint.
- R2 buckets declare `secretExportTemplates` with S3 endpoint + bucket name for K8s secret export
- Tunnels declare `secretExportTemplates` with tunnel token + ID for K8s secret export
- Spectrum Applications show protocol badges and origin connection details
- Logpush Jobs show dataset, destination type (parsed from URL scheme), enable/error status, and last error in mono text

On an Entra ID-integrated cluster that kubeconfig's user is a kubelogin `exec` or legacy `azure` `auth-provider`, which the cloud's kubeconfig policy refuses and which on the desktop would log in as the human, not the account; `withStaticAksToken` (`output-resolver.ts`) rebuilds it around a token minted for the service principal with scope `6dae42f8-4368-4678-94ff-3960e28e3630/.default` (the AKS AAD server app). The SP needs a Kubernetes RBAC role on the cluster.

- Redis Cache keys resolved via `listKeys` ARM API; connection string built as `host:6380,password=...,ssl=True`
- Service Bus connection strings resolved via `listKeys` on the `RootManageSharedAccessKey` authorization rule
- Storage Account keys resolved via `listKeys` ARM API
- Event Hub connection strings resolved via `listKeys` on `RootManageSharedAccessKey` authorization rule
- PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server connection strings built from FQDN + admin login
- Log Analytics shared keys resolved via `sharedKeys` ARM API
- Secret export templates on: SQL Database, Cosmos DB, Storage Account, Redis Cache, Service Bus, Event Hub, PostgreSQL Flexible, MySQL Flexible, Log Analytics
- Provisioning state mapping: Succeeded→healthy, Creating/Updating/Upgrading→provisioning, Stopped/Paused/Deallocated→degraded, Failed/Deleting→error

- VM create auto-provisions VNet, Subnet, Public IP, NSG (with SSH/RDP rule), and NIC before creating the VM
- VM listing resolves public/private IPs by following NIC → IP Configuration → Public IP references
- Create supported for 22 of 26 types: Resource Groups, VMs, Disks, VNets, AKS Clusters, SQL Databases (with auto SQL Server provisioning), Cosmos DB, Storage Accounts, Function Apps, App Services, Container Instances, Key Vaults, Redis Caches, Service Bus, Container Registries, DNS Zones, NSGs, Public IPs, PostgreSQL Flexible, MySQL Flexible, Event Hub, Log Analytics, Managed Identities
- `getCreateCostEstimate` for VM, AKS, Container Instance, Redis Cache, App Service, Function App, SQL Database, Disk — pulls rates from the public Azure Retail Prices API (`prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices`, no auth). Rates are fetched per region in `src/pricing.ts`, cached 6h in `pricingRateCache` with in-flight dedup, and cover VM hourly, managed-disk $/GB/mo (sampled from representative tiers), Redis per-capacity, App Service + Function App per-SKU, SQL DB per-SKU, and Container Instance per-vCPU-second + per-GB-second rates. `getCreateSizePricing` hydrates VM/AKS/Flexible-DB size pickers asynchronously after region selection.

Amazon Linux / Ubuntu / Debian go through SSM Public Parameters (`AmazonSSM.GetParameter`); RHEL / SUSE go through `DescribeImages` with vendor owner IDs (`309956199498`, `013907871322`). Architecture is derived from the instance type — Graviton families ending in `g[a-z]*` and `a1.*` map to `arm64`, everything else to `x86_64`. SSH username comes from a per-family table at create time; the legacy AMI→username map in `ssh-username.ts` remains as a fallback for synced/listed instances.
- `estimateCost` handles `ec2-instance` (instance + gp3 root volume), `ebs-volume` (sizeGb × the selected volume type's rate), `rds-instance` (instance class + gp2 allocated storage; Aurora prices instance hours only — its volume is consumption-billed) and `eks-cluster` (nodes × instance + node volumes; control plane deliberately unpriced, so the estimate is `partial`). Every rate is live and per-region through `pricing.ts` (`pricing:GetProducts`), not a table — see the cost-estimate section below

### ClickHouse (`@infrawrench/plugin-clickhouse`)

- Two API surfaces: ClickHouse **Cloud API** (service management) + **HTTP Interface** (SQL queries)
- Cloud API auth: HTTP Basic Auth (`apiKeyId:apiKeySecret`) against `https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1`
- Credentials: `apiKeyId`, `apiKeySecret` (sensitive), `organizationId`, `chHost` (SQL endpoint), `chUser`, `chPassword` (sensitive)

  - `GET /v1/organizations/{orgId}/services` — list services
  - `POST /v1/organizations/{orgId}/services` — create service (name, provider, region, replicas, memory scaling)
  - `DELETE /v1/organizations/{orgId}/services/{serviceId}` — delete service
  - `PATCH /v1/organizations/{orgId}/services/{serviceId}/state` — start/stop service

- Delete stops the service first if running/idle (Cloud API requires stopped state), then deletes

- Secret export templates: HTTP Connection URL, Host + Port
- Resource ID format: `{accountId}:ch-service:{serviceId}` or `{accountId}:ch-database:{serviceId}/{dbName}`
- Rate limit: 10 requests per 10 seconds per API key; max 100 API keys per org

### New Relic (`@infrawrench/plugin-newrelic`)

Verified against New Relic's docs (NerdGraph introduction, "Query and alert on usage data") and the queries newrelic-client-go generates from the NerdGraph schema (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One GraphQL endpoint per region** (`api.newrelic.com`, `api.eu.newrelic.com`, `api.jp.newrelic.com`), `API-Key: NRAK-…` (a User key, carrying its user's permissions; there are no scoped keys, so there is no preflight template). NerdGraph answers most failures as HTTP 200 with `errors[]`; `api.ts` maps `FORBIDDEN`/`UNAUTHORIZED`/`ACCESS_DENIED` to status 403 so listers and the cost collector can branch on it. NRQL always travels as a `Nrql!` variable, never spliced into the GraphQL document; values spliced into NRQL go through `nrqlString`.
- **There is no billing or invoice API, and no rate data.** The `estimatedCost` attribute on the usage events was deprecated in May 2022 and NerdGraph exposes no contract rates (`customerAdministration.contracts` carries only ids and billing structure). Cost is usage (`NrConsumption` hourly, `NrMTDConsumption` month-to-date) times rates that are **credential fields** defaulting to list prices, so the user edits them with Edit credentials; the manifest declares `estimated`. CCU prices are unpublished, so compute rows are only written once a rate is entered.
- **Usage lives in the parent account.** A parent records the usage of every child, so cost reads one "usage account" (a `providerOptions` picker filled from the key) rather than every account: querying each would double count. Listing, by contrast, covers every account the key can see (entities through cross-account `entitySearch`; policies and NRQL conditions per account, first 100 accounts, 403 in one account lists it empty).
- **Monthly charges become daily rows by differencing month-to-date billable amounts**: ingest above the free allowance (`freeGbPerMonth`, allocated across that day's account/source cells pro rata), users at the month's billable count (`FullPlatformUsersBillable`, else the original-model `FullUsersBillable`; `CoreUsersBillable`), synthetic `billableConsumption`. A month's rows therefore sum to exactly the month's bill at the configured rates, and each month is always read from its 1st even when the requested range starts mid-month (`restatementDays: 35` re-reads the whole current month every pass).
- **Updates are typed per subtype.** NerdGraph has no type-agnostic update for monitors (`syntheticsUpdate{Simple,SimpleBrowser,ScriptApi,ScriptBrowser,Step,BrokenLinks,CertCheck}Monitor`) or NRQL conditions (`alertsNrqlCondition{Static,Baseline,Outlier}Update`); the client reads the current type first and picks the mutation. Policies and conditions are addressed `<accountId>:<id>` because every alerts mutation takes the account.
- **Entity outline fields are not the entity fields.** `entitySearch` returns `*EntityOutline` types; the fragments in `mappers.ts` use those names, which is why a single-entity read goes through `entitySearch(query: "id = '<guid>'")` rather than `actor.entity(guid:)` (whose types are the non-outline `*Entity`). APM `errorRate` and synthetics `successRate` are already percentages; response times are seconds.

### Grafana Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-grafana-cloud`)

Verified against Grafana's published Cloud API OpenAPI document (`grafana/grafana-com-public-clients`, `openapi.json`, 2026-10; its `servers` url is `/api`, so every path below is under `https://grafana.com/api`), the Synthetic Monitoring OpenAPI (`/api/v1/openapi`, v1.18.0) and the Grafana HTTP API reference. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **No "who am I".** Every org route wants the org slug or id in the path. The token (`glc_` + base64 JSON) carries the org id as `o` and its region as `m.r`; `decodeCloudToken` reads them and `GET /orgs/{id}` yields the slug. The format is undocumented (community forum), so the optional `orgSlug` credential is the fallback and every caller treats a non-decoding token as "ask", never as an error.
- **Billed usage is real money and monthly** (`GET /orgs/{org}/billed-usage?month&year`, `orgs:read` or `org-billing-info:read`). One item per dimension with `amountDue` and `usages[]` per stack; per-stack money is `attributedCost` when present, else a usage-proportional split, rounded so the stacks sum to `amountDue` exactly. Rows are `periodNative` and dated to the 1st (see `cost/period-scope.ts`); only months whose 1st lies in the range are written, and `restatementDays: 62` always reaches back to the previous month's 1st. Not `estimated`. The platform fee, tax and credits are not in it (credits appear per stack but whether `amountDue` is already net is undocumented, so they are not emitted). The FOCUS CSV export (`/orgs/{org}/focus`, `org-billing-focus:read`, trailing 60 days) and `invoices:read` (no endpoint exists) were deliberately not used.
- **Access policies and tokens are regional and rate-limited** (600 req/h). The list routes require `region`; the plugin fans out over the token's own region plus every stack's `regionSlug` and dedupes by id (`us` and `prod-us-east-0` can alias). External ids are `region/id` because every write needs the region back. Policy updates send the whole policy (scopes, realms, conditions read back first) so a rename or a status flip never drops scopes. Stacks and the org are cached in-process per token (`account.ts`) because every stack-scoped lister reads them.
- **Mutating Cloud API routes require `x-request-id`** (`requestId()`).
- **Stack-level objects need a second credential, stored per stack, not per account.** A stack's dashboards, alert rules, contact points and data sources come from its own Grafana (`glsa_` service account token), synthetic checks from the region's Synthetic Monitoring API (`regionSyntheticMonitoringApiUrl` on the stack, a tenant access token, not a `glc_`). Both are `password` fields on the stack type: `updateResource` writes them with `services.secrets.setPlaintext(stackResourceId, …)` and listers read them back, so picking the stack _is_ the picker. **Connect stack** mints one instead through the Cloud API's stack proxy (`/instances/{id}/api/serviceaccounts[...]/tokens`, `stack-service-accounts:write`), reusing an existing `infrawrench` service account. Stacks without a token are skipped; a stored token that 401/403/404s lists that stack empty rather than failing the type. `register/install` (which would mint an SM token from a `glc_`) was not used: it needs `metrics:write`/`logs:write`/`traces:write` and its rotation semantics are undocumented.
- **Stack usage metrics** are the `grafanacloud_*` series behind every stack's `grafanacloud-usage` data source, filtered by the instance `id` label (`hmInstancePromId`, `hlInstanceId`, `htInstanceId`). Connected stacks query through the data source proxy; otherwise `https://billing.grafana.net/api/prom` with basic auth `<orgId>:<glc token>` (`billing-metrics:read`; this path is inferred from the data source config and third-party docs, not documented by Grafana).
- **Synthetic Monitoring paths moved**: the spec has `/api/v1/check` and `/check/{id}`; the official Go client still calls `/check/list`, `/check/update`, `/check/delete/{id}`. The client tries the spec path and falls back on 404/405.
- **Alert rule pause** is GET + PUT of the whole rule with `X-Disable-Provenance: true`, which keeps the rule editable in Grafana's UI.
- **Status feed**: status.grafana.com components embed the region slug (`AWS Australia - prod-ap-southeast-2: Querying`), which is exactly the stack's `region` field.

### Elastic Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-elastic-cloud`)

Verified against Elastic's published OpenAPI documents (2026-10): `https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/cloud.json` (Cloud API), `.../elastic-cloud-serverless.json` and `.../cloud-billing.json`, plus Elastic's own billing integration (`packages/ess_billing` in elastic/integrations) for how the v2 cost endpoint is meant to be called. Not to be confused with the `opensearch` protocol plugin, which talks to a cluster; this one manages the cloud around it. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Two hosts, one key.** `api.elastic-cloud.com` serves the Cloud and Serverless APIs and the legacy v1 `/billing/costs/{org}` overview; `billing.elastic-cloud.com` serves the v2 Billing API (costs, charts) and budgets. Both take `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`, and both are on the bastion allowlist. The organization is discovered from `GET /api/v1/organizations`, so there is no organization credential field and no picker; every org-scoped call iterates what the key sees (normally one).
- **v1 deployment cost endpoints are deprecated.** Cost goes through v2 `GET /api/v2/billing/organizations/{org}/costs/instances`, which covers hosted deployments, serverless projects and org-level services alike, but returns a window aggregate with no daily buckets: one request per complete UTC day (the integration does the same), at most 4 in flight. `total_ecu` is a float despite the spec's `integer`. 1 ECU = $1.00 nominal, so rows are USD. Region is parsed out of capacity SKUs (`..._gcp-europe-west1_8192_1`); other line items carry none.
- **The v1 overview is still read** for the hourly rate and the prepaid `balance` (no v2 equivalent).
- **Resizing goes through `PATCH .../elasticsearch/{ref}/tiers`**, not a full-plan `PUT /deployments/{id}`; the GET returns `available_sizes`, which `updateResource` validates against so a bad size fails with the allowed list instead of an opaque 400. Rename is a `PUT` with only `name` and `prune_orphans: false`; `true` would shut every resource the body omits down.
- **Projects are typed everywhere** (`/serverless/projects/{elasticsearch|observability|security|vectordb}/{id}`), so the external id is `{type}/{id}`. The admin password only exists in the create and `_reset-credentials` responses; both store it through `services.secrets.setPlaintext` and the sensitive `password` output reads it back.
- **Traffic-filter associations are actions, not fields**: the edit form has no multi-select, so the deployment page lists region rulesets with Apply/Remove row actions (`attach-filter:<id>` / `detach-filter:<id>`), and the ruleset page removes deployments (`detach-deployment:<id>`). Only IP filters are created here; private-connectivity rules need endpoint ids from the user's cloud.
- **Deleting a deployment is `_shutdown`** (Elastic has no hard delete); deleting a ruleset passes `ignore_associations=true`.
- **A 403/404 on one lister lists that type empty** (Billing admin keys cannot list deployments, deployment-scoped keys cannot read budgets); 401 still throws. Snapshot repositories were left out: `/platform/configuration/snapshots/repositories` is ECE-only and not in the hosted API.

### Sentry (`@infrawrench/plugin-sentry`)

Verified against Sentry's API reference and the OpenAPI document it is generated from (getsentry/sentry-api-schema), plus the endpoint sources in getsentry/sentry where the docs are silent (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Hosts are per region.** Org-scoped calls go to `us.sentry.io` or `de.sentry.io`; `GET /api/0/organizations/` is a region-silo endpoint that only lists organizations in the region it is called on, so the organization picker (`providerOptions`, filled from the token) lists the chosen region's orgs rather than merging both. A self-hosted install is the same `/api/0/...` paths on the user's base URL (`baseUrl`, normalised to drop `/api/0`); bastion egress only allows the sentry.io hosts.
- **Token types.** Internal integration (`sntryi_`) and personal (`sntryu_`) tokens carry scopes; organization tokens (`sntrys_`) are fixed to `org:ci` and can read nothing the plugin lists, so `assertUsableToken` refuses them up front. Preflight probes one read per capability and its template is the scope list (`alerts:*` is a real scope even though the permissions page lists only the older groups).
- **Pagination is the `Link` header** (`rel="next"; results="true|false"`, both cursors always present), and the issues endpoint reports the total in `X-Hits`. Neither survives `jsonRestFetch`, so `api.ts` calls `services.http.request` itself and keeps the headers; it still prefers the host HTTP service for bastions and custom CAs.
- **The legacy alert-rule APIs are gone.** Sentry split alerting into Monitors (detectors, `/organizations/{org}/detectors/`) and Alerts (workflows, `/organizations/{org}/workflows/`) in May 2026; `projects/{org}/{project}/rules/` and `organizations/{org}/alert-rules/` are absent from the spec and the URL conf. Enable/disable uses the bulk `PUT ?id=` form with `{enabled}`. A workflow `PUT` requires `name` and takes the whole alert, so renaming re-sends the fetched alert with only the edited values replaced (not verified against a live org). Detector updates require `type` and are type-specific, so monitors are enable/disable/delete only. Uptime (`uptime_domain_failure`) and cron (`monitor_check_in_failure`) detectors are filtered out of the generic monitor list because they are their own resource types. Uptime endpoints are marked experimental in the source.
- **Cron environment statuses** are `active|ok|error|disabled`; missed and timed-out runs are check-in statuses that put the environment into `error`. Pausing a monitor is `PUT {status: "disabled"}` (paused monitors are not billed), muting `PUT {isMuted}`.
- **There is no billing API and no prices.** Subscription, on-demand budget and invoice data live in the closed-source billing layer behind undocumented endpoints. Cost is `stats_v2` accepted quantity times **credential-field rates** defaulting to the Team plan's pay-as-you-go list prices, with per-category included volumes; the manifest declares `estimated`. Quantity is bytes for attachments and `log_byte` (priced per decimal GB) and milliseconds for profiling; `error` rolls up `default` and `security`. Monthly allowances are applied by month-to-date differencing, so each month's daily series is read from its 1st (clamped to `stats_v2`'s 90-day reach, hence `maxHistoryDays: 90`).
- **`groupBy=project` returns totals, never a series**, so the project breakdown is one `stats_v2` call per day in range (concurrency 4), and each day's billable volume is split across projects pro rata. Cron and uptime monitors are priced from current inventory for the current month only, dated to the 1st; the plan fee is a row on each month's 1st. A self-hosted account throws `CostSetupError` (there is no bill).

### Coralogix (`@infrawrench/plugin-coralogix`)

Verified against Coralogix's published OpenAPI documents (`https://api.eu2.coralogix.com/mgmt/openapi/{4,5}/openapi.yaml`), the `com.coralogix.datausage.v2` protos in `coralogix/coralogix-management-sdk`, and the docs' `.md` twins (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One key, one region, one team.** Auth is `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (a Team or Personal key; Send-Your-Data keys only ingest). Keys only work in their own region, picked by the sign-in address (`<team>.coralogix.com` is EU1, `<team>.app.coralogix.us` is US1, `<team>.app.cx498.coralogix.com` is US2). `regions.ts` is the one list (EU1, EU2, US1, US2, US3, AP1, AP2, AP3, GOV1) and feeds the bastion allowlist; it uses the `api.<region>.coralogix.com` hosts from the endpoints page, not the older `api.coralogix.us`-style hosts the OpenAPI `servers` list still names (both answer). `resolveRegion` also takes legacy domains and a pasted team URL. Every endpoint is implicitly scoped to the key's team, so `team` is the plugin's **account root**.
- **Usage is units, never money.** The per-day breakdown comes from `POST /mgmt/openapi/4/dataplans/data-usage/v2/daily/units` and `.../daily/processed-gbs` (documented only up to API version 4, still served): one row per day with a fixed field per pillar and priority. `totalUnits` is authoritative: the fine fields are emitted as cells and the remainder against the total becomes one blocked (or `other`) cell, because the docs do not say whether `blockedUnits` includes `blockedMetricsUnits`. When the v4 route 404s the collector falls back to the v5 `POST /dataplan/data-usage/v1/query`, grouping by whichever pillar and priority labels `GET .../v1/capabilities` advertises.
- **Cost is `units × unit price`, `estimated: true`.** No API exposes the price; the account has a non-secret `unitPrice` credential defaulting to the published $1.50 per unit, editable later. Rows: service = pillar, region = Coralogix region id, tags `pillar` and `priority` (High/Medium/Low/Blocked by the TCO Optimizer's names: Frequent Search, Monitoring, Compliance, Blocked), `usageAmount` = units.
- **The team id is the `companyId`** other responses carry (E2M limits, parsing limits, policies); the management API has no "who am I". It is matched against the deprecated-but-served `GET /aaa/teams/v2` for name, daily quota and retention; when unreadable those stay blank rather than guessed. `fetchQuotas` reports the daily unit quota against today's units plus the E2M, parsing-rule and enrichment limits (all provider figures; `partial: true`).
- **Updates are whole-object replaces.** Alerts (`PUT /alerts/alerts/v3` with `{id, alertDefProperties}`), TCO policies (`PUT /dataplans/policies/v1`, only the documented update fields are copied; note create uses `disabled` but update uses `enabled`), parsing rule groups (rule ids are stripped from the body) and quota rules (the whole rule set is written back). Alert trigger history is keyed by `alertVersionId`, not the alert id.
- **A 403 on one lister lists that type empty** (a key without that preset); 401 still throws. No Terraform export: the `coralogix/coralogix` provider's alert and policy blocks are deep unions that stored fields cannot reproduce faithfully.

### Fastly (`@infrawrench/plugin-fastly`)

Verified against Fastly's published OpenAPI clients (`fastly/fastly-js`, `src/api/*.js` and `docs/*.md`, 2026-10), which carry every path, query parameter and model field used here. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One token, two gates.** `Fastly-Key` carries an API token whose scope (`global`, `global:read`, `purge_select`, `purge_all`) is intersected with its owner's role (user, billing, engineer, superuser). Billing needs Billing or Superuser, configuration needs Engineer or Superuser, so "manage + costs" needs a Superuser. `preflight.ts` reads both (`/tokens/self`, `/current_user`) and settles costs with one `GET /billing/v3/invoices?limit=1`.
- **Cost is period-native and stitched from two endpoints.** Closed months come from posted invoices (`/billing/v3/invoices`, cursor paged, filtered by `billing_start_date`/`billing_end_date` as `YYYY-MM-DD`), the current month from `/billing/v3/invoices/month-to-date`; every row is dated to the 1st, `restatementDays: 62` (the Mistral rule). A closed month whose invoice has not posted yet returns **nothing**, so the month-to-date rows written while it was current survive until the invoice replaces them under the same keys. The month-to-date invoice has no `currency_code`; the latest posted invoice's is used, USD when there is none.
- **Per-service cost is not attributed.** Invoice lines carry product, product line/group and region but no service, and `/billing/v3/service-usage-metrics` answers one `(product_id, usage_type_name)` pair per request in units, not money; joining it to invoice lines would mean guessing which line a usage type bills under. Per-service numbers are traffic from the Historical Stats API instead (Metrics tab, 24-hour totals and a live panel from `rt.fastly.com`). This month's billable usage by product (`/billing/v3/usage-metrics`) is a table on the account root.
- **Classic config endpoints take form bodies**, not JSON (`/service`, versions, dictionary and config-store items); `fastlyRaw` has `form`, `json` and `raw` (KV values are `application/octet-stream`). Purge by URL is `POST /purge/{host+path}` with the scheme stripped and `Fastly-Soft-Purge: 1` for a soft purge; several surrogate keys go to `POST /service/{id}/purge` as `{surrogate_keys}` (256 per request).
- **Service children come from the live version**: the active version, else the newest. One `GET /service/{id}/details` per service feeds services, versions, domains and backends, memoised for 60 s on the client so one sync pass does not refetch it per type. Logging endpoints have no single list call, so they fan out over all 28 `/logging/{type}` collections per service (6,000 reads/minute is Fastly's published read limit).
- **Dictionaries, config stores and KV stores use the generic key browser** (`kvBrowser`), so items are editable in place; write-only dictionaries can be written but not read. Secret stores list names only (Fastly never returns values).
- **Status feed is StatusCast RSS** (`www.fastlystatus.com/rss/`), not Statuspage: items are posts, the guid's first segment is the incident, and an incident is active when its newest post does not read as finished. Retrospectives and announcements are skipped; POP incidents become a display-only `POP XXX` service.
- **A 403 on one lister lists that type empty** (a `global:read` token limited to some services, or a role without access); 401 still throws.

### MongoDB Atlas (`@infrawrench/plugin-mongodb-atlas`)

Verified against the Atlas Administration API v2 OpenAPI document (github.com/mongodb/openapi, `openapi/v2.json`) and MongoDB's docs (service account token, FOCUS report API), 2026-10. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Distinct from `mongodb`.** `mongodb` is a connection-string protocol plugin (one database, a data browser); `mongodb-atlas` is the Atlas control plane for an organization. A cluster opens its data in `mongodb` through a `peerIntegrations` entry (`connectionString` output -> `connectionString` credential) instead of shipping a second browser. Atlas never returns a database user's password, so `credentialSetupAction` ("Create connection user", the same shape as DigitalOcean's "Make connection user") creates a cluster-scoped user with a generated password and stores user + password through `services.secrets.setPlaintext` against the cluster's resource id; `resolveOutput("connectionString")` injects them into `standardSrv`.
- **One credential field pair, two auth schemes.** A client id starting `mdb_sa_id_` is a service account (OAuth client credentials at `POST /api/oauth/token`, Basic auth, one-hour bearer); anything else is a programmatic API key (HTTP Digest, MD5, `qop=auth`). Token minting is limited to 10 a minute, so tokens are cached module-wide per credential, not per client; the digest challenge is cached and reused with an incrementing `nc`, retrying once on a fresh 401 challenge. `md5.ts` exists because WebCrypto has no MD5 and the plugin also runs in the desktop renderer. The org is a `providerOptions` picker (`GET /orgs`), using the credential-options mechanism copied from the New Relic branch.
- **Every endpoint is versioned by media type** (`Accept: application/vnd.atlas.<date>+json`, wrong version = 406): clusters `2024-08-05` (the `replicationSpecs[].regionConfigs[]` shape), flex `2024-11-13`, search indexes `2024-05-30`, alert acknowledge `2024-05-30`, everything else `2023-01-01`. `/clusters` also returns Flex/serverless entries (`providerName` `FLEX`/`SERVERLESS`); those are skipped there and listed under their own types.
- **Tier and storage live on every region config.** Scaling reads the cluster, rewrites `instanceSize` on every electable and read-only spec (`diskSizeGB` on all three), strips `effective*` and ids, and PATCHes `replicationSpecs` whole. Enabling compute auto-scaling with no bounds sets min = current tier, max = two tiers up the same class. The Scale tier picker comes from `GET /groups/{id}/clusters/provider/regions` filtered to the cluster's region (stashed in `resolvedOutputs` by `getResource`), with the spec's per-cloud enums as the fallback.
- **Cost is billed, from invoice line items** (pending + closed invoices; `GET …/invoices/{id}` for the items). `totalPriceCents` is documented as `unitPriceDollars × quantity × 100`, so rows subtract `discountCents`. The Cost Explorer API was rejected (async token polling, month granularity) and so was the FOCUS report (daily, but a presigned download on another host that bastion egress cannot route). SKU -> service uses the Cost Explorer `services` names, read from words in the SKU (there is no SKU catalogue in the spec); unknowns are "Atlas". `resourceId` is `{groupId}/{clusterName}`, the cluster's external id. No `credits` capability: Atlas exposes credits applied per invoice and credit line items, not a remaining balance.
- **Rightsizing prices come from the org's own invoices.** Atlas has no price API, so `getCreateSizePricing` returns per-node `unitPriceDollars × 730` for instance SKUs billed in the last ~40 days, keyed by region via the cluster inventory (line items carry no region). Tiers never billed have no price and are never recommended; `resizeNote` says so. The size catalogue (`getCreateConfig("cluster")`, no `supportsCreate`) uses AWS's published vCPU/RAM per tier. CPU/memory series labels in `metrics.ts` are load-bearing for the declaration.
- **Process -> cluster matching** for metrics: a process belongs to a cluster when its `userAlias` (or hostname) starts with the SRV host's first label plus `-` and ends with the same project subdomain. Measurements request a full metric set and fall back to a core set on HTTP 400.

### Confluent Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-confluent-cloud`)

Verified against Confluent's published spec (https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/openapi.yaml), the Metrics API reference and its public descriptors (`api.telemetry.confluent.cloud/v2/metrics/cloud/descriptors/metrics`), and the billing docs (2026-10). Distinct from the `kafka` protocol plugin: this one manages the Confluent organization. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One Cloud API key (HTTP Basic) for everything**, management, billing and telemetry; cluster-scoped keys get 401 there. It acts with its owner's RBAC roles: Operator lists, BillingAdmin reads cost, MetricsViewer reads metrics, AccountAdmin manages service accounts, EnvironmentAdmin resizes and pauses. The preflight template is the Confluent CLI role-binding commands.
- **Most lists are environment-scoped** (`?environment=` is required on cmk, fcpm, ksqldbcm, srcm, networking), so the client lists environments first (60s cache) and fans out; a 403 on one environment lists it empty. Resource ids carry the route (`env/lkc`, `env/lkc/connectorName`, `env/slug/id` for network connections) while `externalId` stays the bare provider id (`lkc-…`, `lcc-…`), because that is the id the Costs API reports, which is what the orphan finder's cost annotation joins on. The host never derives an external id from a resource id, which is what makes the split safe.
- **Topics cannot be listed with a Cloud key** (Kafka REST wants a cluster key), so topic and partition counts come from the Metrics API: distinct `metric.topic` labels on `retained_bytes` over the last hour, grouped across every cluster in one query. The listing makes five grouped `granularity: ALL` queries total, not per cluster. Usage fields are **absent, never zero, when the Metrics API refused**, which keeps the `idle` orphan rules quiet for keys without MetricsViewer; a successful query with no row for a cluster does mean zero (no traffic produces no rows).
- **Metrics API limits**: one aggregation per request, seven days of retention (ranges are clamped), granularity bounded by interval length (PT1M to 6h, PT5M to 1d, PT15M to 4d, PT30M to 7d). Counters are 60-second deltas, so a SUM per bucket is divided by the bucket length to chart a rate.
- **The Kafka tab is the kafka plugin**, via a peer integration on `connectionString`. Confluent shows a cluster key's secret once, so `create-kafka-api-key` (header action and the peer pane's credential-setup action) mints one, stores key and secret with `services.secrets.setPlaintext` against the cluster resource id, and `resolveOutput` builds `kafka://host:9092?sasl=plain&ssl=true&user=…&password=…` (query params so a secret's `+`/`/` survive). With no owner picked the key belongs to the owner of the account's own Cloud key, read from `GET /iam/v2/api-keys/{ownKeyId}`; a picked service account can be granted CloudClusterAdmin on the cluster CRN (`metadata.resource_name`), a 409 meaning it already had it.
- **Costs**: `start_date` inclusive, `end_date` exclusive, at most one month per request and one year back, so ranges are walked in 28-day windows; 72h latency, `restatementDays: 5`. The Costs API carries no region, so region is joined from inventory (clusters, pools, registries, ksqlDB via its Kafka cluster, connectors via theirs). Organizations created before 2024-05-15 get a legacy shape with the environment at the top level and, per the community forum, sometimes no `amount`; `netAmount` falls back to original minus discount, then quantity times price. `PROMO_CREDIT` rows are `credit`, `SUPPORT` rows `support`. **Unverified**: whether promo credits also show up inside per-line `discount_amount` (which would double-count against the separate credit rows); check against a real invoice. There is no credit-balance or commitment API, so no `credits` capability.
- **CKU right-sizing reuses the VM contract**: the catalog is a size-picker of 1..24 CKUs with `vcpus = CKUs` (memory scaled alongside, so the unmeasured-memory floor caps a single step at halving), `cpuMetric` is `CKU utilization` (`cluster_load_percent` x100), and `regionFieldKey` is `placement` (`AWS/us-east-1/MULTI_ZONE`) because CKU price depends on cloud, region and availability. Prices come from the org's own billed CKU-hours over the last month (`amount / quantity` of `KAFKA_NUM_CKUS` lines, 6h cache), and a multi-zone placement prices nothing for 1 CKU, which keeps that illegal size out of recommendations. A side effect: the implicit carbon declaration reads the type as `unsupported-provider`, which is the honest answer. Resizes go through `PATCH /cmk/v2/clusters/{id}` with `spec.environment` and `spec.config.kind` on every update.
- **Pausing a connector does not stop billing** (task hours keep accruing, per Confluent's billing dimensions page), which is why connectors declare no `lifecycle` for sleep schedules and the idle rule says so.
- **Status feed**: status.confluent.cloud has a single "Confluent Cloud" component, so `parseStatusFeed` lifts regions out of incident titles (`AWS us-east-1`, `GCP us-central1`, `Azure East US` squashed to `eastus`) and stays provider-wide for "All Regions" or no region.

### Snowflake (`@infrawrench/plugin-snowflake`)

Verified against docs.snowflake.com (SQL API reference and auth pages, the ACCOUNT_USAGE / ORGANIZATION_USAGE view references, ALTER WAREHOUSE, CREATE / ALTER RESOURCE MONITOR) and the SHOW row structs in the Snowflake Terraform provider's SDK (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One transport: the SQL API v2** (`POST https://<host>/api/v2/statements`, `api.ts`). No native driver anywhere, so the same client runs in the desktop renderer, the server and the poller. 202 is polled, 429 retried with the same `requestId` + `retry=true`, extra partitions fetched (gzip; the host HTTP service is asked for binary and the plugin gunzips with `DecompressionStream`). Every value arrives as a string and is decoded by `rowType` (DATE = days since epoch, TIMESTAMP_* = seconds with nine decimals); internal callers get lower-cased keys so SHOW output and SELECT aliases read the same. Every statement runs with session `TIMEZONE = UTC` and `QUERY_TAG = infrawrench`.
- **One credential field takes a PEM private key or a programmatic access token** (`auth.ts`), detected by the armour. That is what lets the role and warehouse `providerOptions` pickers depend on `["account", "user", "credential"]`: `dependsOn` requires every field, so two alternative secret fields would never satisfy it. Key-pair JWTs are signed with WebCrypto; the fingerprint needs the public key's SPKI, which WebCrypto cannot derive from a private key directly, so the private key is exported as JWK and `n`/`e` re-imported as a public key. PKCS#1 keys are wrapped into PKCS#8; encrypted keys are refused with the `openssl pkcs8 -nocrypt` command. JWT account = identifier without region, upper-case, underscores kept; host = hyphen form (`account.ts`).
- **Listing never touches a warehouse.** `listResources`, `fetchDashboardStats` and `resolveOutput` only issue SHOW commands (cloud services). Anything reading ACCOUNT_USAGE (metrics, recommendations, attribution, database storage) needs compute, and the poller refetches pinned resources' metrics every cycle, so those reads go through a module-level 30-minute cache (`client.ts`); without it a pinned warehouse would keep the metadata warehouse awake around the clock. `introspectResource` (called by the host on every detail open when `executeQuery` exists) uses `SHOW COLUMNS` and only for databases and schemas, for the same reason.
- **Cost has two sources decided per account** (`cost-data.ts`): billed `ORGANIZATION_USAGE.USAGE_IN_CURRENCY_DAILY` filtered to `ACCOUNT_LOCATOR = CURRENT_ACCOUNT()` (so several accounts of one org never double count), falling back on a not-authorized error (`002003`/`003001`) to `METERING_DAILY_HISTORY` credits × the credential's credit price plus `STORAGE_USAGE` × storage price (and transfer once a price is entered). The manifest's `estimated` is per plugin, so it is declared `true` and each row carries `costBasis`. Warehouse compute is split per warehouse pro rata to `WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY` compute credits that day. `restatementDays: 35` because org usage restates until month close.
- **Query attribution is a report, not cost rows**: `QUERY_ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY` (no role column, so roles join from `QUERY_HISTORY`) by tag / user / role / warehouse on the account page, the same stance as Datadog's attribution: the daily rows already account for every credit.
- **Capacity balance** (`credits`, from `REMAINING_BALANCE_DAILY`) and **resource monitors as quotas** (`quotas`, `credit_quota`/`used_credits` from SHOW RESOURCE MONITORS) are both Snowflake's own figures. Resource-monitor `TRIGGERS` replaces the whole set, so an edit rebuilds it from the current values plus the change.
- **Rightsizing does not use the generic "Oversized" finder**: that needs a CPU-utilisation series and a size catalog with prices, and Snowflake has neither. Warehouse recommendations (`recommendWarehouse` in `insights.ts`) come from settings plus `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_HISTORY`, rendered with one-click `resize:<SIZE>` / `auto-suspend:<s>` plugin actions; a running warehouse with auto-suspend off is an `orphanRule` so it lands in Potential savings.

### Redis Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-redis-cloud`)

Verified against the live OpenAPI document (`https://api.redislabs.com/v1/cloud-api-docs`, 2026-10) and the official Go client `RedisLabs/rediscloud-go-api`, whose models fill in the response shapes the spec leaves as bare objects with examples. Distinct from the `redis` connection-string plugin, which it reuses rather than duplicates. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Two keys.** `x-api-key` is the account key, `x-api-secret-key` a user key carrying one member's role. Cost reports need Owner, Viewer or Billing admin. 400 requests/minute per key.
- **Writes and several reads are tasks.** Every POST/PUT/DELETE returns a task polled at `GET /tasks/{id}`; `submitTask` waits ~20s and reports "still processing" rather than failing a resize or import that takes minutes, and throws the task's own `response.error.description` on `processing-error`. VPC peerings, Transit Gateways, PSC, the CIDR allow list and PSC scripts are _GETs that return tasks_ too (`readViaTask`); the data is the finished task's `response.resource`.
- **Pro and Essentials are separate API trees** (`/subscriptions` vs `/fixed/subscriptions`) with slightly different spellings (`security.enableDefaultUser` vs `defaultUserEnabled`, `sourceIp` vs `sourceIps` on update). One resource type covers both; the subscription external id carries the family (`pro-123` / `ess-456`), database ids are account-unique and resolved to their subscription through an index filled by listing.
- **Only the single-database GET returns the default user's password**, which is what `connectionString` is built from (`rediss://` when TLS is required). That output feeds the `redis` peer tab (console, key browser) via `credentialMappings`, with `unreachableWhen` on an empty public endpoint.
- **Metrics are three point-in-time sources**, because the REST API has no metric history: memory used vs dataset limit from the API; the Pro subscription's `prometheusEndpoint` (v1 `bdb_*` gauges at `https://<endpoint>:8070/`, internal network only, so it answers through a bastion in the peered VPC; `*.rlrcp.com` is on the bastion allowlist for this); and the `redis` plugin's new INFO-based `fetchMetricSeries`, merged in via `exposeMetricsToParent` (labelled "Redis · …"). The poller's sampling of pinned resources builds the trend.
- **Cost report lines are periods, not days.** A Pro database line covers its hours between configuration changes, an Essentials line a month. `focusRowsToCostRows` spreads `BilledCost` by UTC-day overlap and keeps only days in the requested window, so adjacent chunks never double count whether or not Redis clips the period to the request. Rows are aggregated by full key before return. `restatementDays: 5` covers the up-to-72h lag on Pro network lines.
- **Right-sizing is a detail-view hint, not a `rightsizing` declaration**: that contract is CPU-and-size-picker shaped. A Pro database under 25% of its dataset limit gets a suggested size (data ≤ 50% full, 0.1 GB steps) prefilled into Resize memory; resize refuses less than stored data + 10% (`minDatasetGb`). Empty paid databases (< 5 MB used, free Essentials excluded) carry `savingsFlag: empty`, which the declarative `orphanRule` reads.
- **Role assignments live in an undeclared `ruleSpec` field** (JSON of `{ruleName, databases: ["sub/db"]}`), read by the edit prompt's defaults and the Terraform mapping; Essentials subscriptions likewise store undeclared `planId`/`paymentMethodId`.
- **Status feed** is FireHydrant's RSS at `status.redis.io/data/rss.xml`: one item per incident _update_, grouped by incident link, state read from "Milestone is now '…'", items older than 14 days dropped.

### GitHub (`@infrawrench/plugin-github`)

Billing-focused: verified against GitHub's published REST description (`github/rest-api-description`, api.github.com and ghec, 1.1.4), the fine-grained token permission tables in `github/docs`, and GitHub's GraphQL schema (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Its own token, not the server's GitHub App** (`web/src/api/routes/github.ts`, used for git-triggered workflows and agent clones). The App requests repository contents/metadata; billing, budgets, seats and codespaces need organization Administration and Copilot permissions, so reusing it would force every org that installed it for workflows to re-approve a much broader grant, enterprise billing is unreachable from an org installation, and the installation token is minted server-side, so the desktop app and local mode could never use it. A plugin-held token keeps all of it inside the plugin.
- **One owner per account**, stored as `org:<login>` or `enterprise:<slug>` (a bare name is an org), picked through `providerOptions` from `GET /user/orgs` merged with GraphQL `viewer { organizations, enterprises }`. Fine-grained tokens are not documented for `/user/orgs` and cannot see enterprises, hence both sources and the typed fallback. The billing account is therefore the `accountRoot`. Runners, caches and codespaces are org-only in GitHub's API and list empty (without a request) on an enterprise account; cost centres are enterprise-only.
- **Fine-grained tokens cannot reach `/enterprises/*` at all**; enterprise accounts need a classic token (`manage_billing:enterprise`, plus `manage_billing:copilot`/`read:enterprise`, `manage_runners:enterprise`). Org billing routes are `/organizations/{org}/settings/billing/...` (long form), not `/orgs/`.
- **Data residency**: `host` accepts `github.com` or any spelling of a `*.ghe.com` subdomain and maps it to `api.<sub>.ghe.com`; anything else is refused (also via `validateServerCredentials`) so a token is never sent to an arbitrary host. The bastion allowlist is `api.github.com`, `*.ghe.com`, `*.githubusercontent.com`; the last is a guess for the Copilot metrics report download host (GitHub's examples use `example.com`), so on a bastion-routed account the Copilot active-user series may be missing until that is confirmed.
- **Cost is the usage report, not the summary.** `GET {billing}/usage?year&month` returns dated line items with gross/discount/net, product, SKU, org and repository. Gross becomes a `usage` row and the discount a negative `credit` row (`chargeTypes: true`), so totals equal net while included minutes stay visible. For an enterprise the report returns usage **outside any cost centre** by default and one cost centre's usage with `cost_center_id` (unlike `/usage/summary`, whose default covers all), so the collector calls default + every active cost centre and tags `costCenter`. The repository is the cost `resourceId`, matching the `actions-cache` externalId (`owner/repo`). A backfill month refused with 400/404/422 is skipped unless it is the newest month (pre-enhanced-billing history). Product and SKU strings arrive in either identifier or friendly form (GitHub's own examples show both), so everything goes through `normalizeId`.
- **Copilot moved from premium requests to AI credits in June 2026**: both `premium_request/usage` and `ai_credit/usage` are read, and the metrics derive both series from the usage report's unit type. Copilot active users come from the `organization-28-day/latest` metrics report, which returns signed NDJSON `download_links` (fetched without the token) whose records wrap `day_totals`; the old `/copilot/metrics` endpoint is gone from the description.
- **Seat removal is "pending cancellation"**, not immediate (`DELETE …/copilot/billing/selected_users`), and returns `seats_cancelled: 0` for a seat that comes from a team, which the client turns into an explanatory error. Seat price is read from the month's summary (`pricePerUnit` of `copilot_for_business`/`copilot_enterprise`), never a hardcoded list price. Idle = 30 days without activity (or never used and assigned 30+ days ago); stale codespace = 14 days unused.
- **Budgets**: `PATCH` only accepts amount, stop-usage, alerting and `expires_at`; product, type and scope are immutable (non-editable fields). `user`/`multi_user_customer` scopes only allow `ai_credits`/`premium_requests` and must stop usage. "Spent this month" is computed from the month's line items by product/SKU and scope; `consumed_amount` from the API is only used for user budgets.
- **Larger-runner cost is per SKU** (`hostedRunnerSku` maps platform + cores to `actions_<os>_<n>_core[_arm]`), so runners of the same shape share the figure. Self-hosted minutes are not billed by GitHub (the announced per-minute platform charge was postponed indefinitely).
- No Terraform export: the `integrations/github` provider has no resources for seats, budgets or cost centres, and runners/caches/codespaces are not configuration.

### CircleCI (`@infrawrench/plugin-circleci`)

Verified against the v2 OpenAPI document (`circleci.com/api/v2/openapi.json`), the v3 spec (`circleci.com/fullopenapi.yaml`), the runner API reference and circleci-cli's `internal/apiclient/runner.go` (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Three APIs, two auth headers.** v2 (`circleci.com/api/v2`) and the runner API (`runner.circleci.com/api/v3`) take the personal token as `Circle-Token`; v3 (`circleci.com/api/v3`) only accepts `Authorization: Bearer`, wraps everything in `{data}` and pages with `page[cursor]`. `api.ts` picks the header from the base URL. Project API tokens do not work on v2 at all, and personal tokens carry no scopes, so there is no preflight template.
- **The organization picker stores the collaboration UUID** (`/me/collaborations` `id`, falling back to the slug when it is null), because the Usage API wants the UUID while Insights, pipelines and contexts want the slug; the client resolves the slug from the same list. `providerOptions` mechanism, see plugin-base above.
- **v2 cannot list projects.** v3 `GET /projects?filter[org_id]=` gives ids and names but no slug. For `gh/`/`bb/` organizations the slug is the org slug plus the name; for GitHub App and standalone organizations (`circleci/<id>`) it is opaque, so it is learned from `GET /pipeline?org-slug=` and matched by name through `GET /project/{slug}`, falling back to `<org slug>/<project id>`. Without v3, Insights' `all_projects` names stand in.
- **Cost is the Usage API, asynchronous**: POST an export job (≤ 31 days, ≤ 1 year back), poll, then download one or more presigned gzip CSVs (magic-byte checked, `DecompressionStream`, so it runs in both the renderer and Node) with UPPERCASE headers. Both endpoints are limited to about 10 calls an hour per organization (sources disagree: 10/hour vs 10/minute for GET), and the cost collector re-runs every month chunk when a backfill fails, so `maxHistoryDays: 180` keeps the first pass at seven exports; anything longer would 429 at the same chunk forever. Polls back off from 5 s to 4 min within a 20-minute budget, inside the poller's 30-minute lease.
- **Credits, never money.** Rows are credits per day × kind (compute, DLC, storage, network, IP ranges, leases, users, plus `Other` for a total no known column explains) × project, resource class and executor tags, priced at the editable `pricePerCredit` credential ($0.0006 published). `includedCreditsPerMonth` (Free plan: 30,000) applies month-to-date differencing, which is why exports start on the 1st and `restatementDays` is 35. `estimated: true`.
- **No credit balance and no rightsizing, both on purpose.** No public v2 or v3 endpoint exposes plan or remaining credits (open feature requests on ideas.circleci.com), so there is no `credits` capability. Per-job CPU/RAM utilisation does exist (usage CSV columns, experimental v3 `analysis/usage`), but the host's rightsizing contract needs an editable size field applied through `updateResource`, and a job's resource class lives in the repository's `config.yml`.
- **Insights is daily-refreshed and 90 days deep**; workflow metrics come from the individual runs endpoint (bucketed to p50/p95/success/credits per day or hour), project metrics from summing the busiest ten workflows' job time series. No queue time anywhere; the runner API's unclaimed task count is the queue for self-hosted classes.
- **Schedules vs triggers**: the schedule API covers GitHub OAuth and Bitbucket projects only; GitHub App and CircleCI projects use pipeline-definition triggers (`/projects/{project_id}/…`, UUID not slug), where a cron schedule is `event_source.provider: "schedule"`. Both are modelled, each with create/edit/delete. Runner resource classes and tokens are v3; `DELETE ?force=true` also revokes the class's tokens, and "Get credentials" mints a token through `exportCredential`.
- **Trigger a pipeline** goes to `POST /project/{provider}/{org}/{project}/pipeline/run` and falls back to the legacy `POST /project/{slug}/pipeline` on a 400/404; a 200 with `{message}` means nothing was triggered and is surfaced as an error.

### Depot (`@infrawrench/plugin-depot`)

Verified against the generated Connect client in `github.com/depot/sdk-node` (`src/gen/depot/**`), depot.dev/pricing and the runner-types docs, 2026-10. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **The API is Connect RPC, spoken as plain JSON.** `POST https://api.depot.dev/{package}.{Service}/{Method}` with a JSON body; no SDK dependency. Canonical proto3 JSON means camelCase names, RFC 3339 timestamps, enum value names (`STATUS_SUCCESS`, `HARDWARE_8X16`), uint64 as a string, and **default-valued fields omitted**, so every wire field is optional. All method names live in `RPC` in `api.ts`.
- **Usage, never money.** `UsageService/GetUsage` answers one aggregate per `[start_at, end_at]` window (container build minutes per project _name_, Actions minutes per repo by workflow and runner, storage per type, sandbox minutes) with no daily buckets, so a cost day is a request (`maxHistoryDays: 90`). Depot's own example treats the end as inclusive, so `getUsage` sends `endMs - 1`. The plan is not exposed either: the account carries a **plan picker** (it reuses the credential field's `regions` list, the only static picker a credential field has) and a `key=value` **rate overrides** field, both editable from Edit credentials (`rates.ts`).
- **Included minutes are a per-cycle pool**, so the collector always reads from the start of the cycle containing `fromDate` and accumulates; the billable part of a day is shared pro rata across that day's rows so per-project/repo amounts still sum. `minutes_billed` already includes the runner-size multiplier; macOS runners are priced from elapsed minutes at their flat rate and kept out of the pool. The plan fee is spread per day, only in cycles with any usage.
- **Child resources carry their project in the external id** (`projectId/childId`) because builds, tokens, trust policies and image tags are addressed by project; build rows join cost by project id, mapped from the usage's project name via ListProjects.
- **GitHub Actions repositories are not Depot objects**; they are listed from the current cycle's usage, because that is how the API attributes runner minutes.
- Status: incident.io page (`/api/v2/incidents.json`, filtered to unresolved like Groq); the `us-east-1`/`eu-central-1` components map to project regions.

### Devin (`@infrawrench/plugin-devin`)

Verified against the Devin v3 OpenAPI document (`https://docs.devin.ai/v3-openapi.json`) and the billing docs (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One host, Bearer auth, org ids from the key.** `https://api.devin.ai`, service user credential `cog_…` or a personal access token. `/v3/self` names the org for an org-scoped service user; an enterprise key (no org there) lists `/v3/enterprise/organizations` and the plugin covers **every** org; a PAT tries that listing and falls back to `devin_sessions_org_id`. Enterprise service users inherit the org-level permission in every org, so after resolution the plugin only ever calls `/v3/organizations/{org}/…` (plus `/v3beta1/organizations/{org}/members/users`, the only member listing an org key can read). No picker is needed, so it does not use `providerOptions`. Every non-org resource is addressed `<org_id>/<id>`.
- **ACUs, never money.** Consumption is metered in ACUs on every plan (`ViewOrgConsumption`), but no endpoint exposes a rate or an invoice: Enterprise rates live in the order form, and self-serve plans moved to on-demand credits "the same dollar value as" ACUs. Cost is ACUs × the `acuPrice` credential (default $2.25, the published Devin 2.0 pay-as-you-go rate), manifest `estimated`.
- **Billing days start 08:00 UTC** (midnight PST). Consumption `date` values are that boundary in Unix seconds; `billingDay()` maps any timestamp to its day and `fetchConsumption` sends `time_after`/`time_before` on those boundaries.
- **Attribution is a three-level allocation** (`allocateOrgRows`, pure and tested): session rows (resource = session, tags user/playbook/`session_tag`/origin/category) inside each principal's daily total, principal residue (Cascade, terminal, Review, capped sessions) inside the org total, org residue last; each level is scaled down if it exceeds its parent so a day/product always sums to the org figure. A session whose `created_at` and `updated_at` share a billing day spent all of `acus_consumed` that day, so only multi-day sessions cost a per-session request (`MAX_SESSION_LOOKUPS` = 400/org/pass; over the cap the pass reports `degraded`). Multiple session tags are joined with `+` into one `session_tag` value so a session is never counted under two groups.
- **Service users have no names on org endpoints** (the listing is enterprise-only), so they are tagged `Service user <id>` except the key's own, named from `/v3/self`.
- **Writes are replace-only.** Playbook and knowledge-note `PUT`s replace the whole object, so updates (and the note enable/disable action) read the current object and send unchanged fields back. `DELETE /sessions/{id}` _terminates_ a session, so it is a confirmed destructive plugin action, not `supportsDelete`. Secrets are write-only: no value is ever read, and there is no update endpoint.
- **Status feed** is the Statuspage at `devinstatus.com` (status.devin.ai redirects there); "X (Enterprise)" components fold into X.

### Oracle Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-oracle-cloud`)

OCI with an API signing key (tenancy OCID, user OCID, fingerprint, PEM private key, home region). APIs verified against the OCI TypeScript SDK models and Oracle's docs (2026-10); the request signer reproduced Oracle's published test vector (Go SDK `http_signer_test.go`) byte for byte. The committed tests check the signing strings against that vector and verify signatures with a key generated per run, because GitHub push protection rejects any committed PEM private key, Oracle's public test key included. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Signing is WebCrypto, not `node:crypto` or the OCI SDK.** Plugin clients run in the desktop renderer as well as on the server, and WebCrypto is the RSA signer both have. Browsers forbid setting `Date`, `Host` and `Content-Length`, so the signer signs **`x-date`** (OCI accepts it in place of `date`) and _signs_ `host` / `content-length` without setting them: every transport derives the same values from the URL and the exact body bytes signed. A PKCS#1 key is wrapped into PKCS#8 by hand (`pkcs1ToPkcs8`), the only form WebCrypto imports; passphrase-protected keys are refused with instructions. The key is imported lazily so a bad key fails on the first request, not in the synchronous `createClient`. Object Storage `PutObject` is Oracle's documented exception: date, target and host only (`excludeBody`).
- **Hosts differ in whether they sit under `.oci.`** (identity, containerengine, usageapi, usage = Budgets, limits, query = Resource Search) or not (iaas incl. Load Balancer `/20170115`, database, objectstorage, telemetry). Getting that wrong is a DNS failure, so `serviceHost` in `regions.ts` is the only place it lives.
- **List operations never recurse into child compartments**, so a naive lister is regions × compartments calls per type. `inventory.ts` runs one Resource Search structured query per region (`query instance, volume, … resources`) to learn which compartments hold each type and lists only those, plus the root (Search is eventually consistent). A refused or failing Search falls back to the full fan-out. A compartment the user cannot read lists empty (`NotAuthorizedOrNotFound` 404 is OCI's answer for both missing and forbidden).
- **The region of a resource comes from its OCID** (fourth segment: a three-letter key resolved through `GET /regions`, or a region name), because `getResource`/`invokeAction`/`updateResource` receive only the id. Buckets have no OCID in their summary and use `region/name` as the external id; budget alert rules use `budgetId/ruleId`.
- **Cost is two Usage API passes per ≤90-day window** because `groupBy` allows four keys: spend by service, SKU, region and resource (every row), then a time-aggregated resource → compartment-path map stamped on as the `compartment` tag (adds no money, so it cannot double count). `computedAmount` is the billed amount; credits are a separate `queryType` and are not written as rows (their sign and overlap with COST are not documented). DAILY windows start/end at midnight UTC, end exclusive; 48h lag, 12 months of history.
- **Credits are OneSubscription subscribed-service lines with an `availableAmount`** (Universal Credits commitments). Classic-subscription tenancies return nothing, which reads as no balance. Amounts arrive as strings.
- **The size picker is synthetic**: each fixed VM shape once, each flex shape at 1/2/4/…/64 OCPUs with OCI's default memory per OCPU, id `shape/ocpus/memoryGB` (the instance's `size` field uses the same format, so right-sizing can match). An instance with a non-default memory ratio has no catalogue entry and gets no recommendation. vCPUs: 2 per OCPU on x86/A2/A4, 1 on A1. Prices come from Oracle's public price list API (no auth, CORS-enabled for simple GETs) keyed by **part number** (display names were renamed in 2026), paid tier of tiered parts, 744 h/month like Oracle's own calculator, with a 2026-10-04 fallback table.
- **Create forms never ask for an OCID**: compartments are a select labelled by path, subnets/VCNs are resource pickers scoped by region, images are `OS|version` resolved to the newest matching image in the chosen region (image OCIDs are regional), availability domains are "AD 1/2/3" resolved in the region, budget tags come from `listCostTrackingTags`. CreateLoadBalancer answers with a work request only, so the handler polls `loadBalancerWorkRequests` briefly for the new id.
- **Stopped instances are an orphan finding, not a free state**: standard shapes stop compute billing but boot/block volumes keep billing, and Dense I/O, GPU (except A10) and HPC shapes keep billing compute (`billedWhenStopped`). Reserved public IPs are flagged when unassigned, with a reason that says OCI does not bill for them (they consume a limited allowance).
- **OKE kubeconfigs (token version 2.0.0) exec the OCI CLI**, so the cluster is not a Kubernetes peer (it could not work server-side); the kubeconfig is a credential export with that warning.
- Monitoring dimension casing differs per namespace (`resourceId`; Object Storage `resourceDisplayName`; Autonomous Database documented as `RESOURCEID`, so ADB queries retry with it when the first spelling returns nothing). Load balancer metric names are lowerCamel (`httpRequests`).
- The tenancy detail (`enrichDetail`) shows month-to-date spend with OCI's own BASIC forecast, the commitment lines, and OCI's provider-reported carbon emissions (`/20200107/usageCarbonEmissions`, location-based, power-based falling back to spend-based). The org-wide carbon estimate still uses the shared coefficient tables, not OCI's figure.
- Status feed is `https://ocistatus.oraclecloud.com/history.rss`; titles are `service | region display name | ref`, mapped back to region ids by the display names in `regions.ts` (checked against the status page's own components list).

### Datadog (`@infrawrench/plugin-datadog`)

Verified against Datadog's published OpenAPI documents (`DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript`, `.generator/schemas/v{1,2}/openapi.yaml`, 2026-10); the `x-permission` blocks there are where every permission name in `preflight.ts` comes from. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Two keys, one site.** `DD-API-KEY` names the org, `DD-APPLICATION-KEY` names the user and carries their permissions (or a scoped key's subset). Keys only authenticate on their own site, and a wrong site answers **403**, not 401, so it reads as a permission gap. `sites.ts` is the one list of sites (US1, US3, US5, EU, AP1, AP2, UK1, US1-FED, US2-FED) and also feeds the bastion allowlist; `resolveSite` accepts the picker id, Datadog's label or the `DD_SITE` value.
- **Cost is two endpoints stitched together, and the stitch is what `restatementDays` protects.** Estimated cost (`/api/v2/usage/estimated_cost`) only covers the current and previous month; with `cost_aggregation=cumulative` it is month-to-date running totals per day, which `cost-data.ts` differences into days, one request per calendar month from its 1st. Older months come from historical cost, monthly only, dated to the 1st, and **only months lying entirely inside the fetched range are written**. Backfill chunks are whole months; an incremental window of 35 days can never contain a whole month older than the estimated window (that needs at least 59), so no month is ever filed both daily and as a lump. Raising `restatementDays` past ~58 would break that.
- **`charges[]` has a `total` that is the sum of `committed` + `on_demand`** (projected uses `projected_committed` / `projected_on_demand`). `chargesByPricing` uses the fine split when present and `total` only when alone; the split rides as the `pricing` tag.
