The charge-type vocabulary is not in the reference; it comes from recorded fixtures in Datadog's own client test suites.
- **Several product ids share a display label** (`productLabel` in `products.ts`, a pure function so `service` stays reproducible), so rows are aggregated by final key before return; two rows with one key would collapse in `cost_daily`.
- **All cost endpoints are parent-org only.** A child org's keys list resources fine and get a `CostSetupError` for cost. USD is assumed: the API carries no currency.
- **Cost attribution by tag is a detail view, not cost rows**, because the same dollars split by tag would double every total. The configured attribution keys are read from `tag_config_source` (`<org>:::<tag1>///<tag2>`) on a first, unbroken-down request, so nobody types a tag key; not offered on US1-FED.
- **Muting a monitor is a v2 downtime** (`monitor_identifier.monitor_id`); the v1 mute endpoints are gone from the spec. Unmute cancels current downtimes whose `monitor_id` matches, and says so when the silence comes from a tag-scoped downtime it will not touch. `matching_downtimes` on the v1 monitor has integer ids that do not address v2 downtimes, which is why unmute lists v2 instead.
- **A 403 on one lister lists that type empty** (a scoped key without that scope); 401 still throws.
- **Business metric source** (`business-metric-source.ts`): v2 `POST /api/v2/query/timeseries` (Datadog's recommendation over v1 `/api/v1/query`), with a fixed `.rollup(<method>, 3600)` appended, folded into the importer's local days the way CloudWatch's source does. Calendar-aligned `.rollup(sum, daily, 12am, '<tz>')` exists but is only documented for dashboards, so it is not relied on. Rollup buckets are UNIX-aligned, so where a local midnight is off the hour (Kolkata, Kathmandu) the width drops to 900 s. A series holds at most 1,500 points and v2 silently _widens_ `interval` past that, so windows are chunked at 1,440 points and a response whose first two `times` are not exactly one interval apart fails the run rather than folding hours across midnight. `times` is milliseconds in practice though the schema says seconds; both are accepted. The query is assembled from validated parts (metric name regex, scope may not contain braces, single tag key for `by {}`), and `group_tags` values become point labels.

### UploadThing (`@infrawrench/plugin-uploadthing`)

- Auth is `x-uploadthing-api-key` (not a bearer token) against `https://api.uploadthing.com`. **Every endpoint is a POST**, including the read-only ones — `listFiles`, `getUsageInfo` and `getAppInfo` all take a POST with a JSON body.
- The versioning is mixed and both halves are live: nearly everything is `/v6/*`, and only `getAppInfo` and `prepareUpload` have `/v7/` forms. They are not aliases — v7 `prepareUpload` returns a single presigned PUT target, where v6 `uploadFiles` returned S3-style POST policies. Endpoints were read off the live OpenAPI document at `https://api.uploadthing.com/openapi-spec.json`, which is the only complete listing (the docs site's REST page just links to it).
- **One account is one app.** An API key is app-scoped and every endpoint is implicitly scoped to it, so there is no "list apps" call — `ut-app` is a singleton per account, and a second app means a second account.
- One credential field takes **either** shape: the v7 `UPLOADTHING_TOKEN` (base64 JSON of `{apiKey, appId, regions[], ingestHost?}` — what the dashboard's copy button gives you) or a raw `sk_live_…` key. `decodeApiKey` sniffs the `sk_` prefix first, then tries the base64/JSON decode, then sends whatever was pasted so an unusable credential produces UploadThing's own 401 rather than a guess. The token's `appId` is deliberately ignored — `getAppInfo` has to be called anyway for the ACL policy and is authoritative, so trusting the pasted copy would only add a way for the two to disagree. The **region** goes the other way: it exists nowhere in the REST API, so a token is the only place it can come from.
- Files are served at `https://<APP_ID>.ufs.sh/f/<FILE_KEY>` (and at `customId`, when set). The older `https://utfs.io/f/<KEY>` still resolves but is on its way out and is not what the plugin stores — it is only accepted as a fallback when `requestFileAccess` returns an empty `ufsUrl`.
- `getAppInfo` is memoised per client instance. Every file listed needs the app id (to build its URL) and `allowACLOverride` (to decide whether the ACL actions render), and clients are per-request — without the cache a 500-file page would ask for the same three fields 500 times.
- **The listing is not capped.** `fetchFiles` pages `POST /v6/listFiles` (500 at a time) until `hasMore` goes false, so a poll cycle costs one row per file — six figures of rows for a six-figure app. That is the accepted trade for a listing that is actually complete; the earlier 2,000-file cap made the app page lie about its own contents. The loop also breaks on an empty page, because `hasMore` is the server's word and a server asserting it while returning nothing would otherwise spin forever. `fetchFiles` is **memoised per client instance** — one request can list resources, open the browser, and resolve a folder delete, and there is no reason for each to walk the whole app — and every mutation (`uploadBlob`, rename, both delete paths) clears the memo, `updateResource` doing so _before_ its re-read.
- The ACL actions (`make-public` / `make-private` → `POST /v6/updateACL`) are **hidden** when the app has `allowACLOverride: false`, because the API rejects the change rather than ignoring it. `allowAclOverride` and the app default are stamped onto every file's fields at list time so `renderDetail` can make that call without a second fetch.
- `signedUrl` is a declared output but is never populated into `resolvedOutputs` — minting one costs an API call per file. The host only reaches outputs through `resolveOutput` (peer credentials and output-ref reconciliation), so declaring it is free.
- **Content type is not in the file listing.** `GET /v6/pollUpload/{key}` is the only read that returns it, so `getResource` calls it best-effort in a try/catch — it is really an upload-progress endpoint and is not guaranteed to still know about an older file.
- The namespace is **flat**: no folders, no delimiters, no server-side prefix filter. `listStorageObjects` honours `prefix` as a case-insensitive name match client-side, and `makeStorageFolder` is implemented purely to throw a readable explanation — the desktop `StorageBrowserContainer` passes `onMakeFolder` unconditionally (`makeStorageFolder!`), so leaving the method off would surface as a TypeError on an undefined call.
- Create is "upload from URL": download the URL, `POST /v7/prepareUpload` for a presigned target, then PUT the bytes as multipart form data. `slug` (a file route) is optional on prepareUpload, which is the only reason uploading from outside an app's own router works at all. The PUT must not carry the API key or a hand-set `Content-Type` — the URL carries its own signature, and setting the content type strips the boundary `fetch` generates.
- `orphanRule` flags files with `status: "Failed"` — an upload that never completed cannot be served.
- **Folder uploads** keep the picked folder's relative path in the file _name_ (`photos/sub/a.png`), not just the leaf. UploadThing creates no folder either way and assigns its own opaque key, so the slash is only a character in a string — but flattening to the leaf lands two `a.png` files from two subfolders as two identical-looking rows. `uploadStorageObject` strips a leading slash for `pathMode: "absolute"` browsers.
- **`listStorageObjects` synthesizes the folder tree** from those names, S3-delimiter style: everything sharing a first segment folds into one directory entry. Without it an archive upload browses as a screenful of long near-identical rows. Two invariants the rest of the class depends on: a **file** entry carries the real UploadThing key (delete and download address files by key, never by name), and a **directory** entry carries the name prefix and always ends in `/` — which a real file key never does. That trailing slash is how `deleteStorageObject` tells the two apart without a host-side signature change (`FileBrowser` passes an `isDirectory` third arg that `PluginClient.deleteStorageObject` does not declare and neither host forwards), and it then deletes every file under the prefix in `DELETE_BATCH_SIZE` chunks. Note `prefix` here is **navigation, not search** — `FileBrowser` filters its search box client-side and only calls `onList` to open a directory.
- **Downloads** need a `StorageNodeDriver`: `web/src/api/routes/storage.ts` refuses the download when `storageDrivers.get(pluginId)` misses, so a plugin with a file browser but no driver silently loses its Download button. `src/node-driver.ts` is that driver, registered in both `server-core/src/drivers.ts` and `desktop/electron/drivers.ts`. Unlike GCS there is no bearer token covering many objects — the only read grant UploadThing issues is `requestFileAccess`, which presigns **one** file — so `getStorageAccessToken` hands the driver the API key and the driver spends it on a per-file grant. Composing the public `ufs.sh` URL instead would 403 on any private file, and an app's default ACL can be either.
- `ut-app` sets `hiddenChildTypeIds: ["ut-file"]` rather than a `childTables` entry. The storage-browser tab already _is_ the file listing, with upload/download/delete on the same rows; and it browses the name paths as folders, which a flat table cannot — an Overview copy is just a second listing to disagree with it.
- `ut-app` declares `accountRoot: true` (see the contract section above), so opening the account lands on the app page and the sidebar expands the account straight to its files. This is also why `ut-file` is sidebar-hidden: the promotion in `getListableResourceTypes` is what surfaces it, not `showInSidebar`.

### Twilio (`@infrawrench/plugin-twilio`)

The customer's own Twilio account. Unrelated to `server-core/src/twilio-pager.ts` and the `twilio_settings` table, which are Infrawrench's org-level SMS/voice paging transport and never touch this plugin (different AAD namespace too: the pager encrypts under `buildAad("twilio", orgId, …)`, plugin credentials under the account's). Verified against Twilio's published OpenAPI documents (`twilio/twilio-oai`, `spec/json/twilio_{api_v2010,messaging_v1,verify_v2,pricing_v1}.json`, 2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Four hosts, one Basic credential, form-encoded writes.** `api.twilio.com` (2010 API: accounts, numbers, usage, balance, triggers, apps, keys), `messaging.twilio.com/v1`, `verify.twilio.com/v2`, `pricing.twilio.com/v1`; all four are in the bastion allowlist. Auth is `SK… : secret` (API key, preferred, and chosen when both are present) or `AC… : auth token`. 2010 lists page by a relative `next_page_uri`; v1/v2 by an absolute `meta.next_page_url` (`api.ts` `list2010` / `listV1`).
- **Key types gate what lists.** A Standard key gets 401/403 on Accounts and Keys; those listers return empty rather than failing the sync, and the balance throws `CreditAccessError`. Parent-account API keys **cannot reach subaccount resources at all** (Twilio: "Main account API Keys are only available to access main account resources"), so per-subaccount cost and subaccount phone numbers only happen with the auth token.
- **Usage categories overlap and there is no hierarchy field.** `calls ⊃ calls-inbound ⊃ calls-inbound-local`, `pv` holds all video, `authy-sms-outbound` is "also included in the SMS categories". `categories.ts selectLeafCategories` keeps priced categories nothing else priced refines (hyphen-prefix rule, an explicit rollup table, a duplicate list, and a not-a-child list for `calls` vs `calls-sip`/`calls-client`). Then `cost-data.ts` reconciles every day against that day's `totalprice`: a shortfall becomes an `Other`/`unattributed` row, an excess scales the leaves down. The total is therefore always the billed figure even when Twilio ships a rollup the table does not know.
- **Request budget.** Per scope: one range summary (`Usage/Records.json`) decides the priced leaves, then one `Daily.json?Category=` per leaf plus `totalprice`. A scope with zero `totalprice` stops after the summary, which keeps idle subaccounts at one request each. With the auth token the main account (`IncludeSubaccounts=false`) and up to 100 subaccounts are separate scopes (`resourceId` = account SID, `subaccount` tag); the parent's `IncludeSubaccounts=true` daily total is reconciled against their sum, so subaccounts past the cap or unreadable ones land in `Other subaccounts`. With a key it is one `IncludeSubaccounts=true` scope, `resourceId` only when there are no subaccounts.
- **Phone-number price needs a country the number record does not carry.** `pricing.ts` reads it off the E.164 calling code (longest prefix, Canadian NANP area codes told apart from US) and looks up `current_price` by normalised type (`toll free` in Pricing vs `tollfree` on the number). Messaging-service membership comes from `Services/{sid}/PhoneNumbers`, memoised 60 s with the subaccount list so one sync does not repeat it per type. The orphan rule (no webhook, app, trunk or service) is what puts idle numbers on Potential savings.
- **Usage triggers are the provider-side budget alert.** Twilio only lets `FriendlyName`, `CallbackUrl` and `CallbackMethod` change after create, so the rest are `editable: false`. The create form's category picker is built from `Usage/Records/ThisMonth.json` (every category Twilio meters on the account, with this month's spend) behind a curated common list; defaults `totalprice` / `price` / `monthly`. The callback URL suggests an Infrawrench workflow webhook rather than a new inbound route.
- **Subaccount delete is `Status=closed`** (permanent, releases its numbers); suspend/reactivate are plugin actions and the editable `status` enum. Deleting the API key the connection signs in with is refused.
- Account usage, balance and subaccounts live in US1; regional (IE1/AU1) keys are not supported.

### Temporal Cloud (`@infrawrench/plugin-temporal-cloud`)

- **HTTP/JSON, no gRPC.** The Cloud Ops API is gRPC with a grpc-gateway surface on the same host (`https://saas-api.tmprl.cloud`, OpenAPI at `/spec.json`). Every operation is on both, so the plugin uses plain `jsonRestFetch` through the host HTTP service. JSON names are the protobuf camelCase names, enums are their string names (`RESOURCE_STATE_ACTIVE`), int64s are strings. Bearer API key; `temporal-cloud-api-version` is optional over HTTP and pinned to `v0.22.0` in `api.ts` so a default bump cannot change shapes under the mappers.
- **Every mutation is async** and returns an `asyncOperation`; `waitForOperation` polls `/cloud/operations/{id}` for a bounded time, throws on `STATE_FAILED/REJECTED/CANCELLED` with `failureReason`, and returns quietly on timeout (slow is not failed). Updates are **full-spec replaces** guarded by `resourceVersion`: always GET, modify, POST the whole spec back. Namespace tags are the exception (`update-tags`, upsert/remove diff).
- **Billed cost comes from billing reports** (`POST /cloud/billing-reports` → poll `GET /cloud/billing-reports/{id}` → download the CSV from `downloadInfo[].url`). Ranges must be whole billing months; daily granularity reaches the current + previous two months, monthly the current + previous eleven; one report generates per account at a time. `TemporalCostCollector` lives on the client and is reused across the host's month chunks, so a pass creates at most two reports (one daily for the daily window, one monthly for older months on a backfill). FOCUS columns: `ResourceID` is the namespace id, `ServiceSubcategory` the dimension, `ChargeCategory` the charge type, `Tags` a JSON map of arrays (`$tmprl_project` becomes `temporal_project`). **Unverified: whether cost columns are dollars or cents** (the docs' example for `BillingCurrency` reads "USD (cents)"); `amountsInCents` divides by 100 when the currency cell says cents or an actions unit price exceeds 100 per million. Check against a real report.
- **Fallback is usage × editable rates, tagged.** `GET /cloud/usage` (deprecated "pre-release" in the proto, absent from the OpenAPI document, last 90 days only, midnight-aligned) gives actions and active/retained storage in byte-seconds per namespace per day. Priced in `pricing.ts` at published list prices (Business volume tiers on the month-to-date count, decimal GB-hours, plan charge pro rata), overridable by optional credential fields. The manifest cannot say "sometimes estimated", so rows carry `cost_source=estimated|billed`; the estimate pass is **not** flagged `degraded`, so the next billed pass's reconciliation zeroes the estimates instead of leaving both standing.
- **Metrics are a scrape, not a query.** `metrics.temporal.io/v1/metrics` (OpenMetrics, separate Metrics Read-Only key optional) returns only the latest minute, and the account limit is 180 requests/hour, so `scrapeMetrics` caches one all-namespace scrape per key for 60s; history comes from the host's metric store for pinned namespaces. Percentiles combine by max (worst operation), rates by sum. `temporal_namespace` may be the name or the full id; both match. The legacy PromQL endpoint is disabled 2026-10-05 and was not used. There is no schedule-to-start latency in either.
- Removing a custom search attribute is not supported by Temporal Cloud (rename only), so there is no remove action. Failover, add/remove replica, search attributes, connectivity rules and namespace access are `prompt-nosql-command` forms handled in `executeNoSqlCommand`. The failover form needs the namespace name typed back.
- Status feed: Statuspage components are bare provider regions (`us-east-1`, `us-central1`); `regionIdForComponent` maps them to Temporal ids (`aws-us-east-1`, `gcp-us-central1`) by shape, and namespaces store the active region in `fields.region` for correlation.
- The billing-report CSV download URL host is not documented, so it is not in the bastion allowlist (`saas-api.tmprl.cloud`, `metrics.temporal.io` are); an account behind a bastion may fall back to estimates until that host is known.

### Cursor (`@infrawrench/plugin-cursor`)

Team administration over Cursor's Admin API (`api.cursor.com`, Basic auth with the `crsr_` key as username and an empty password), plus the Enterprise-only Analytics and AI Code Tracking APIs on the same host. Every endpoint lives in `src/api.ts` with the doc URL it was verified against; `cursorRequest` keeps the HTTP status (`CursorApiError`) because the plugin branches on 401/403/404 to drop Enterprise-only series silently, and retries 429s itself (most Admin endpoints are **20 requests/minute per team**, which is why the client caches its team snapshot for a minute).

- **Cost is two halves with different provenance.** Usage-based spend is billed data: `POST /teams/filtered-usage-events`, summing `chargedCents` (it includes Cursor's token fee) only for chargeable events whose free-text `kind` matches usage-based/on-demand. Included-pool requests cost nothing extra and are skipped. Seats are _derived_: no endpoint reports the plan, seat tier or price, so rows are paid members × the per-account seat price credentials (defaults $40 standard / $120 premium; premium members listed by email; `free-owner` is the unpaid admin and takes no seat). That one derived component is why the manifest declares `estimated: true`. Seat rows are written **only for days inside the current billing cycle** (`subscriptionCycleStart` from `POST /teams/spend`): the member list is today's snapshot, and backfilling it would bill people for months before they joined. Removed members are excluded even though Cursor bills them to cycle end; there is no removal date to know when.
- **Join keys.** Daily usage rows carry a numeric `userId` and usage events carry only `userEmail`, while members and spend use the encoded `user_…` id. Everything joins on lower-cased email, and cost rows map email → `user_…` so `resourceId` equals the `team-member` externalId; that is what lets Potential savings put a cost next to an idle seat.
- **Idle seats** are a declarative `orphanRule` on `seatStatus = idle`, which the lister sets for a paid, non-removed member absent from 30 days of `POST /teams/daily-usage-data` (only active days come back). There is no join date, so a brand-new member reads idle until first use.
- **Group membership is edited as an email list** because the edit modal has no pickers: `updateResource` resolves emails to ids (refusing unknown addresses by name), reads current membership fresh, and sends the add/remove diff. Create forms use a `policy-picker` of team members instead. Billing groups (`/teams/groups`) and directory groups (`/teams/directory-groups`, which carry `monthlySpendingLimitDollars`) are different objects in Cursor; the plugin calls the latter "Member Group". Directory group members cost one request per group, so listings only fetch them for up to 10 groups and `getResource` always does.
- **Preflight never writes.** Cursor has no read endpoint that distinguishes a read-only key from an admin one, so the `write` capability reports `unknown` rather than probing with an empty bulk update.
- **Not in the API, deliberately not faked:** plan/seat price/invoices, member join or removal dates, invites, role changes, the team-wide default spend limit (shown read-only as `monthlyLimitDollars`). Model access (`/teams/model-access/*`) is a preview API and not surfaced yet.

### CoreWeave (`@infrawrench/plugin-coreweave`)

GPU cloud. One API access token reaches everything, which is CoreWeave's own design rather than a shortcut: the same secret is the Bearer token for the Cloud API (`api.coreweave.com`: CKS clusters, VPCs, AI Object Storage control plane, FOCUS export), for the Prometheus-compatible metrics API (`observe.coreweave.com`), and, as `users[].user.token` in a kubeconfig, for every CKS cluster's own Kubernetes API server. Facts that shaped it:

- **Cost is derived, not billed.** The only usage surface is the FOCUS Billing Export (`GET /v1/billing/focus`, public preview since 2026-09-11, CKS only): hourly billable quantities with **no money fields**, history from 2026-01-01, 90 days per request, 1,000 rows per page, and a 403 that means "export not enabled for the org" (Support turns it on), not a missing role. `cost-data.ts` multiplies quantities by the account's optional **Negotiated rates** credential, else the published on-demand price in `catalog.ts` (read 2026-10-04 off coreweave.com/pricing, no pricing API exists), so `costs.estimated: true` and each row's `pricing` tag says `negotiated`, `list` or `unpriced` (SKUs CoreWeave only quotes on request keep usage, no money). `GPU-Hour` rows divide the instance price by GPU count; `Instance-Hour` uses it whole.
- **The two FOCUS views are pivots of the same usage.** `group_by=location` has cluster and zone but no capacity plan; `group_by=capacity_plan` has the plan but no location; per (hour, SKU) the totals agree. Each location row is split across plans by that day's plan mix for its SKU, which is what lets a Reserved hour carry a `reserved/` rate while still landing on its cluster. A failed plan view degrades to `capacityPlan: unattributed` at flat rates rather than failing collection.
- **Node Pools are Kubernetes, not REST.** The CKS API manages clusters only; pools are the cluster-scoped `NodePool` CRD (`compute.coreweave.com/v1alpha1`) on each cluster's API server, read and merge-patched with the same token. `node-pools.ts` validates before sending: NVL72 types (`gb200-4x`, `gb300-4x*`, `verarubin-4x-e`) take multiples of 18 and reject autoscaling; with autoscaling `min <= target <= max`. Private clusters (and ones still provisioning) list no pools rather than failing the sync. **Scale to zero** stores the prior size in the `infrawrench.io/restore-scale` annotation and **Restore** removes it, which is what makes pools a `lifecycle` type for sleep schedules.
- **The cluster is a Kubernetes peer like DOKS.** `kubeconfig` is built locally from `apiServerEndpoint` + the token (inline token, no CA data: the API servers present publicly trusted certificates), so it passes the server kubeconfig policy. `nodeHourlyRates` covers every priced catalog instance id plus negotiated keys; CKS nodes carry the instance id on `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type`, which is the key the cost model reads. `unreachableWhen` keys on `publicEndpoint`, a field set only when `public` is true.
- **Object Storage needs no static key.** `GET /v1/cwobject/temporary-credentials/api-token` exchanges the token for AWS container-credentials JSON (cached until 5 minutes before `Expiration`); buckets are created/deleted and browsed over SigV4 at `cwobject.com` (virtual-hosted, region = the bucket's zone). That needed `S3StorageConfig.sessionToken` in plugin-base (sent as a signed `x-amz-security-token`), now usable by any plugin with temporary S3 credentials. Bucket inventory, size and settings come from the Bearer API (`/v1/cwobject/bucket-info`, `/v1/cwobject/bucket/settings`). Access keys are listed from `/v1/cwobject/access-key`; CoreWeave only changes key status per principal (`PUT /v1/cwobject/access-key-status`), so the suspend action says so.
- **There is no public API for the account's API access tokens**: they are managed only on the Console's Tokens page, so they are not listed. Object Storage access keys are the closest listable credential and feed the expiry radar.
- **GPU metrics**: `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL` and `DCGM_FI_PROF_PIPE_TENSOR_ACTIVE` with a `cluster` label (cluster name) are the series CoreWeave documents; `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED` and `DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE` are dcgm-exporter defaults CoreWeave does not list by name (**unverified against a live account**; an absent one just hides its chart). Node Pool charts select `node=~` from the pool's nodes (label `compute.coreweave.com/node-pool`). Clusters also chart billable GPU-hours per day from FOCUS.
- **Status feed** is status.io RSS with history: each item's description is the whole update log, so only items whose last state is not `Resolved`/`Completed` (or a not-yet-started `Scheduled` maintenance) are reported.
- **Not done**: the bucket policy editor (`BucketPolicyEditorCapability.vendor` is a closed union of three vendors), Capacity Finder (Spot availability, beta), Telemetry Relay, Dedicated Inference and SUNK resources.

### Modal (`@infrawrench/plugin-modal`)

Modal has **no REST API**; everything, the documented `Workspace.billing.report()` / `modal billing report` included, is the gRPC service `modal.client.ModalClient` on `api.modal.com`, whose schema is `modal_proto/api.proto` in `github.com/modal-labs/modal-client` (the file the official Python, JS and Go SDKs are generated from). Every message and field number the plugin touches is transcribed with its source line in `modal/src/api.ts`. Things the code does not make obvious:

- **gRPC over plain HTTP/1.1, no new dependency.** Modal's Envoy front end accepts gRPC over HTTP/1.1 (verified with curl and Node `fetch`), so `grpc.ts` posts length-prefixed protobuf through the ordinary `HostServices.http` with `content-type: application/grpc` and `te: trailers`. Errors are trailers-only, so `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` arrive as plain headers any fetch can read; the success trailer is invisible over a proxied fetch, so a 200 with `application/grpc` and a well-framed body is success. `te` is a forbidden header for browser fetch (Envoy answers "Missing :te header" without it), which is why calls must go through the host HTTP service (Node on the server, main on desktop), never the renderer's fetch. `proto.ts` is a ~250-line codec (writer + field-number index) instead of protobufjs plus generated code for a 5,000-line schema. Unknown fields are kept and ignored, so Modal adding fields never breaks it; a renumbered field would, and the wrappers are where to look.
- **Desktop `k8s_api_request` honours `responseEncoding: "binary"` now.** It is the renderer's `HostServices.http` and used to UTF-8-decode every body, silently breaking the `rawBody` contract `HttpHostServices` already promised (server and main-process hosts did honour it). Any binary-protocol plugin on desktop needed this.
- **Auth is two headers**, `x-modal-token-id` / `x-modal-token-secret`, plus `x-modal-client-type: 8` and `x-modal-client-version: 1.0.0` (what Modal's own JS SDK sends; the server gates behaviour on the version). The short-lived `x-modal-auth-token` the SDKs fetch via `AuthTokenGet` is only needed on the input plane, which the plugin never calls.
- **Cost = billing report + monthly adjustments.** `WorkspaceBillingReport` (server-streaming) gives per-object, per-day cost with `cost_by_resource` (CPU, Memory, each GPU type), and `tag_names: ["*"]` returns every user tag. It is metered, pre-credit cost. `WorkspaceBillingSummary` per cycle gives `metered_cost`, `billed_cost` and `adjustments` (credits, plan, reservations, egress allowance); those become charge-typed rows on the cycle's 1st. Modal does not document the adjustments' sign, so `adjustmentRows` takes it from the identity `billed - metered`: used as given, flipped, or (when the keys do not add up) one "Adjustments" row carrying the difference. `restatementDays: 35` keeps the current 1st inside every incremental window. Both RPCs are Team/Enterprise-only; a `PERMISSION_DENIED`/`FAILED_PRECONDITION`/`UNIMPLEMENTED` on the report becomes a `CostSetupError`. A streamed report cut short mid-stream would lose its error trailer over HTTP/1.1; `unframe` throws on a truncated frame, and a clean cut between frames is re-read by the 35-day restatement.
- **No credit balance exists in the API**, so there is no `credits` capability; the cycle's credits used are on the workspace page. **Per-function cost does not exist either**: report objects are apps, sandboxes, volumes.
- **Quotas** come from `EnvironmentListItem`: `max_concurrent_tasks`/`gpus` against `current_concurrent_*`, and `effective_cycle_spend_limit` against `current_cycle_usage`, only where a cap is set. `EnvironmentUpdate` takes `optional int32` caps, so a cap can be changed but **not removed** through the API; `updateResource` refuses a cleared field rather than writing 0 (which would mean "zero containers").
- **Functions** are listed from `AppGetInfo` (one call per deployed app, capped at 300, what `modal app info` prints: tag to function id plus GPU and schedule summaries) rather than `FunctionGetById` per function; the detail page calls `FunctionGetById` for resources, autoscaler settings and GPU fallbacks (`ranked_functions`). Function charts bucket `FunctionGetTimeRangeStats` into 24 calls per window (concurrency 6); `container_started_count` is the cold-start count.
- `https://modal.com/id/<object id>` is Modal's own redirect to any object's dashboard page (`modal app dashboard` opens it); environments use `WorkspaceDashboardUrlGet`.
- Status feed: status.modal.com is a Better Stack page; `/index.json` is JSON:API, and a `status_report` whose `aggregate_state` is not `resolved` is an active incident.

### Postmark (`@infrawrench/plugin-postmark`)

Verified against postmarkapp.com/developer/api/* (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **One host, two token headers.** `api.postmarkapp.com` takes `X-Postmark-Account-Token` for the account API (`/servers`, `/domains`, `/senders`) and `X-Postmark-Server-Token` for everything inside a server (`/message-streams`, `/webhooks`, `/templates`, `/triggers/inboundrules`, `/bounces`, `/deliverystats`, `/stats/outbound/*`, `/messages/outbound`). The account `/servers` list returns each server's `ApiTokens`, so the account token alone reaches everything; the plugin caches the server list (60 s) and uses `ApiTokens[0]` per server. A server token alone works too (`GET /server`), minus domains and signatures, which list empty. Errors are `{ ErrorCode, Message }`; `PostmarkApiError` carries the HTTP `status` and `code`.
- **Paging is `count`/`offset`, both required**, with `TotalCount` and items under a per-endpoint key (`Servers`, `Domains`, `SenderSignatures`, `Templates`, `InboundRules`). `/message-streams` and `/webhooks` are not paged (`MessageStreams`, `Webhooks`). Bounce/message search caps `count + offset` at 10,000.
- **Server-scoped external ids are `{serverId}/{id}`** (streams, webhooks, templates, inbound rules) because every call needs that server's token and `getResource` only gets the resource id.
- **Required DNS records are synthesised**, not listed: `GET /domains` carries no DNS fields, so each domain is re-read with `GET /domains/{id}` (concurrency 4, cached with the list) and turned into `postmark-dns-record` children: `DKIMHost`/`DKIMTextValue` (TXT, full FQDN), `DKIMPendingHost`/`DKIMPendingTextValue` during a rotation, and `ReturnPathDomain` → `ReturnPathDomainCNAMEValue` (`pm.mtasv.net`). They declare `dnsRole: record` with the default `name`/`type`/`content` keys and the sending domain (not a zone) as parent, so the Domains view lists them unattributed. SPF is deliberately omitted: Postmark no longer requires it (`verifyspf` is deprecated).
- **Streams cannot be deleted**: delete archives (`POST /message-streams/{id}/archive`, purged 45 days later), `unarchive` restores. Lists use `IncludeArchivedStreams=true`. Create needs a client-chosen `ID` plus `Name` and `MessageStreamType` (`Transactional`/`Broadcasts`; inbound streams are created by Postmark).
- **Webhook edits are partial at Postmark** (omitted triggers are unchanged) but the plugin still merges with the current webhook so the basic-auth password, which `GET /webhooks/{id}` returns in clear, is resent rather than wiped. The password never lands in fields. `POST /webhooks/{id}/verify` tests every enabled trigger and returns `{ Success, Results[] }`; the "Send test events" action throws the failing triggers.
- **Suppressions**: `GET /message-streams/{id}/suppressions/dump`, add/remove are POST `.../suppressions` and `.../suppressions/delete`, 50 addresses per call (the prompt command batches). SpamComplaint suppressions cannot be deleted. Bounce reactivation is `PUT /bounces/{id}/activate`, offered as a prompt listing recent `CanActivate` bounces.
- **Metrics** are per day only (`Days[]` with `Date`), from `/stats/outbound/{sends,bounces,spam,opens,clicks}`, `messagestream` narrows to a stream. Soft bounces sum `SoftBounce + Transient`.
- **Status feed** is Sorry™, not Statuspage (`/api/v2/*` 404s): `GET status.postmarkapp.com/api/v1/notices`, custom JSON. Reported: unplanned notices with `timeline_state` present/past_recent, planned ones underway. Notices carry no components, so all are provider-wide.
- **Not done, deliberately**: costs/credits/quotas (Postmark has no billing or usage-limit API); Terraform export (no official Postmark provider, only community ones); orphan rules (an archived stream or unconfirmed signature costs nothing, so it is not a savings finding). Server deletion via API is not enabled on every Postmark account (docs: "not enabled for all accounts"); the error surfaces as-is. Template bodies are only read on `getResource`, not in the lister.

### Runpod (`@infrawrench/plugin-runpod`)

Verified 2026-10 against the REST OpenAPI document (`https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json`), the GraphQL schema reference (`https://graphql-spec.runpod.io`, introspection is disabled on the live server, but unknown fields still fail validation, so queries were checked against it), `runpodctl` source and the Terraform provider source.

- **Three hosts, one key.** REST `rest.runpod.io/v1` (pods, endpoints, templates, network volumes, registry auths, billing) and GraphQL `api.runpod.io/graphql` both take `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; the Serverless host `api.runpod.ai/v2/{id}/{health,purge-queue}` is documented with the bare key in `authorization`. A bad key is HTTP 401 with `{"error":{}}` on both REST and GraphQL; GraphQL application errors are HTTP 200 with `errors[]`, which `api.ts` turns into status-bearing errors. REST lists are plain arrays with no pagination.
- **GraphQL is not optional.** Only GraphQL has the account (`myself { clientBalance currentSpendPerHr spendLimit maxServerlessConcurrency pubKey savingsPlans }`), GPU types with prices and stock (`gpuTypes { ... lowestPrice(input:{gpuCount:1}) { stockStatus } }`), data centers with per-GPU availability (`dataCenters { gpuAvailability }`), pod runtime telemetry and `machine.podHostId`. `gpuTypes` and `dataCenters` answer without auth. Pod enrichment is best effort: a key GraphQL refuses still lists pods, just without utilization or SSH proxy user.
- **Pod state is desired state only** (`RUNNING`/`EXITED`/`TERMINATED`). RUNNING with a null GraphQL `runtime` is shown as `starting`. Lifecycle is `POST /pods/{id}/{start,stop,restart,reset}`; terminate is `DELETE /pods/{id}`; lock is `PATCH {locked}`.
- **SSH goes through the proxy**: user `<podId>-<machine.podHostId>` at `ssh.runpod.io:22`, which fits `sshEndpoint` (no port field) via `usernameFieldKey: sshUser`. The direct route (`publicIp` + `portMappings["22"]`) is an output only, because `sshEndpoint` cannot carry a non-22 port.
- **SSH keys are one string.** `myself.pubKey` holds every authorized_keys line; writes replace it whole with `updateUserSettings(input: {pubKey})` (not in the public GraphQL reference, but it is what `runpodctl ssh add-key` uses). Keys are identified by SHA256 fingerprint (`sha256-<urlsafe b64>` externalId), computed with Web Crypto.
- **`region` is the data center id** (`EU-RO-1`). The status page (`uptime.runpod.io`, Better Stack, `/index.json`) names its components with the same ids (one has a trailing space, so trim), so status correlation is exact.
- **Billing**: `/billing/pods?grouping=podId`, `/billing/endpoints?grouping=endpointId`, `/billing/networkvolumes`, all `bucketSize=day` with RFC 3339 `startTime`/`endTime`; `amount` is USD, `time` the bucket start. Network-volume rows carry `amount` and a separate `highPerformanceStorageAmount`; the spec describes them as separate charges and the plugin emits them as two services. If Runpod ever turns out to include HP storage in `amount`, that is a double count to fix in `mapVolumeRecords`.
- **Quotas**: `spendLimit` (USD/hour, default $80) against `currentSpendPerHr`, and `maxServerlessConcurrency` against the sum of `workersMax` across endpoints (Runpod's documented rule for the worker quota). Both rise with balance, so `increaseUrl` is the billing page.
- **Savings plans** come from `myself.savingsPlans` as `savings_plan` commitments with `upfrontCost` and `costPerHr`.
- **Terraform**: `runpod/runpod` (Runpod's own provider, v1.0.x, community tier). None of its resources implement `ImportState`, so exports carry no import id and say so. `runpod_pod.ports` is one comma-separated string, while `runpod_template.ports` is a list.
- **CORS**: `rest.runpod.io` and `api.runpod.ai` answer preflights with `*`; `api.runpod.io/graphql` answered the preflight with 204 and no CORS headers in testing, so GraphQL from a browser renderer depends on `services.http`.
- **Not done**: env var values are never synced (only names), so secret env cannot leak into inventory; there is no metrics time series (Runpod's public API has only point-in-time `runtime` utilization, stored as fields); endpoint template changes are not editable (would need a picker in an edit form); Instant Clusters and the Hub are not covered.

### Render (`@infrawrench/plugin-render`)

- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <api key>` against `https://api.render.com/v1` (OpenAPI spec at api-docs.render.com, verified 2026-10). Keys are per user, unscoped, and see every workspace the user is in. Optional `workspaceId` credential (provider-options picker over `GET /owners`) narrows every list with `ownerId=`; empty means all workspaces.
- 15 resource types: `workspace`, `service` (all five types in one type, `serviceType` field), `deploy` / `env-var` / `custom-domain` / `job` (children of service, externalId `{serviceId}/{childId}`; env vars keyed by name), `disk`, `postgres`, `key-value`, `env-group`, `env-group-var` (child, `{groupId}/{key}`), `project`, `environment` (child of project), `blueprint`, `maintenance`.
- Lists are arrays of `{<item>, cursor}` wrappers (`service`, `postgres`, `keyValue`, `envVar`, `customDomain`, `deploy`, `job`, `disk`, `owner`, `blueprint`, `sync`, `project`, `environment`); `/env-groups` and `/maintenance` are **not** wrapped. `api.listAll` unwraps when the key is present. Next page = `?cursor=<last row's cursor>`, `limit` max 100.
- `GET /environments` requires `projectId`, so environments are listed per project. Env group lists carry no variables; `GET /env-groups/{id}` does.
- Rate limits per user: 400 GET/min, 30 other writes/min, 30 `/logs`/min, 10 deploy/suspend/resume/PATCH per service per min, 20 service creations/hour. 429 retried once when `Ratelimit-Reset` <= 5 s. Manifest `rateLimit` 40/5 per s. Deploys capped at 10 and jobs at 20 per service per sync.
- Connection strings come only from `GET /postgres/{id}/connection-info` and `/key-value/{id}/connection-info`; they are outputs resolved on demand, never fields. Env var values likewise (the API returns them in clear).
- Actions: service deploy / clear-cache deploy / deploy a commit or image (`POST /deploys` with `commitId` or `imageUrl`), rollback (`POST /services/{id}/rollback {deployId}`; auto-deploy stays on), restart, suspend/resume (lifecycle), scale, autoscaling (`PUT`/`DELETE /autoscaling`), maintenance mode (PATCH `serviceDetails.maintenanceMode`), edge cache purge, one-off jobs, cron run/cancel (`/cron-jobs/{id}/runs`). Postgres: restart, suspend, resume, failover (HA only), export, PITR (`POST /recovery {restoreTime, restoreName}` makes a new db), create/drop users. Disk snapshot restore. Env group link/unlink (also drag-to-attach onto a service). Maintenance reschedule (PATCH `scheduledAt`) and trigger. Parameterised ones use `prompt-nosql-command` + `executeNoSqlCommand`.
- Logs: `GET /logs` needs `ownerId` + `resource[]`, pages by `nextStartTime`/`nextEndTime`; tail reads <= 3 pages backward. Job logs use the job id as resource.
- Metrics: `/metrics/{cpu,memory,instance-count,http-requests,http-latency(quantile=0.95),bandwidth,disk-usage,disk-capacity,active-connections,replication-lag}` with `resource=`; bandwidth takes no `resolutionSeconds`. Disk metrics query the disk's service id. Each metric fails independently.
- Plans: no plan-listing API. Service sizes are the spec's hardware ids (`0.5c-512mb` … `12c-96g`) plus legacy named plans, with CPU/RAM/list price from render.com/pricing; Postgres and Key Value plans are the spec enums.
- Status feed: status.render.com Statuspage; per-region components share names under five region groups, so `regionalizeBody` rewrites incident components via fixed `group_id` → region before `parseStatuspageIncidents`. Dashboard/APIs are provider-wide; marketing site ignored.
- Terraform: `render-oss/render` ~> 1.9; services (by type, `runtime_source` native/docker/image), `render_postgres`, `render_keyvalue`, `render_env_group` (values not synced, comment says so). Projects skipped (need the whole `environments` map). All import by Render id.
- Posture: Postgres/KV allow lists containing `0.0.0.0/0`; workspaces without enforced 2FA. Expiry: free Postgres `expiresAt`. Peers: Postgres → `postgres`, Key Value → `redis`, both gated on a non-empty allow list.
- Not done: costs (Render has no billing API; open feature request on feedback.render.com), webhooks, registry credentials, log/metrics streams, notification settings, workflows, dedicated IPs, routes/headers for static sites, secret files editing.

### Stripe (`@infrawrench/plugin-stripe`)

Stripe as infrastructure, not a payments dashboard. Verified against Stripe's published OpenAPI spec (`github.com/stripe/openapi`, `latest/openapi.spec3.sdk.json`, version `2026-09-30.endive`) and docs.stripe.com, 2026-10.

- **Auth**: one `apiKey` credential, `Authorization: Bearer`. Restricted (`rk_…`, recommended) or secret (`sk_…`); `pk_…` is refused in the constructor. A key belongs to exactly one account, so `stripe-account` is the `accountRoot`. Live vs test is read off the key prefix (`(sk|rk)_live_`) and drives `/test/` Dashboard links. Every request pins `Stripe-Version: 2026-09-30.endive` (v2 rejects requests without one). `api.ts` is the only HTTP path (host `services.http` when present, `StripeApiError` carries `status`/`type`/`code`). CORS is open on `api.stripe.com` (echoes the Origin), so no Electron work.
- **Two API generations on one host.** v1: form-encoded bodies with bracket nesting (`recurring[interval]`, `enabled_events[0]`), pages by `has_more` + `starting_after`. v2 (`/v2/core/event_destinations`, `/v2/core/events`): JSON bodies, pages by `next_page_url` (a relative path), redacted fields need `include[]` (`webhook_endpoint.url` on reads, `webhook_endpoint.signing_secret` only on create).
- **10 types**: `stripe-account` (root), `stripe-connected-account`, `stripe-webhook-endpoint`, `stripe-event-destination`, `stripe-product`, `stripe-price` (child of product, `showInSidebar`), `stripe-meter`, `stripe-payout` (100 most recent), `stripe-report-run`, `stripe-sigma-query-run`. Connect, meters, Reporting and Sigma listers return `[]` on 403/404/"not a platform" 400 (but still throw on 401).
- **Signing secrets are one-shot.** `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints` returns `secret` and v2 create returns `signing_secret` only when included; neither is ever readable again and there is no roll API. Create stores it as a plaintext `secretState` plus `services.secrets.setPlaintext`; `resolveOutput("signingSecret")` reads it back and explains the Dashboard for endpoints made elsewhere. `secretExportTemplates` exports it as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- **Event pickers are static**: Stripe has no list-event-types endpoint. `event-types.ts` copies the 269-entry `enabled_events` enum of `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints` (snapshot) and the 240 `type`s of `v2.core.event` schemas (thin: `v1.*` and `v2.*` names) from the spec; refresh when the pinned version moves. Create forms use `policy-picker` (JSON array); edits take a comma list; `parseEventList` reads both.
- **Webhook endpoint quirks**: no `connect` field on the returned object; an endpoint created with `connect=true` carries `application`. Disable/enable is `POST …{disabled}`. `api_version` is create-only.
- **Meter usage needs a customer.** `GET /v1/billing/meters/{id}/event_summaries` requires `customer`, `start_time` and `end_time` aligned to the `value_grouping_window` (day/hour). Metrics find customers via active prices with `recurring.meter == id` then `GET /v1/subscriptions?price=&expand[]=data.customer`, capped at 10 customers. Meters cannot be deleted, only deactivated/reactivated; only `display_name` is updatable.
- **Prices are immutable** except `nickname`, `lookup_key` (+`transfer_lookup_key=true` so setting a key steals it), `tax_behavior` (once, from unspecified), `active`, `metadata`. Sub-cent amounts go as `unit_amount_decimal` in minor units. Products with prices cannot be deleted (400): the plugin rewrites that into "archive instead".
- **Currency exponents**: zero-decimal `bif clp djf gnf jpy kmf krw mga pyg rwf ugx vnd vuv xaf xof xpf`, three-decimal `bhd jod kwd omr tnd`, everything else hundredths (`api.ts currencyExponent`).
- **Cost = Stripe's own fees from `GET /v1/balance_transactions`**, paged one UTC day at a time (`created[gte]/[lt]`, ≤100 pages per day, 4 days in flight). Two sources: `fee_details[]` on any transaction (`stripe_fee`, `payment_method_passthrough_fee` usage; `tax` → chargeType tax; negative → refund; `application_fee` and `withheld_tax` are excluded as not Stripe's) and whole-amount fee transactions `stripe_fee` (product named from the description before `(`/`:`/`-`, e.g. "Billing", "Radar for Fraud Teams"), `stripe_fx_fee`, `tax_fee`. Service from `reporting_category` otherwise. Rows stay in the transaction currency, tag `feeType`, `chargeTypes: true`, not estimated. Stripe has no invoice API for its own charges.
- **Subscriptions overview** (account detail, via `enrichDetail` stash): 10 pages of `status=all`, counts per status, cancel-at-period-end, MRR per currency from licensed items of active/trialing/past_due subs (`items[].price.recurring`, normalised to a month). `current_period_*` moved to subscription items in recent versions; not used.
- **Failing deliveries**: `GET /v1/events?delivery_success=false` (last 30 days). It does not say which endpoint failed; the endpoint detail filters it to its subscribed types and links to the Workbench delivery log. Account `getLogs` has three containers: events, failed deliveries, thin events (`/v2/core/events`).
- **Status feed**: `status.stripe.com/current` JSON has been frozen since Feb 2024. The live feed is the Atlassian Statuspage at `www.stripestatus.com` (page `d5zv7xbys5v3`), six ungrouped components: "Stripe API" (provider-wide), "Global payments", "Revenue and finance automation", "Stripe core components", "Banking-as-a-service" (unmapped) and "Acquirers and payment methods" (unmapped).
- **Terraform**: official `stripe/stripe` (~> 0.3, generated by Stripe): `stripe_webhook_endpoint`, `stripe_product`, `stripe_price` (recurring block; tiered/custom-amount skipped), `stripe_billing_meter`, `stripe_v2_core_event_destination` (`azure_event_grid` is an attribute, the others blocks). Provider config `api_key`. Import ids are object ids.
- **Preflight** probes each area with a `limit=1` GET; a restricted key without the permission gets 403. `policyTemplate` emits the Dashboard permission list (text).
- **Deliberately not done**: API key management (`POST /v2/iam/api_keys` is a preview limited to approved Stripe Apps with `api_key_write`, and only mints unrestricted keys); payout creation (moves money); connected-account creation/edit (controller-dependent rules); downloading report/Sigma files (`files.stripe.com` needs the key; Dashboard link instead); quotas/credits (no API).

### Supabase (`@infrawrench/plugin-supabase`)

Verified against the Management API OpenAPI document (`https://api.supabase.com/api/v1-json`, 2026-10) and the `supabase/supabase` Terraform provider 1.11.0.

- **Auth**: one personal access token (`sbp_…`, classic or scoped) as `Authorization: Bearer` against `https://api.supabase.com`. Scoped tokens carry the operation's `x-oauth-scope` (`projects:read`, `secrets:read`, `database:write`, `analytics:read`…); there is no endpoint that reports a token's scopes, so `verifyCredentials` probes one read per capability and reads 401/403 as missing. Limit 120 req/min per user per project/org scope; analytics endpoints 10-30/min, so logs and metrics are on demand only.
- **Resource types**: organization, project, branch, function, secret, api-key, bucket, backup, read-replica, auth (one per project, settings editor), sso-provider, third-party-auth, signing-key. Children live under the project; external ids are `{ref}/{id}` (branch: `{parentRef}/{branchRef}`, so every `/v1/branches/{x}` call uses the branch ref, not the deprecated UUID).
- **Projects list is thin.** `GET /v1/projects` has no compute size, disk or replicas; `GET /v1/organizations/{slug}/projects` (offset/limit paged) does, including `READ_REPLICA` databases (that is the only replica listing) and `is_branch` (preview branches are projects too and are filtered out of the project list). The lister also reads ssl-enforcement, network-restrictions, backups, pooler, `api-keys/legacy` and `billing/addons` per running project, each failure-tolerant, because posture checks need those fields synced.
- **Paused projects** (`INACTIVE`) answer errors from service endpoints; `perProject(..., {runningOnly})` skips them for functions/secrets/keys/buckets/auth types. A per-project 404 is skipped; other errors fail the listing (a short list reads as deletions).
- **The postgres password is never returned** after create. Created projects store it via `services.secrets.setPlaintext(resourceId, "dbPassword")`; otherwise "Reset database password" (`PATCH /database/password`, also `rerollOutput` and the postgres peer's `credentialSetupAction` via `executeNoSqlCommand("reset-db-password")`) sets and stores a new one. Pooler connection strings come from `config/database/pooler` with a literal `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` placeholder (transaction mode on 6543; session mode is the same host on 5432). Branch credentials ARE returned by `GET /v1/branches/{ref}` (`db_user`/`db_pass`).
- **SQL** runs through `POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/query` (`supportsRestQuery`, `executeQuery`, sentinel `connectionStringOutputKey: "__supabase__"`), so it needs no password.
- **Settings editors**: project "Configuration" tab fans changed `{section}.{key}` ids out to `PUT config/database/postgres`, `PATCH config/database/pooler`, `PATCH postgrest`, `PATCH config/storage` (nested `features.*.enabled`) and `PATCH config/realtime`; only keys the write bodies accept are listed. Auth tab is a curated subset of `PATCH config/auth` (238 keys); OAuth client secrets and `smtp_pass` are write-only hashes and deliberately omitted.
- **Edits through add-ons**: compute size is `PATCH billing/addons {addon_type: compute_instance, addon_variant: ci_<size>}`, PITR `pitr_7|14|28` (DELETE the selected variant to turn off), IPv4 `ipv4_default`. Disk is `POST config/disk {attributes}` (gp3 takes `throughput_mibps`, io2 does not). Network restrictions are replaced whole with `POST network-restrictions/apply`; an empty config means open to all.
- **Edge Functions** deploy via multipart `POST functions/deploy?slug=` (`metadata` JSON field + `file` parts, `buildMultipartBody`); deploy upserts, which is how code is changed. `GET functions/{slug}/body` returns the bundle, not source, so there is no code editor for existing functions.
- **Secrets list returns a SHA-256 digest** in `value`, never the value. `POST secrets` upserts. `SUPABASE_*` names are platform-reserved and hidden.
- **Storage** is not in the Management API beyond a bucket list: create/update/empty/delete and the object browser use `https://{ref}.supabase.co/storage/v1` with a secret key read via `api-keys?reveal=true`. New `sb_secret_…` keys go in `apikey` only (not a JWT, never a Bearer); legacy `service_role` JWTs go in both. The storage browser's bucket handle is `{ref}/{bucket}` because bucket names repeat across projects. Empty folders are a `.emptyFolderPlaceholder` object.
- **Logs**: `analytics/endpoints/logs` is the ClickHouse-backed unified endpoint that replaced `logs.all` (removed 2026-09-23). One `logs` table, filter with `source = 'edge_logs'` (the current guide says `source`; the July changelog said `source_name`), structured fields in the `log_attributes` string map (`function_id` for function logs), max 24 h window.
- **Metrics**: `usage.api-counts` (window enum 15min…7day) for request series; `config/disk/util` and the Prometheus scrape at `analytics/endpoints/metrics` (node_exporter/postgres_exporter names) for point-in-time gauges; `functions.combined-stats` per function id.
- **Costs**: no billing API exists. `estimated: true` rows from today's selected add-ons at list price only (hourly × 24, monthly ÷ days in month); plan fee, compute credit and usage lines are absent. Rows only for the day the pass runs.
- **Quotas**: database disk used vs filesystem size per running project (a full disk forces read-only mode).
- **Status feed**: Statuspage at `status.supabase.com`; region components are named exactly like project regions (`eu-west-1`), service components map to resource types, Management API/Dashboard escalate provider-wide.
- **Terraform**: `supabase_project` (import id = ref, per-project sensitive password variable), `supabase_branch` (needs `git_branch`; import id is the branch UUID which inventory does not keep, so no import id), `supabase_apikey` (import `{ref}/{name}`). Edge functions skipped (provider deploys from local files); `supabase_settings` not emitted.
- **Deliberately not done**: PITR restore and physical-backup restore (need a timestamp or are `x-internal`), JIT database access, SQL snippets, CLI login roles, pgsodium root key (destructive), project claim tokens. Advisors, health, disk, upgrade eligibility and domains are fetched in `enrichDetail`, stashed under `_`-prefixed field keys.

### Vultr (`@infrawrench/plugin-vultr`)

- Auth: account API key as `Authorization: Bearer` against `https://api.vultr.com/v2`. The key carries its user's ACLs (`subscriptions`, `provisioning`, `billing`, `dns`, `firewall`, `objstore`, `loadbalancer`, ...) and Vultr's per-key IP **Access Control** list; a refused IP answers 401/403, which preflight calls out. Preflight probes one list call per area. Errors are `{error, status}`; `VultrApiError.status` keeps the HTTP code. API verified against `vultr/govultr` v3.33.1 (2026-10-05) and `terraform-provider-vultr` v2.32.0 docs.
- Pagination is cursor-based: `per_page` (max 500) + `cursor`, next cursor in `meta.links.next` (empty string on the last page). Every payload is wrapped in a named envelope (`instances`, `vke_clusters`, `billing_invoices`, `invoice_items`, `object_storages`, `reserved_ips`, `firewall_groups`, `bare_metals`, ...), so `api.all(path, key)` takes the key.
- Public without a key: `/regions` (with `options` like `kubernetes`, `load_balancers`, `block_storage_high_perf`), `/plans?type=all` (151 plans, `monthly_cost`, `hourly_cost`, `locations`, and `location_cost` overrides, e.g. São Paulo), `/os`, `/applications`, `/kubernetes/versions`. `/databases/plans` and `/object-storage/tiers` need a key.
- Resource types: `instance`, `bare-metal`, `block-storage`, `snapshot`, `backup`, `kubernetes-cluster` + `node-pool` (`{cluster}/{pool}`), `database` + `database-user` / `database-db` (`{db}/{name}`), `load-balancer`, `firewall-group`, `vpc`, `reserved-ip`, `domain` (externalId is the domain name) + `dns-record` (`{domain}/{recordId}`), `object-storage` (subscription) + `bucket` (`{subscription}/{bucket}`), `ssh-key`, `startup-script`, `account` + `invoice`.
- Instance create needs exactly one boot source; the image picker encodes it as `os:<id>`, `app:<id>` (one-click), `image:<image_id>` (marketplace) or `snapshot:<id>`. SSH keys must be stored keys (`sshkey_id`), so a picked public key is matched by material or uploaded first. `user_data` and startup `script` are base64 on the wire, and the startup-script list omits the body (single GET has it). Backups, DDoS and IPv6 are read from `features[]` (`auto_backups`, `ddos_protection`, `ipv6`); backups are toggled with `PATCH {backups: "enabled"|"disabled"}` and cost 20% of the plan. Plan changes go through `PATCH {plan}`; `/instances/{id}/upgrades` lists the allowed target plans (upgrade only).
- Verb quirks: PATCH for instances, blocks, reserved IPs, LBs, node pools, records, SSH keys, scripts, SOA; PUT for VKE clusters, databases, firewall groups, VPCs, snapshots, domains (`{dns_sec}`) and object storage. Firewall rules have no action (allow-only); "anywhere" is subnet `0.0.0.0`/`::` with size 0; `source: "cloudflare"` allows Cloudflare's ranges.
- VKE kubeconfig is base64 in `kube_config`; the cluster's `endpoint` is a bare host, so `apiEndpoint` is read from the kubeconfig's `server:`. Deleting with `/delete-with-linked-resources` also removes the LBs and volumes Kubernetes made.
- Databases: no engine-version listing exists, so the create form offers pg 18 to 14, mysql 8, valkey 7, kafka 3.8/3.7; `/version-upgrade` (GET) lists real upgrade targets. Restore/fork `type` is `basebackup` or `pitr` (from `vultr-cli`), and both create a new database. Kafka has no backups (`managedBackups: false`) and its SASL port is `sasl_port`. `ca_certificate` may be base64-wrapped PEM; `pemOf` handles both.
- Object Storage: each subscription has its own S3 host (`{region}.vultrobjects.com`) and keys from `GET /object-storage/{id}`; the bucket browser signs path-style SigV4 with those keys (`plugin-base` S3 helpers, direct fetch, not `services.http`). Buckets are listed/created/deleted through `/object-storage/{id}/bucket`.
- Costs (`cost-data.ts`): invoices + `/billing/invoices/{id}/items` (items have `product`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `total`, no subscription id or region), spread evenly over covered days; the open month from `/billing/pending-charges` spread to today; negative items are `credit`, tax-named items `tax`. Dimension: `service` only. `restatementDays: 62`. Credits: negative `balance` minus `pending_charges`.
- Metrics: the API has no instance CPU/memory series. Instances and bare metal show daily bandwidth (`/bandwidth`, bytes per `YYYY-MM-DD`); databases show a one-point CPU/memory/disk reading from `/usage`. No rightsizing for that reason.
- Status feed: `https://status.vultr.com/status.json` (custom JSON, not Statuspage): `regions.{id}.alerts[]` keyed by API region ids plus `service_alerts[]` with an optional `region`; `status: "ongoing"` while active.
- Not done: Container Registry, CDN, Serverless Inference, ISOs, organizations/IAM, NAT gateways, database connection pools/topics/connectors, LB auto-SSL. Vultr's DNS records cannot point at Vultr instances through the shared `dnsContentField` source lists until plugin-base adds Vultr outputs there.

### Resend (`@infrawrench/plugin-resend`)

Verified against Resend's published OpenAPI spec (`github.com/resend/resend-openapi` `resend.json`, 1.5.1, updated 2026-09-29) and resend.com/docs, 2026-10.

- **Auth**: one `apiKey` (`re_…`), Bearer, host `api.resend.com`. Only **Full access** keys work: a sending-access key answers 401 `restricted_api_key` on everything but sending (the account lister rethrows that with a "needs Full access" message). A malformed key is a 400 `validation_error`, not a 401. Errors are `{statusCode, message, name}`; `ResendApiError` keeps `status` and `errorName`.
- **No CORS** on `api.resend.com` (no `Access-Control-*` even on preflight), so the desktop renderer depends on the host `services.http` path; `api.ts resendFetch` uses it whenever present.
- **Rate limit 10 req/s per team** (shared across keys). `resendFetch` retries a 429 up to 3 times after `retry-after` (capped 10 s), except `daily_quota_exceeded` / `monthly_quota_exceeded`, which waiting does not fix. Manifest `rateLimit` is 5/s.
- **Pagination**: `limit` 1-100 + `after=<last id>` cursor, `has_more`. Timestamps come back as Postgres text (`2023-04-26 20:21:26.347412+00`); `toIso` normalises.
- **15 types**: `resend-account` (root, from `GET /usage`), `resend-domain`, `resend-dns-record` (child), `resend-api-key`, `resend-webhook`, `resend-email` (100 newest), `resend-broadcast`, `resend-template`, `resend-segment`, `resend-topic`, `resend-contact` (1,000 newest), `resend-contact-property`, `resend-suppression`, `resend-automation`, `resend-oauth-grant`.
- **DNS records are only on the single GET**: `GET /domains` omits `records`, so each domain is re-read (`GET /domains/{id}`, concurrency 3) and cached 60 s so the domain and DNS-record listers share one pass. Record names are relative (`resend._domainkey`, `send`, `@`/empty for apex) and stored fully qualified; `record` is the purpose (SPF/DKIM/Receiving/Tracking/TrackingCAA), `ttl` is the string `"Auto"`, MX carries `priority`. Declared `dnsRole: record` with `priorityKey`, parent is the domain (not a zone), like Postmark. Domain posture check: `status` not `verified`.
- **Domain update**: `PATCH /domains/{id}` takes `capabilities` as a whole object, so changing only `sending` re-reads the domain to keep `receiving`. Region and custom return path are create-only. `tls` is accepted on create/update but not returned on read.
- **Secrets**: webhook `GET /webhooks/{id}` returns `signing_secret` every time (resolved live; `POST …/signing-secret/rotate` rotates). API key tokens are returned only by `POST /api-keys` (stored as plaintext secretState + `services.secrets`); the list returns only `id, name, created_at, last_used_at`, never the permission or domain.
- **Webhook events**: no list endpoint; the 19 types come from the spec's `webhooks` section (email._, contact._, domain._, suppression._). Deliveries: `GET /webhooks/{id}/events` (status pending/attempting/success/failed), replay `POST …/events/{event_id}/replay`; the detail table's per-row Replay button encodes the event id in the action id (`replay:<id>`).
- **Metrics**: `GET /emails/metrics` with `dimensions=period`, `granularity` hourly/daily, filtered by `domain_id` or `broadcast_id`; list params are comma-joined. Rows carry metric keys directly; rates are fractions (charted ×100). Cached by Resend up to 15 min, clamped to plan retention.
- **Quotas** from `GET /usage`: emails daily (free plan only) and monthly, contacts, segments, domains, automation runs, AI credits; `null` limits (unlimited / not on plan) are skipped.
- **Status**: `status.resend.com` redirects to `resend-status.com`, incident.io's Statuspage emulation: `/api/v2/incidents.json` filtered to unresolved (unresolved.json 404s). Incidents carry no components, so they read provider-wide.
- **Not done**: cost (no billing API), Terraform (no official provider; only community ones), audiences (deprecated for segments; broadcasts' `audience_id` mapped to `segmentId`), automation create (step graphs), contact imports, segment metrics (private beta), sending email.

### Convex (`@infrawrench/plugin-convex`)

Verified against the Management API OpenAPI (`https://api.convex.dev/v1/openapi.json`) and the Deployment API OpenAPI (`npm-packages/@convex-dev/platform/deployment-openapi.json` in `get-convex/convex-backend`), 2026-10.

- **Auth**: one team access token (Team Settings > Access Tokens). Management API wants `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the per-deployment Deployment API (`{deploymentUrl}/api/v1`) wants `Authorization: Convex <token>` and accepts the same team token. The team id comes from `GET /token_details` (`type: "teamToken"`); project tokens and deploy keys are rejected with a 400 there because they cannot list the team.
- **Writes are RPC-style POSTs** (`/projects/{id}/delete`, `/deployments/{name}/create_deploy_key`, `/update_environment_variables`…); only project and deployment updates are `PATCH`. Errors are `{code, message}`; `ConvexApiError` keeps both and the status.
- **Pagination**: `{items, pagination: {hasMore, nextCursor}}` with `cursor`/`limit` (max 100). Deploy keys list is a bare array; preview keys are `{items}` and need `includeManaged=true` to show integration-managed ones (Vercel).
- **Deployments** come from `GET /teams/{id}/list_deployments` (one paged call for the whole team); `kind: "local"` entries are skipped. `deploymentUrl` can carry a regional host (`*.eu-west-1.convex.cloud`), so always use it for Deployment API calls rather than building `{name}.convex.cloud`. HTTP actions live on the matching `.convex.site` host; `get_canonical_urls` gives the real pair (custom canonical URLs).
- **No paused flag anywhere** in either API: lifecycle declares pause/unpause without a status field.
- **Env vars**: `list_environment_variables` returns values in plaintext (docs warn secrets may be omitted in future); `update_environment_variables` with `value: null` deletes. Default env vars are per (name, deploymentType) pairs; external id `{projectId}/{type}/{name}`.
- **Deploy keys** are returned only by the create call; list gives id/name/lastUsed/allowedActions. Delete takes the key's _name_ (or secret) as `id`, not the numeric id.
- **Usage**: `get_current_usage` (beta) gives current day and month per metric with a unit and a `seedStatus`; it feeds point-in-time metrics. Enabled `list_usage_limits` entries become quotas (both halves from Convex). Usage limit update replaces the whole config.
- **Log streams**: discriminated by `logStreamType` (datadog, webhook, axiom, sentry, postHogLogs, postHogErrorTracking, s3Export). Create returns `hmacSecret` for webhooks; `get_log_stream` returns it later too. S3 export create (needs AWS keys and a table selection) is deliberately not offered.
- **No billing API** (only usage), no official Terraform provider (registry has no convex namespace), no log retrieval API (the CLI's log tail is not public), and no deployment transfer UI (needs a destination prompt `invokeAction` cannot carry).
- **Status feed**: Statuspage at `status.convex.dev`; components are plan tiers (Free & Starter / Professional / Business) duplicated under "Live Traffic" and "Development Services", so everything is provider-wide except AI Gateway; the website component is ignored.

### Railway (`@infrawrench/plugin-railway`)

- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (account or workspace token) against the GraphQL endpoint `https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2`. Project tokens (`Project-Access-Token` header, one environment) are not supported. Introspection is open without auth; every document in `queries.ts` was validated against it (2026-10) with graphql-js `validate`.
- Workspace discovery is `apiToken { workspaces { id name } }`, which works for both account and workspace tokens (`me` fails for workspace tokens). Optional `workspaceId` credential is a provider-options picker over it.
- GraphQL failures arrive as HTTP 200 + `errors[]`; `statusForGraphQLError` maps "Not Authorized" → 403, "not found" → 404, auth → 401, else 400, and HTTP 429 keeps its status (retried once on a short `Retry-After`).
- Rate limits are per hour by plan: Free 100, Hobby 1,000 (10 rps), Pro 10,000 (50 rps). Manifest `rateLimit` 20 / 0.25 per s. Inventory is one `project(id)` tree query per project (environments → serviceInstances with domains + latestDeployment, volumeInstances), cached 60 s; deployments (10 per instance), variables and TCP proxies are per service instance.
- 10 types: `workspace`, `project`, `environment` (child of project), `service` (a service **instance**, externalId `{environmentId}/{serviceId}`, child of environment, `showInSidebar`), `deployment` (externalId = deployment id), `variable` (`{env}/{service}/{key}`), `shared-variable` (`{env}/{key}`, child of environment), `volume` (`{env}/{volumeId}`, stores `volumeInstanceId` for backups), `domain` (`railway/{id}` or `custom/{id}`), `tcp-proxy`.
- Variables: `variables(projectId, environmentId, serviceId?, unrendered: true)` returns a JSON map with values; only keys are stored, values resolve on demand. `serviceId: null` gives shared variables. `variableUpsert` / `variableDelete`.
- Service settings: `serviceInstanceUpdate` (ServiceInstanceUpdateInput: build/start/preDeploy (array)/region/numReplicas/sleepApplication/restartPolicy/source…), name via `serviceUpdate`, CPU/memory via `serviceInstanceLimitsUpdate {vCPUs, memoryGB}`; `serviceInstanceLimits` is an untyped JSON scalar, shown flattened only. `serviceDelete(id, environmentId)` removes the service from that environment.
- Actions: `serviceInstanceDeploy(latestCommit|commitSha)`, `serviceInstanceRedeploy`, `deploymentRestart/Stop/Rollback/Redeploy/Cancel/Approve/Remove`, volume backups (`volumeInstanceBackupCreate/Restore/ScheduleUpdate` with DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY), volume remount via `volumeInstanceUpdate {serviceId}` (drag-to-attach), `customDomainIssueCertificate`.
- `tcpProxyCreate` is deprecated ("use staged changes"; a proxy made with it needs a redeploy), but staged environment patches are an untyped JSON config; the plugin calls `tcpProxyCreate` then `serviceInstanceRedeploy`.
- Costs (`estimated: true`): Railway meters but never prices usage. `usage(workspaceId, measurements, groupBy: [PROJECT_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, SERVICE_ID], startDate, endDate, includeDeleted)` one call per workspace per day. Values are minute-integrated; rates and conversion match the official CLI (`railwayapp/cli` src/commands/usage.rs): CPU vCPU-min × 20/43,200, memory GB-min × 10/43,200, NETWORK_TX_GB × 0.05, DISK/BACKUP GB-min × 0.15/43,200. `maxHistoryDays: 60` to stay inside hourly limits. `estimatedUsage` × the same rates is the projected bill on the workspace detail.
- Billing: `workspace(workspaceId).customer { creditBalance currentUsage billingPeriod usageLimit {softLimit hardLimit isOverLimit} }` (dollars). Credits = `creditBalance`; quota = `currentUsage` vs `hardLimit` (only when a hard limit is set). Workspace edit sets them via `usageLimitSet {customerId, softLimitDollars, hardLimitDollars}` / `usageLimitRemove`. Needs a workspace admin.
- Metrics: `metrics(environmentId, serviceId|volumeId, startDate, endDate, measurements, sampleRateSeconds)` samples `{ts (epoch s), value}`; HTTP via `httpMetrics` / `httpDurationMetrics` (p50/p95/p99) only for instances with a domain.
- Logs: `deploymentLogs`, `buildLogs`, `httpLogs` by deployment id (`limit`), a service uses its latest deployment.
- Status: status.railway.com is Railway's own app, not Statuspage; `GET /api/status` (public JSON: `activeIncidents`, `recentIncidents`, `maintenances`, components carry `groupName` + `impact`). Region groups map to `us-west2`, `us-east4-eqdc4a`, `europe-west4-drams3a`, `asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`; incident URL `/incident/{slug}`. Authentication and Payments & Billing are ignored; Railway/API and Dashboard are provider-wide.
- Not done: Terraform export (no official provider, only community ones), project tokens, buckets, functions, sandboxes, cloud agents, templates, egress gateways, private networking endpoints, invoices (`customer.invoices` exists but would duplicate the usage estimate as period-native rows).

### GitLab (`@infrawrench/plugin-gitlab`)

Verified against `doc/api/*.md` on gitlab-org/gitlab master, the GraphQL reference and `gitlab-org/terraform-provider-gitlab` docs (2026-10). Things the code does not make obvious:

- **Auth and host.** `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header for REST, Bearer for `/api/graphql`; personal, group and project access tokens all work. `url` accepts a bare host, a trailing `/api/v4` or a sub-path install, and refuses userinfo in the URL; `validateServerCredentials` requires https on the cloud host. Preflight reads `GET /personal_access_tokens/self` scopes: `read_api`/`api` for inventory, `api` for changes, `create_runner` for `POST /user/runners` (the runner docs name `manage_runner`/`create_runner` explicitly; whether `api` alone suffices is reported as unknown, not guessed).
- **Scope**: the optional `group` credential (picker from `GET /groups?min_access_level=10`) limits the account to `GET /groups/:id/projects?include_subgroups=true` plus `descendant_groups`; empty means `GET /projects?membership=true`. Projects are read 500 at most, most recently active first, and child types fan out over the 100 most recent non-archived ones only (`FANOUT_LIMIT`), skipping projects whose feature is disabled (`builds_access_level`, `environments_access_level`, `container_registry_access_level`, `packages_enabled`) and asking Maintainer-only endpoints (variables, hooks, deploy keys/tokens) only where `permissions` says >= 40. A 403/404 from one project skips it.
- **Pagination**: offset `page`/`per_page` (max 100) following `X-Next-Page` (empty on the last page). `X-Total` is omitted above 10,000 rows, so the open-MR count (`merge_requests?state=opened&per_page=1`) reads as unknown, never zero, past that. Host HTTP header names are lower-cased before reading.
- **External ids** are `<projectId|groupId>/<child>`; variables are `<owner>/<KEY>/<environment scope>` because two variables may share a key across scopes and scopes contain slashes (`review/*`). Every variable call passes `filter[environment_scope]`.
- **Variable PUT requires `value`**, so an edit that only flips flags re-reads the current value; a masked-and-hidden variable returns `value: null` and the edit then demands a new value. Values are never written to fields.
- **Protected branch levels can only be changed through PATCH on Premium** (`allowed_to_push` with `access_level` is Premium-only), so a level change unprotects and re-protects with `push_access_level`/`merge_access_level`, carrying force push and code owner approval over. PATCH is used for those two flags alone.
- **Tokens shown once**: deploy tokens and `POST /user/runners` return the token once; it is stashed with `services.secrets.setPlaintext(resourceId, "token")` and served by `resolveOutput("token")`. `POST /runners/:id/reset_authentication_token` backs Get credentials and re-stashes. Without a secret store, create returns a `token-not-kept` warning.
- **Runner list omits tags, version and last contact**: each runner (up to 100) is re-read with `GET /runners/:id`. Group accounts list `group_type` runners per group and `project_type` per fan-out project; instance runners are excluded (on GitLab.com they are GitLab's fleet). `version`/`platform` on the runner are deprecated in REST in favour of GraphQL runner managers, read while present.
- **Metrics** are bucketed client-side: pipelines (`created_after`/`created_before`), jobs (newest first until older than the window, 10 pages), runner jobs (`order_by=id&sort=desc`), deployments per environment (`updated_after`). Queue time is `queued_duration`. Group compute minutes per month come from GraphQL `ciMinutesUsage(namespaceId: "gid://gitlab/Group/<id>")`.
- **Quotas**: compute minutes only when `GET /namespaces/:id` returns `shared_runners_minutes_limit` (instance administrators only; `ci_minutes_usage.total_minutes_used` is visible to owners), storage only when GraphQL `group.storageSizeLimit` > 0 (namespace storage enforcement). Never a documented default.
- **Logs**: each pipeline job is a Logs-tab container; `GET /projects/:id/jobs/:job_id/trace` returns the whole log, stripped of ANSI and `section_start/section_end` markers and tailed locally.
- **Status feed**: status.gitlab.com is status.io page `5b36dc6502d06804c08349f7`; polled at `api.status.io/1.0/status/<id>`. Components map to services and resource types (`CI/CD - …` collapses to CI/CD); API and Website are provider-wide; degraded components without an incident are synthesised. It only describes GitLab.com.
- **Terraform**: `gitlabhq/gitlab ~> 19.4` (GitLab-maintained). Branch protection levels are `no one`/`developer`/`maintainer`/`admin`; schedule `ref` must be a full ref, so short refs are emitted as `refs/heads/…` with a comment; variable values and deploy-key public keys become variables. Runners, pipelines, packages and registries are not exported.
- **Not done**: cost (GitLab has no spend API; seats and minutes are on the group instead), jobs as their own type (they live in the pipeline view and Logs tab), DORA metrics (Ultimate-only endpoint), project/group access tokens, issues and merge requests beyond counts. Self-managed hosts cannot be bastion-routed (allowlist is `gitlab.com`).

### Civo (`@infrawrench/plugin-civo`)

- Auth: account API key as `Authorization: bearer <key>` against `https://api.civo.com/v2` (created under Profile, Security, API Keys; full access, no scopes). Verified against `civo/civogo` (2026-08-31) and `terraform-provider-civo` docs (2026-09). Errors are `{code, reason}`; `CivoApiError.status` keeps the HTTP code.
- Almost everything is **regional**: civogo sends `region` as a query parameter on every request and also in POST/PUT bodies; `api.send()` does both. Listers fan out across `GET /v2/regions` (filtered by `features.iaas/kubernetes/dbaas/loadbalancer/object_store/volume`) four at a time and skip a failing region.
