Pure maths in `server-core/src/cost/anomaly-detect.ts` (`detectSpike`: mean + 3σ over the trailing 28 days, ≥$10 absolute rise, ≥7 observed days — unit-tested, no I/O); the evaluator `cost/anomaly-eval.ts` `detectCostAnomaliesForOrg` runs from `poller/src/cost-poll.ts` right after `evaluateBudgetsForOrg`, and re-judges a 3-day trailing window ending **yesterday** (today is always partial and reads as a dip) per provider and per service via two grouped `queryCosts` calls, per currency. Evaluating only yesterday was a bug: providers restate late and an org's accounts collect at jittered times, so a day judged once and early can be missing most of its data and would never be reconsidered. Because the read for the oldest day already covers the newest, the wider window is one query, not three. Called per account, so it self-rate-limits per org via an in-process map (`MIN_EVAL_INTERVAL_MS`, 1h) — the ClickHouse reads are the expensive half and row dedup does nothing for them; correctness never depends on the gate. Dedup is two-layer: `cost_anomalies` unique (org, day, dimension, dimensionKey, currency) + `onConflictDoUpdate` refreshing the amounts (a restated day gets the corrected figure) with `notifiedAt` left alone — RETURNING `notifiedAt` is what says whether to alert, so an anomaly stored while no transport was connected, or one whose delivery failed, is retried by a later pass instead of being lost (migration `0051`). Then a 7-day per-key cooldown counting **only notified** rows: counting stored ones would let a suppressed day extend its own silence into an unbounded rolling quiet period, and would let an anomaly nobody received suppress the alert that would have told them. Noise floor (`minDeltaAbs`) is USD-denominated and converted per series by `optionsForCurrency` — a flat 10 units is ~$0.07 in JPY, which would page on nothing. Fan-out through the existing transports under a NEW `PushTrigger` `"anomalyAlerts"` — which means an `anomaly_alerts` boolean on `push_preferences`, `slack_channels`, AND `msteams_webhooks`, plus the trigger-column maps in `push/dispatch.ts`, `slack.ts`, `msteams.ts` (adding a trigger touches all six). Twilio paging for anomalies is **opt-in and batched** — see the anomaly-SMS entry below. Push payload `type: "cost_anomaly"` routes mobile to `/org/:orgId/costs`. Read side: `GET /api/org/:orgId/costs/anomalies?days=` (`costs:read`, web `services/cost-anomalies.ts`, `API_VERSION` → 0.24.0); `CostAnomaly` contract in `client-core/src/costs.ts`; `ui/src/cost/CostAnomaliesSection.tsx` renders on `CostsPanel` for web+desktop, gated on the host wiring the optional `CostsClient.listAnomalies` (desktop: `cloud_costs_anomalies` IPC). Toggles live wherever budget toggles live: web paging settings (`ALERT_TRIGGERS`), mobile notifications screen. CLI: `infrawrench costs --anomalies` (`desktop/electron/cli/commands/costs.ts` `cmdCostAnomalies`) — a flag on `costs` rather than its own command, since it asks about the same data; window from `--days <n>` or `--last 2w` via `resolveDayWindow` in `cli/args.ts`, bounded 1–90 client-side so a typo fails before the round trip. Mobile renders the list too (`mobile/src/features/costs/CostAnomaliesSection.tsx` + `useCostAnomalies.ts`), as a section of the Costs tab under the chart and budgets — the same order as `CostsPanel`, and the reason the `cost_anomaly` push's existing `/org/:orgId/costs` deep link now lands on something that contains the anomaly it is about. The fetch is `listCostAnomalies` in `client-core/src/costs.ts` (unwraps the `{ anomalies }` envelope, clamps `days` to 1–90 client-side like the CLI does), not a hand-rolled `api.org` call in the screen.

**Cost anomaly tuning + new-spend-source detection** (follow-ups to the above). Two knobs the detector used to hardcode are now per-org in `org_cost_anomaly_settings` (migration `0052`), a one-row-per-org table modelled on `org_digest_settings` — **no row means the shipped defaults**, so every org that predates the table keeps working: `sigmas` (`double precision`, default 3), `min_delta_cents` (1000), `new_source_min_cents` (2500). `server-core/src/cost/anomaly-settings.ts` owns get/set plus `anomalyOptionsFor` (cents → currency units) and `normalizeAnomalySettings` (clamps a hand-written row); `minBaselineDays` stays fixed — it is a statement about how much history a baseline needs, not a preference. `anomaly-detect.ts` stays pure: `detectCostAnomaliesForOrg` reads the settings once per pass and threads them in, and its `options` argument still wins for tests. Bounds are enforced in Zod (`costAnomalySettingsSchema` in `ui/src/cost/config.ts`, asserted `Exact` against the `CostAnomalySettings` type like the budget schema): sigmas 1–10 (0 alerts on every fluctuation, <1σ flags a third of ordinary days, >10 fires on nothing), both floors 100–10,000,000 cents ($1–$100k; the cap catches "I typed dollars into a cents field"), sigmas rounded to 1dp to match the form's step. `GET /costs/anomaly-settings` is `costs:read`; `PUT` is **`costs:write`** — matching `POST /costs/rows`, the other mutating cost route, not `budgets:write`, since it changes what the whole cost feed alerts on. New-spend-source detection is `detectNewSpendSource` in the same pure module: a key whose spend across the **entire** 28-day window is under `minNewSourceAbs` (not `=== 0` — real bills are full of sub-cent trial usage, and stating it relative to the floor scales with currency) and whose day clears that floor. It exists because a $0 → $5,000 key clears no sigma bar at all (mean and stddev are both 0) and the ≥7-observed-day guard silences it besides. On this half `minBaselineDays` means **collection coverage, not array length** — a distinction the first cut got wrong and which cost nothing to ship silently: `detectForDimension` zero-fills every baseline to a dense 28 entries via `fillDailySeries`, so the `baseline.length < minBaselineDays` guard it shipped with could never fire, and the day an org first collected, every provider and every service read as a new source and was pushed/Slacked/Teams'd at once. The fact cannot be recovered from the array — zero-filling makes "we collected and it spent $0" and "we hold no data for that day" the same `0` — and counting non-zero days the way `detectSpike` legitimately does would be worse, since a real new source is all-zero by definition and the detector would never fire again. So it is passed in and the module stays pure: `detectNewSpendSource(baseline, actual, baselineCoverageDays, options)`, where `baselineCoverageDays` is whole days (`dates.daysBetween`) from the org's earliest cost day to the day being judged. The evaluator gets that day from `getCostCoverage` (min over its per-account rows) — one extra ClickHouse read per org per pass, read once and shared by both dimensions, and a failure of it degrades to spikes-only rather than aborting the pass. Deriving it from the window `detectForDimension` already fetches would be free but wrong: that window reaches back only 31 days, so an org that spent nothing for a month and then started again would look brand new and have a genuine new source suppressed. Deliberately **per-org, not per-key**: a key first appearing yesterday inside an established org _is_ the finding, and only an org's own first days of collection go quiet. Represented as a `kind` discriminator on `cost_anomalies` (`'spike' | 'new_source'`, DEFAULT `'spike'` so existing rows keep their meaning) rather than a parallel table, so the dedup unique index, the 7-day cooldown, the list endpoint, the UI and the Slack/Teams/push fan-out all come for free; `kind` is deliberately **not** in the unique index — the two detections are mutually exclusive per (day, key) and `judgeDay` runs spike-first, so including it could only produce two rows for one day. Alert copy branches on kind ("New spend source: X … with no spend at all in the prior 28 days"). A $0 baseline has no percentage: `deltaPercent` (ui) and `anomalyDeltaPercent` (CLI, now takes `kind`) both return null for `new_source` **whatever the baseline rounded to** — a near-zero window rounds to a cent and would print a six-figure percentage. UI: `CostAnomaliesSection` gained a "New source" badge, `none` for the baseline, and a `Tune detection` panel gated on the optional `CostsClient.getAnomalySettings` / `updateAnomalySettings` (read-only when the update half is absent, same rule as the budget half). Desktop gets the editor too via `cloud_costs_anomaly_settings` / `cloud_costs_update_anomaly_settings` IPC. **Mobile deliberately does not** — it lists anomalies and says the thresholds are tuned from web or desktop. It is org-wide policy behind `costs:write` that decides what the whole cost feed alerts on, set once and rarely revisited, and the knob someone reaches for on a phone ("stop paging me") is the per-user push toggle the notifications screen already has. Same line as the custom-graph script editor and the secret-reroll wizard. The one thing that _is_ shared is the percentage rule: `costAnomalyDeltaPercent` moved into `client-core/src/costs.ts` and `CostAnomaliesSection` (web/desktop) plus mobile both call it, so "a `new_source` never prints a percentage, whatever its baseline rounded to" is stated once. The CLI's `anomalyDeltaPercent` stays a copy on purpose: `cli/format.ts` is CJS and pure by design so `electron/__tests__/cli-format.test.ts` can import it without dragging Electron in, and client-core resolves to ESM there (see the dynamic-import note in the CLI section). API surface changed (2 new routes + a new `CostAnomaly.kind` field) — `API_VERSION` bump is owned by a later centralized step.

**Cost anomaly SMS paging** (follow-up; migration `0056`). Anomalies can now text the org's Twilio recipients, and the whole design is about _not_ being one text per anomaly. A pass detects per dimension (`provider` **and** `service`) per key per currency, so the day one account jumps yields a provider anomaly plus one per service under it — all new, all past the 7-day per-key cooldown, all in the same loop. So `cost/anomaly-eval.ts` **collects** what it alerted on into `paged[]` and calls `pageAboutAnomalies` **once, after both dimension loops**; `cost/anomaly-sms.ts` owns the batching, rendering and claim (split from the evaluator the way `drift/summary.ts` is split from `drift/alerts.ts`, and pure-tested the same way). Two bounds, because batching bounds a _pass_ and not a _day_: the pass itself is hourly per org (`MIN_EVAL_INTERVAL_MS`) and the per-key cooldown only silences the _same_ key, so a trickle of different keys crossing the bar as restated data lands would still text 24×/day — hence a **page-level cooldown of 6h per org**, claimed with one conditional UPDATE on `org_cost_anomaly_settings.sms_last_paged_at` (`sms_alerts <> 'off' AND (sms_last_paged_at IS NULL OR <= cutoff)`), the `org_drift_alert_settings.last_notified_at` protocol reused so N replicas produce one text, and **released when the text reached nobody** so an outage does not buy six hours of silence. It is an UPDATE, not drift's upsert: reaching the claim at all means a saved row said `sms_alerts <> 'off'`, so there is nothing to insert — and re-reading the opt-in _inside_ the claiming statement makes an org that turned it off mid-pass silent immediately. A suppressed text loses nothing (the anomalies are stored, listed, and already fanned out over push/Slack/Teams) — SMS is the interrupt, not the record. **Body** (`formatAnomalySmsBody`, pure): built to fit rather than trimmed to fit — the header and the `; and N more` tail are budgeted _before_ items are appended and items only go in while the whole string stays ≤ 320, which is the cap `sendOneShotPage` truncates at; that truncation cuts mid-word and would eat the overflow count, the one part that says the list is partial. `MAX_LISTED_ANOMALIES` = 3 named, keys shortened at 28 chars, spikes render `key $actual vs $mean/day` and new sources `new <dimension> key $actual`, day is a single ISO day or a `min–max` span since a pass judges three. **Opt-in** is `sms_alerts` on the existing `org_cost_anomaly_settings` (no new table), a **three-valued enum `off` (default) | `new_source` | `all`**, not a boolean and not two booleans: the values nest (off ⊂ new sources ⊂ everything) so no combination ever needs two texts out of one pass, and the middle value is the one worth having — a source appearing from nothing is what a leaked key looks like, a spike on an existing line is usually a busy day. Default off because every org that already configured Twilio for budgets would otherwise gain a new pager on deploy; `normalizeAnomalySettings` **fails closed** on an unrecognised stored value. **No voice** (budget precedent: `sendOneShotPage` leaves voice off unless a caller asks). **Stamping** is the subtle part: the loop stamps `notifiedAt` when push/Slack/Teams delivered, and the batched text stamps whatever it carried that nobody else delivered — otherwise an org whose _only_ transport is Twilio would re-alert every pass and never start the 7-day per-key cooldown (which counts only notified rows). API: `smsAlerts` is a required 4th field on `PUT /costs/anomaly-settings` — deliberately no server-side default, so an older client that omits it is rejected rather than silently switching a deliberate opt-in back off (a breaking request-shape change; the `API_VERSION` bump is the centralized step's) — and both settings responses carry a derived read-only `smsConfigured` (`CostAnomalySettingsView`), computed by `twilio-pager.isSmsPagingConfigured` (enabled + creds + from-number + ≥1 SMS recipient, no decryption) because the Twilio routes that hold that fact are `org:settings:write` and a `costs:read` member cannot ask them. Without it the form would accept "text everyone" and deliver nothing; `CostAnomaliesSection`'s tuning panel shows the warning instead, and strips `smsConfigured` from the PUT body since the schema is strict. **Mobile still omits the editor** (org-wide `costs:write` policy, same line as the thresholds) and its notifications screen deliberately gains nothing: that screen is per-device push plus the Slack/Teams routing, and has never carried the org's Twilio card at all — the anomalies section's footnote just now also names the SMS opt-in as web/desktop-tuned.

**Cost anomaly root-cause hints** (follow-up). When an anomaly fires, the evaluator attaches up to 3 human-readable hints from what the platform already indexes for the same window: the change timeline (`resource_changes`, aggregated by kind+type — "12 gce-instance resources appeared") and the audit log (allowlisted spend-plausible actions with actor names — "Astrid ran workflow \"Nightly rebuild\"", "a change freeze lifted"). `server-core/src/cost/anomaly-hints.ts` follows the detect/eval split: `composeAnomalyHints` (ranking + phrasing, pure, `__tests__/anomaly-hints.test.ts`) vs `buildAnomalyHints` (the queries; **never throws** — hints are garnish on an alert that must go out, and the evaluator guards its call anyway). Window is `[day-1T00Z, day+1T00Z)` — the anomalous day plus the day before; wider starts explaining the baseline. Both queries range-scan existing `(organization_id, created_at)` indexes, **no new indexes**; provider-dimension anomalies additionally filter `resource_changes.plugin_id`, service anomalies read org-wide (a service name maps to no plugin generically). Ranking: created > freeze-lifted > workflow-run > deployment > deleted > in-app creates > updated; audit rows group by (action, actor, entity) so ten identical runs are one hint with a count; `workflow.run` logs only the workflow id, so names are resolved in one `workflows` read; API-key actors read "an API key". Hints are computed in the notify loop **before the cooldown check** (suppressed rows still render in the list) and stored on the row — `cost_anomalies.hints` jsonb, null for pre-hint rows — so clients never re-run the window queries. Delivery: Slack/Teams bodies get the full `\n\nAround then: a; b; c.` suffix, push gets only the top hint (lock-screen budget), **SMS gets none** (its 320-char budget is spent naming anomalies — asserted in the eval suite). Read side: `hints` on `CostAnomaly` (`GET /costs/anomalies`; always an array server-side, `?? []` over old rows) but **optional** in `client-core`'s interface so a desktop/mobile build a release ahead of its server renders rather than crashes; rendered as faint sub-lines in `ui` `CostAnomaliesSection` (web+desktop) and mobile's `AnomalyRow`; CLI `costs --anomalies --json` carries it for free (text table unchanged — hints don't fit a row). In `anomaly-eval.test.ts` the hints module is mocked at the boundary (the fake db only speaks the evaluator's own query shapes).

**Frontend** — shared components in `@infrawrench/ui/cost` (React) + React-free `@infrawrench/ui/cost/config` (zod config schemas + `resolveCostDateRange`; own tsdown entry so the server API can import it without UI code). `ui/src/cost/`: `config.ts`, `transform.ts` (pure pivot/fold/comparison-align/forecast-splice — unit-tested), `CostGraphCard` (recharts ComposedChart: stacked/multi bar, line, stacked area, pie; forecast = dashed line keyed `__forecast__`, comparison = muted dashed `__previous__` totals line; "Other" always gray `#6b7280`; per-currency series with mixed-currency notice), `CostGraphConfigModal` + `CostFilterRows` (shared with budgets), `BudgetCard` (progress bar, threshold ticks, forecast marker, alert badge), `BudgetConfigModal`. Web `DashboardView`: "+" tile is now an `AddMenu` popover (Pin resource / Cost graph / Budget); `costApi` wraps `apiFetch`. Desktop: cloud-mode only (`activeCloudOrgId`); IPC handlers in `electron/cloud-data/costs.ts` (+ preload whitelist), renderer wrappers `src/lib/cloud-costs.ts`, same shared components; local mode never shows cost entries. Budget widget config = `{version, budgetId}` — the budget row outlives the widget.

**Provider integrations** — each plugin's `src/cost-data.ts`: AWS (Cost Explorer `GetCostAndUsage`, service+region daily, needs `ce:GetCostAndUsage` IAM, us-east-1 signing, $0.01/request). Wave 2+: Vercel (FOCUS `/v1/billing/charges`), DigitalOcean, Azure (Cost Mgmt Query API), ClickHouse Cloud (usageCost, CHC=list-$), Atlas/PlanetScale/Scaleway/OVH (invoice/consumption, periodNative), Databricks (system.billing × list_prices via SQL warehouse, list-$), Neon (consumption units × published rates), Turso (org invoices), Cloudflare (PayGo usage API — **v1 alpha**), GCP (BigQuery billing export; optional `billingExportTable` credential field, `CostSetupError` with a console deep link until configured). No API: Fly, Hetzner, Netlify, Cloudinary ($-underivable), protocol plugins.

**Mobile renders the same widgets, not a pointer to the web app.** The Dashboards tab (`org/[orgId]/index.tsx`, labelled "Home" until it became a list) is `GET /dashboards` — every dashboard, default first — and opening one pushes `dashboard/[dashboardId]`, where `mobile/src/features/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx` renders resource pins, workflow pins, cost graphs, and budgets in `orderDashboardCards` order. That screen is a hidden tab (`href: null`), so it has no back affordance of its own: the layout draws a `headerLeft` chevron back to `/org/:orgId`, and the screen `setOptions({title})` once the fetch lands, since the title is data the layout can't know. There is no standing "Budgets" section anywhere, because a budget belongs to the dashboard it was created on — which is why `budget_breach` pushes route to **`/org/:orgId/costs`** (`pushDataToPath`) rather than the dashboard list: the Costs tab lists every budget in the org, so an alert always opens something that contains the budget it is about. Its earlier standalone version also read `status.actualCents`, a shape `GET /budgets` never returned (actual/forecast/month are top-level), so every budget rendered at $0: that class of drift is why the contract now lives in client-core rather than being re-declared per screen.

**Mobile authors dashboards too, over the same endpoints.** `New dashboard` on the list (`POST /dashboards`, then straight into the empty one — the only reason to make it is to put something on it) and an `Edit` toggle on the dashboard screen that turns `DashboardBody` editable via one optional `editing: DashboardEditing | null` prop. Everything it writes is an endpoint web already had (`/dashboards/pin`, `/unpin`, `/workflow-unpin`, `/widgets` POST/PATCH/DELETE, `/:id/reorder`, `/:id/rename`, `DELETE /:id`, `/budgets` POST/PUT) — **no server surface was added and no `API_VERSION` bump was needed**, which is the bar for mirroring a cloud feature onto mobile. `useDashboardEditing.ts` holds every mutation: failures `Alert` once and re-throw so a sheet can also show them inline, and a reorder writes the new `gridX` into the cached `DashboardData` (`cardOrderIndex`) _before_ the request — the Move up/Move down buttons replace drag-and-drop, and a card that only moves after a round trip reads as a dropped tap. Three deliberate gaps against web: no drag (arrows instead), no custom absolute date range in the graph editor (two date pickers don't fit a sheet; a config that already has one is shown and preserved), and no zod validation client-side — the schemas live in `@infrawrench/ui`, which mobile can't import, so the editors are valid by construction over the client-core enums and the API is the validator.

The sheets are `mobile/src/features/dashboard/{AddCard,CostGraph,Budget,BudgetPicker,PinResource}Sheet.tsx` over `mobile/src/components/form.tsx` (`Sheet`, `TextField`, `ChipSelect`, `ChipMultiSelect`, `ToggleChip`, `BareInput`) — **chips, not dropdowns**: a phone select is itself a modal, and nesting one inside a sheet that is already one is where native pickers go wrong. `CostFilterEditor.tsx` is the native `CostFilterRows`, over the same `GET /costs/dimensions`. What moved to client-core for this (the "second host moves it" rule): `BudgetInput`, `CostDimensionOption`, `DEFAULT_COST_GRAPH_CONFIG`, `DEFAULT_BUDGET_INPUT`, and the four label maps; `ui/src/cost/config.ts` re-exports each at its old name and now also asserts `Exact<z.infer<typeof budgetInputSchema>, BudgetInput>`, so the schema can't drift from the interface mobile builds against.

`mobile/src/features/dashboard/CostChart.tsx` draws all five chart types with `react-native-svg` — recharts is DOM-only. It shares binning, axis (`niceAxis`), and formatting with web through client-core, so a bar lands on the same tick. Two deliberate differences: a phone has no hover, so the tooltip layer is replaced by a legend carrying each series' period total (which also supplies the secondary encoding the two closest hues in our categorical order need), and only the first and last bucket are labelled on the x axis — interior labels collide at phone width. The series colours are **shared, not copied** — `client-core/src/chart-colors.ts` owns them and both `chart-theme.ts` and `mobile/.../chart-primitives.tsx` read `SERIES_COLORS` from it: colour follows the entity across surfaces. `SERIES_COLORS` is a categorical rotation, so **no slot in it carries a meaning**; the overlays are named constants (`FORECAST_COLOR`, `SCENARIO_COLOR`, `OTHER_SERIES_COLOR`) for exactly that reason. Writing an overlay as `colors[3]` both collides with whichever series holds that slot and silently changes hue if the rotation is reordered — which is how the web scenario projection came to be drawn in the palette's red while the caption naming it was amber, and why `x[3] ?? "#f59e0b"` never caught it (a fallback cannot fire against a populated slot). `SCENARIO_COLOR` is `#fbbf24` because that is what `--color-warning` resolves to in the dark theme, i.e. the caption's own colour.

Docs: `website/src/content/docs/features/cloud-costs.md` (+ dashboard.md "+"-menu update, roles doc, per-plugin pages).

### Cost estimates (forward-looking, all four surfaces)

`fetchCostData` reports what a provider **has** billed; `PluginClient.estimateCost(typeId, fields)` answers what a configuration **would** cost per month. It replaced `getCreateCostEstimate`, which returned a bare `number | null` and could therefore only ever be a badge — the shape is now `CostEstimate` (`plugin-base/src/cost.ts`): a `monthlyAmount` that is **always** the sum of its `lineItems`, a `currency`, an optional `partial` flag and `notes`. Build one with `buildCostEstimate(lineItems, opts)` rather than by hand: it drops unpriced/zero components, rounds each line to cents _before_ summing (so the displayed lines add up to the displayed total), sorts largest-first, and returns `null` when nothing priced.

**`null` is not `$0`.** "We can't price this" and "this is free" are different answers and the whole capability exists to keep them apart — a `$0` quote for an unknown SKU is exactly the failure the old static AWS table produced. Same rule at every layer: `buildCostEstimate` returns null rather than an empty estimate, the API returns `estimate: null`, and no host renders a chip. When only _part_ of a resource can be priced, quote that part and set `partial` — hosts then say "at least $X/mo".

**Field keys are the create form's.** That is the one spelling every caller can produce, and it is what the form has in hand mid-typing. Hosts pricing an _existing_ resource pass its stored fields, so a plugin whose lister spells a key differently must accept both — `fields["size"] ?? fields["vmSize"]` on Azure, the same split `rightsizing.createSizeFieldKey` already names. AWS needed none: its listers already store `region`/`instanceType`/`sizeGb`/`volumeType`/`instanceClass`/`allocatedStorage`/`engine`/`multiAZ` under the create form's names.

**Implemented by four plugins** — aws, azure, gcp, digitalocean. All rates are live and per-region: AWS `pricing.ts` (Price List `GetProducts`, SigV4 against api.pricing.us-east-1, 6h cache per (service, region, dimensions) — which is what makes it safe to call on every keystroke), Azure Retail Prices, GCP Cloud Billing catalog, DO's published size prices. The static us-east-1 table that used to back AWS is gone; its `cost-estimate.ts` now takes credentials and fetches. Unverifiable filters fail **closed**: a `databaseEngine` string AWS spells differently matches no SKU, so the line drops and the estimate goes partial rather than falling through to another engine's rate.

**One route, three questions** — `POST /api/org/:orgId/resources/cost-estimate` (renamed from `create-cost-estimate`; response changed from a number to an object, hence the `API_VERSION` minor bump). `fields` prices a proposed create, `resourceId` prices an existing resource, **both** prices a proposed edit — `fields` is merged over the stored fields, so the caller sends only what changed. `server-core/src/cost/estimate.ts` owns that merge (`estimateResourceCost`) so the route and the digest can't drift; the web route only handles the peer-client case itself, because peer plumbing is web-only.

**Surfaces.** Create form: `useCreateResourceForm` debounces 220ms and the plugin's estimate _wins over_ the size-picker price (the picker can't see boot disks or node counts). Resource detail: a `costEstimate` prop on `DetailView` renders the same `CostEstimateChip` in the header, so the create-time quote and the after-the-fact one are one number. Edit modal: `EditResourceModal.loadCostEstimate` prices `{}` for the baseline and the changed keys for the projection, then `costEstimateDelta` → "This change adds $340/month" (null across currencies or with either side unpriced — an unknown end makes the delta unknown, not nil). Mobile: `features/costs/ResourceCostEstimateCard.tsx`, a card with the breakdown already open, because a phone header has no room for a disclosure. CLI: `infrawrench estimate <resource-id>` (`--json`), cloud-only. Weekly digest: a **Projected spend** line from `projectMonthlySpend`, deliberately separate from the spend totals — a cluster spun up last Sunday barely registers in last week's bill and is most of next month's.

Formatting lives in `client-core/src/cost-estimate.ts` and deliberately does **not** reuse `formatMoney` from `costs.ts`: that one drops cents above $10, which is right for reported spend and wrong here — a create form's figure has to visibly move when a disk slider adds $0.37/month.

`projectMonthlySpend` is the one part of the digest that talks to provider APIs, so it is bounded twice (250 resources, 12 accounts) and groups by account so each account's pricing cache is shared. It reports `unpricedCount` and `truncated` rather than hiding them, and the digest drops the line entirely when both sides are zero — "no change" would assert knowledge the estimates don't have.

### Price catalog (browse and compare list prices)

The estimate answers "what does _this_ configuration cost"; the catalog answers "what could I run and what would it cost", over the same price sources. **Contract** (`plugin-base/src/price-catalog.ts`): a manifest `priceCatalog` declaration (services with a product family, regions in preference order each with a coarse `area`, `source`, `refreshHours`, `regionScoped`, `requiresCredentials`, optional `permission`), Zod-validated, plus a fetch that lives where `requiresCredentials` says: **`Plugin.fetchPriceCatalog(request, services?)`** for a public source (Azure Retail Prices, Linode types, CoreWeave's static table), **`PluginClient.fetchPriceCatalog(request)`** for a credentialed one (AWS Price List + spot history, GCP Billing Catalog + machine types, DO sizes, Hetzner server types, Scaleway instance types, OCI shapes). `runPluginContractTests` checks the right half exists. Products carry specs (vCPU, memory, GPU count/model/memory, storage, arch) and prices (region, `rateType` on-demand/spot/reserved/savings-plan, `term`, `paymentOption`, unit hour/month/gb-month, currency, `effectiveDate`), plus an optional `estimate: {resourceTypeId, fields}` keyed the way the create form keys them (`{region}` substituted by the host). Plugins pass results through `normalizePriceCatalogProducts`. **Every figure is a published list price**: no invented rates, no scaling one region to another, absent rate types stay absent. Commitment prices are hourly equivalents (Azure reservations publish a whole-term total; AWS partial/all-upfront amortize the fee over the term), and OCI emits hourly even though its estimator uses 744-hour months, so every host compares on the same 730.

**Server** (`server-core/src/price-catalog/`): `createPriceCatalogService(deps)` with injected deps (`service.ts`, unit-tested without a database) and the wired singleton in `index.ts`. In-memory cache per (plugin, service, region), keyed additionally by org + account for credentialed catalogs (a result fetched with one org's credentials is never served to another org), TTL = `refreshHours`, stale-while-revalidate, failures remembered 5 minutes, a cold fetch waited on for 20 s then reported `loading` while it finishes in the background. Credentialed catalogs borrow the org's oldest live account on that plugin (falling back to the second). Provider state is always reported (`ready`/`no-account`/`no-region`/`loading`/`error`, `truncated`, last `error` over a stale list) so "not searched" never reads as "nothing matches". Search/compare/filter/sort/region choice are pure functions in `client-core/src/price-catalog.ts`, shared by the routes, MCP tools, CLI and UI; `normalizePriceCatalog{Search,Compare}Query` coerce a loose bag (query string or tool input) and `priceCatalogQueryString` is their inverse. Compare is spec-based only ("at least" each stated axis, GPUs excluded unless asked for), never name-based. Currency: rows keep their native currency; `comparable` is the monthly figure in the org's configured display currency at the org's own stated rate (one hop, `null` without a rate), else native, and `mixedCurrencies` says when sorting crossed currencies at face value.

**Surfaces.** Routes `GET /api/org/:orgId/price-catalog/{providers,search,compare}` (`resources:read`, authenticated and org-scoped on purpose even though the data is public: credentialed catalogs use the org's accounts). Workspace tab kind `price-catalog` (single-instance) through the whole chain, shared `ui/src/price-catalog/PriceCatalogPanel.tsx` (search with filters, compare, coverage notes, "Use in estimate"), `WebPriceCatalogPanel` / `DesktopPriceCatalogPanel` (cloud mode only; `cloud_price_catalog_search|compare` IPC serializes the query in main so the renderer can only reach those two routes). "Use in estimate" opens the host's own `CreateResourceModal` with the new `initialFields` prop (`CreateResourceCallbacks.initialFields`, merged over the config defaults once per load) and an account picker when the org has several accounts on the plugin. CLI `infrawrench prices search|compare` (`--json`). MCP/chat tools `list_price_catalog_providers`, `search_price_catalog`, `compare_instance_prices` (`resources:read`). **Deliberate omissions:** no mobile surface (a filter-heavy planning table, and the chat tools already reach it from the phone); no desktop local mode (no org accounts to borrow, no shared cache); OVH and the SaaS plugins publish no machine catalog the plugin reads, so they are absent rather than approximated; GCP machine types with attached accelerators and shared-core types are skipped (GPU SKUs are separate and fractional cores bill differently), and Azure memory is shown only where a verified size table has it.

### The Costs panel and budget lifecycle

`CostsPanel` (`ui/src/cost/CostsPanel.tsx`) is a workspace tab beside Agents and Workflows — target kind `costs`, sidebar entry, `/costs` route on both hosts, and a read-only `costs` tab on mobile. It shows month-to-date spend (a fixed `mtd` config with only a group-by choice; anything configurable belongs on a dashboard where it can be saved) over the org's budgets.

**A budget is an org object, not a dashboard object.** It evaluates and alerts whether or not any dashboard carries a card for it, and `dashboard_widgets` points at it by `config.budgetId` with no foreign key — so a budget can outlive every card. Before this panel the only way to reach one was to find a dashboard showing it, which meant removing a card made a still-firing budget unreachable. That is what the panel fixes, and why `BudgetWithStatus.placements` exists: each row names the dashboards showing it, or says "On no dashboard".

The two directions are deliberately asymmetric, and both hosts must keep it that way:

- Removing a **card** (`DELETE /dashboards/widgets/:id`) is a display change. The budget is untouched.
- Deleting a **budget** (`softDeleteBudget`) also soft-deletes every widget pointing at it. Nothing else ever would: a widget resolves its row by `config.budgetId`, so a card left behind renders as a permanent "budget unavailable" tile that no amount of dashboard editing explains.

The dashboard `+` menu offers **New budget** and **Existing budget** for the same reason — one budget, many views. Adding a placement from either side is the same plain widget POST; `BudgetPickerModal` is shared by web and desktop so the two cannot drift.

Desktop gates the sidebar entry on `activeCloudOrgId` (spend is collected server-side, so local mode has nothing to show) and `createDesktopCostsClient` resolves the org per call rather than closing over it, matching the dashboard's cost API. Mobile omits the mutating half of `CostsClient` and `CostsPanel` renders read-only rather than showing controls that would fail on click.

**There is exactly one `CostApi` factory per platform — `createWebCostApi` (`web/src/lib/cost-client.ts`) and `createDesktopCostApi` (`desktop/src/lib/cost-api.ts`) — and every cost surface spreads it.** Nearly all of `CostApi` is optional (`listScenarioModels?`, `listSavedFilters?`, `listBusinessMetrics?`, `listCostAnnotations?`), and the shared components render a picker **only when its loader is present**, so a host that hand-rolls a smaller literal typechecks fine and silently ships a graph editor with controls missing. That is exactly what happened: both `DashboardView`s built their own three-method object, so a cost graph opened from a dashboard had no scenario, saved-filter or unit-cost picker while the identical modal on the Reports page did (#115) — and desktop's `createDesktopCostReportsClient` had separately drifted to omit scenarios and unit costs. The Costs panel's and the Reports page's clients now extend the one factory instead of restating the reads, and `{web,desktop}` each carry a test asserting the three clients expose the same loaders _and_ that `DashboardView` builds from the factory. Desktop's `queryCosts`/`queryUnitCosts` are `async` on purpose: `requireCloudOrgId()` throws, and `CostGraphCard` queries from an effect with a `.catch()` and no `try`, where a synchronous throw would escape.

### Costs panel tabs (`SectionTabs`)

The panel is split into in-page tabs: Overview, Alerts, Savings, Commitments & credits, Network, Carbon, Allocation. The ids are `COSTS_PANEL_TABS` in `client-core/src/costs-panel-tabs.ts`, shared by web, desktop and mobile; mobile's `pushDataToPath` appends `?tab=` so a push opens the tab holding the section it is about (budget → overview, change/efficiency alerts → alerts, savings/extended support → savings). Mobile has no Network tab.

These are **not workspace tabs**: they are view state inside one `costs` workspace tab, so nothing in the workspace-tab chain (ui.store kinds, `validate-tabs`, `TabTarget` enum) changes. `SectionTabs` (`ui/src/components/SectionTabs.tsx`) remembers the last tab per viewer in `localStorage` (try/catch, so blocked storage just forgets) and takes an `initialTab` that beats the remembered one. Panels mount on first open and stay mounted (hidden), so a page's dozen section fetches no longer all fire on load and a half-filled form survives a tab switch. A new Costs section goes into an existing tab; adding a tab id means updating `COSTS_PANEL_TABS`, both renderers and the docs table in `features/cloud-costs.md`. Settings > Notifications uses the same component (Channels, Routing, Alerts & digest). Reach for it when a page grows past a handful of stacked sections.

### Budget hierarchies, usage budgets and flexible periods (migration `0132`, API `1.57.0`)

A budget now answers three independent questions, each defaulted so every pre-existing row reads exactly as before: **what** it counts (`measure`: `cost` money in `currency` against `amount_cents`, or `usage`: the cost rows' `usage_amount` in one `usage_unit`, against `usage_amount`), **when** (`period` jsonb: null is the calendar month, `{kind:"recurring", unit, interval, startDate}` a custom cadence, `{kind:"explicit", periods:[{start,end,amountCents|usageAmount}]}` a list with an amount per period) and **where** it sits (`parent_budget_id`, FK-less like `saved_filter_id`).

- **One period resolver.** `client-core/src/budgets.ts` `resolveBudgetPeriod(period, today)` is the only code that decides which days a budget counts; the server evaluator and every card call it. Month-based cadences clamp from the original anchor (never chained), so a series starting on the 31st does not drift to the 28th. The period key (`BudgetPeriodWindow.key`) is what `budget_alert_events.month` now stores: **`YYYY-MM` for the calendar month** so existing alert history keeps deduping and nothing re-fires on deploy, the period's start day otherwise. Events gained `period_start`/`period_end` and `actual_usage`/`forecast_usage` (a usage event's cents columns are 0). No period covering today (a cadence not started, a gap in a list) means `periodStart: null`, no queries and no thresholds.
- **Cross-field rules live in `budgetInputError`** (client-core), not a zod refinement, because the MCP tools spread `budgetInputSchema.shape` and a `superRefine` would make that a `ZodEffects`. Route, tools, the web/desktop modal and the mobile sheet all run it. `amountCents` became `.default(0)` (a usage budget and an explicit list do not use it); the rule insists on a positive one where it is the limit. Usage budgets refuse `scenarioModelId` and `useAdjustedSpend`: both adjust money.
- **Rollup semantics: a parent is the sum of its children, measured over the parent's window.** `BudgetStatusResolver` (`server-core/src/cost/budget-eval.ts`) takes the org's whole budget list, memoizes per (budget, window), and sums children's `ScopeMeasurement`s (major units; cents happen once in `costFigures`). A yearly parent over monthly children re-measures each child over the year, which is why the memo key includes the window. A parent's own scope, scenario and billing-rule opt-in are set aside while it has children; each child measures on its own settings and a parent's `scenarioForecastCents` is non-null when any child opted in. `hierarchyWarnings`: `allocation` (children's own amounts exceed the parent's, counting only children on the identical window, since a monthly amount says nothing about a quarterly parent), `actual`, `forecast`. One resolver per list request and per evaluation pass, so a parent and its children share reads. A failing child throws out of the parent's status rather than reporting a short total.
- **Hierarchies and cost visibility: a rollup only sums what its owner can see.** The resolver is built over the _visible_ budgets, never the raw org list: `loadVisibleBudgets` (`visibilityOwnerCondition`) at request time, and in `evaluateBudgetsForOrg` one resolver per `visibility_user_id` (null = every budget; a scoped owner = only their own), whose `status()` runs inside that owner's resolved scope. So a scoped member's parent never rolls up a budget they cannot read, and the per-resolver memo never serves a figure measured in one scope to another. A parent that is not visible to a budget's owner simply leaves that budget as a root in their tree. `validateBudgetWrite` keeps the structural checks (cycle, depth, unit) over the whole org tree, but the parent itself must be visible, so a hidden budget id reads as "not found".
- **Write-side hierarchy checks** are in `web/src/services/budgets.ts` `validateBudgetWrite` (`BudgetValidationError` → 400): parent exists, not self, not a descendant (cycle), depth ≤ `BUDGET_LIMITS.maxDepth` (4) counting the moved subtree's height, and parent/child count the same thing (currency, or usage unit). An update may not change what a budget with children counts. `softDeleteBudget` re-parents children to the deleted budget's own parent; config-as-code `remove` does the same.
- **Usage data** comes from `cost_daily.usage_amount`/`usage_unit` via `queryUsageDaily` and `getCostUsageUnits` (`GET /costs/dimensions?dimension=usage-units`, also the MCP `list_cost_dimension_values`). Units match exactly and are never converted. Only plugins that set `usageUnit` on rows (OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Hetzner, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Speechmatics) and pushed rows feed it; AWS groups by service+region with mixed units, so it does not.
- **Alerts** speak the unit (`usage 600K tokens has reached 50% of 1M tokens`), add `sum of N child budgets` for a parent, and give routing **no money facts** for a usage budget, so an "over $500" rule cannot match tokens. Workflow budget triggers take the period limit and usage figures; `BudgetTriggerEvent` keeps cents fields as cents (0 for usage) and adds `measure`, `usageUnit`, `usageLimit`, `observedUsage`, `periodStart`/`periodEnd`.
- **Surfaces.** `budgetProgress` (client-core) is the one reading of a status row every card uses; `budgetWithStatusToInput` replaced four hand-rolled `budgetToInput` copies (desktop's had been dropping `savedFilterId`, `scenarioModelId` and `useAdjustedSpend` on save). Costs panel draws `buildBudgetTree` as an expandable tree (open by default when a warning or child alert needs attention); a dashboard card for a parent lists its children collapsed (`BudgetWidgetCard.allBudgets`). Mobile mirrors both (`features/costs/BudgetTree.tsx`) and edits measure, unit, cadence and parent, but **deliberately not explicit period lists** (two date pickers per row do not fit a sheet); they are shown and round-trip. CLI `infrawrench budgets [--json]` (pure helpers in `cli/format.ts`). Config as code carries `measure`/`usageUnit`/`usageAmount`/`period`/`parentKey`, written only when non-default so monthly spend budgets export byte-identically. Terraform `infrawrench_budget` gained `measure`, `usage_unit`, `usage_amount` (custom `positiveFloatAtMost` validator: float64validator has no exclusive bound), `parent_budget_id`, a `recurring_period` single block and `explicit_period` list blocks (conflicting via `resourcevalidator.Conflicting`), and `amount_cents` became optional with default 0. `GET /budgets/{id}` is now documented as the `BudgetWithStatus` it always returned.

## Charge types, amortization & estimate provenance

`CostRow` carries optional `chargeType` (`usage|commitment_fee|commitment_discount|credit|tax|refund|adjustment|support|other`, absent = `usage`), `amortizedAmount` and `commitmentId`; `CostCapabilityDeclaration` gained `chargeTypes`, `amortization` and `estimated`. Queries take `costBasis: "cash"|"amortized"|"blended"` (blended: see "Blended commitment discounts") — **amortized falls back to the cash amount per row** (`if(amortized_amount != 0, amortized_amount, amount)`), because otherwise a non-amortizing provider mixed with an amortizing one drops out entirely and reads as a saving. `charge_type` and `commitment` are groupable/filterable dimensions.

**The dedupe trick is load-bearing.** `cost_daily`'s ORDER BY is frozen and excludes charge type, so a provider reporting a usage line, the credit against it and the tax on it as three otherwise-identical rows would collapse under ReplacingMergeTree to whichever paged in last. Charge type and commitment id are folded into `tags_hash` as reserved `infrawrench:`-prefixed synthetic entries (same trick as pushed rows). **The fold is conditional**: a row with no charge type hashes exactly as before, so restatement re-fetches replace history instead of doubling it. ClickHouse additive `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is now an established path in `migrate.ts` — additive only, never the sort key.

`estimated: true` marks providers whose amounts we compute rather than collect (inventory × rate card, or usage × published list prices). Surfaced through `CostCollectionNotice` on all three platforms and the CLI, naming the three one-directional errors: resources deleted mid-period are missing, rates are list rates, credits and tax are absent.

## Kubernetes cost allocation (derived, not billed)

A cluster has no billing API, so cost is derived in `plugin-kubernetes/src/cost-model.ts` (pure, db-free): split each node's price into CPU and memory pools (**65/35**, from GCP's published per-vCPU/per-GiB component rates — the only vendor publishing them; it moves money _between_ tenants on a node but never changes the cluster total or any efficiency figure), charge each pod `max(request, usage)` per dimension, measure shares against node **capacity** not allocatable (capacity is what the invoice is for), clamp overcommit proportionally, and split the remainder into named `idle` and `systemReserved` buckets. **Neither is spread across tenants** — doing so overcharges them and hides the finding, which is that the cluster is oversized.

Node rates arrive via the existing `credentialMappings` mechanism (`nodeHourlyRates` on all seven cluster resource types); DigitalOcean gives real billed price, AWS/Azure list price (Azure for every agent pool via the lister's `vmSizes`), GCP list price per node pool keyed by the `cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool` label (`byNodeLabel`, because two pools can share a machine type and differ by attached GPUs), CoreWeave the account's negotiated rates or its published list price, Scaleway/OVH none. **With no rate, capacity and efficiency render with no money attached** rather than a fabricated number. `metrics.k8s.io` is optional — a 404 degrades to requests-based allocation.

Surfaced through the plugin: peer-pane subtitles and status (`PeerPaneSchema` has no chart/table slot, so real breakdowns go elsewhere), `dashboard-stats.ts`, `TableNode` breakdowns in `detail-renderers.ts`, and `fetchMetricSeries` merged onto the parent cluster's Metrics tab via `exposeMetricsToParent`. Cost rows use `maxHistoryDays: 1` with namespace/workload as tags. **Allocation deliberately does not inherit `SYSTEM_NAMESPACES`** — it reads pods directly so kube-system's cost cannot silently vanish.

**The peer pane's Namespaces grid does the opposite, on purpose.** It is a filter control over the pane's own workload listings, and those listings _do_ inherit `SYSTEM_NAMESPACES`, so no pod ever reports `kube-system` and offering it as a filter would empty the pane. `PeerPaneView` therefore draws only namespaces present in the set derived from the other groups — the same set the namespace `<select>` is built from, so the two controls always agree — and takes the group's header count from that list rather than from `group.items`, which is what stopped the header claiming more namespaces than it drew. The old system/user disclosure inside `NamespaceGrid` was unreachable for the same reason and is gone. Group titles carry their count inside the string (`Namespaces (5) · by cost`), so all count handling goes through `PeerPaneView.utils.ts`, which anchors on "a parenthesised integer ending the title or preceding the `·` suffix" — matching only a _trailing_ count read that title as uncounted and appended a second one.

## Cost reports, currency, query language & exports

**Cost reports** (`cost_reports`, migration `0075`) are first-class: named, addressable, with a `cost-reports` workspace tab (`reportId` compared in `workspaceTabTargetsEqual`, fixed tab id) and a `cost_report` widget kind. Deletion is asymmetric like budgets — removing a card leaves the report; deleting the report removes every card. `folder_id` is a reserved nullable column with no folders table yet. The ad-hoc `cost_graph` widget is untouched.

**Currency** (`org_currency_settings`, `org_exchange_rates`, migration `0076`) is opt-in conversion at the org's _own_ stated rates with effective dates, plus (since the FX feed) opt-in automatic ECB rates; see the next paragraph. Rates are `numeric(20,10)` (drizzle returns strings; float becomes one only at the multiply). Conversion happens in app code after per-currency aggregation, never in SQL. A zero/unparseable rate reads as _no rate_, conversion is all-or-nothing per currency, and an unconvertible currency keeps its own series rather than being dropped. Budgets fold in other currencies only when the budget currency is the display currency, so conversion can only ever count _more_ spend and cannot un-fire an alert.

**Automatic exchange rates** (`fx_reference_rates`, `fx_rate_feed_state`, `org_currency_settings.auto_rates`/`rate_basis`, `org_exchange_rates.effective_to`). Source is the ECB euro reference rates (eurofxref XML; ~30 currencies, TARGET working days, history from 1999-01-04), chosen because it is free, unauthenticated and stable since 1999; no fallback source, currencies it lacks are **manual-only** and say so on the Currency page. Stored **once globally**, as published (units per EUR, `numeric`); crossing and carry-forward happen at read time, so nothing derived is stored. The poller's `runFxRateFeedPass` (`server-core/src/cost/fx-feed-pass.ts`) claims the single `fx_rate_feed_state` row with the status-feed lease pattern; the first success fetches the full history (~8 MB, under the egress proxy's 10 MB cap for a few more years; move to the zipped CSV when it is not), later runs the 90-day file (heals gaps and ECB corrections). Next fetch is 15:30 UTC, re-checking every 2h on a weekday whose publication is late, hourly after a failure; errors land on the row and show in Settings. Fetches go through `fetchPublicFeedBody` (`status/fetch-feed.ts`, shared with status feeds). **Carry-forward is per publication, not per currency**: a day uses the newest publication on or before it, and if that publication lacks the currency there is no rate (ISK 2008-2018, BGN after euro adoption, RUB), so a discontinued currency is never carried forward for years. Cross rates use both legs from the same publication. Readers hold the whole history in a per-process snapshot (`fx-feed-store.ts`: one `string_agg` row per day, parallel `Float64Array`s, <2 MB, 15 min TTL), which is what lets the pure converter look rates up synchronously without threading date ranges through every loader. **Precedence lives in one class, `RateBook` (`cost/currency-convert.ts`)**: the latest stated rate effective on or before the day wins unless its `effectiveTo` has passed (an older stated rate never resurfaces past an end date), else the feed (at the day, or at the month end under `month_end`; manual coverage is always judged by the cost day), else unconverted. Every converter takes `RateSource = RateBook | ExchangeRate[]` (a bare array means stated-only, the old behaviour) and every caller loads through `loadOrgRateBook`; invoices resolve to their own billing currency with it. `CostConversionRate` gained `source` and `firstDay`/`lastDay` (the span of data each rate converted), which is how graph tooltips name the rate behind a bucket (`conversionRateForDay`) without re-implementing precedence client-side; `summarizeConversionRates` condenses sixty daily feed rates to one range line. Invoice CSV has `rate_source`/`rate_effective_from` columns; frozen invoices predating the feed have no `source` and read as manual. `describeCostConversion` is now also the digest/report-delivery caveat and the dashboard-PDF note. Settings: `PUT /currency` takes optional `autoRates`/`rateBasis` (omitted keeps the stored value, so old clients and Terraform configs without them cannot reset them); `GET /currency/lookup` and `GET /currency/feed` are read-only (`costs:read`) and already inside the desktop allowlist's `currency` prefix. CLI `infrawrench currency [rate|feed]`, MCP `get_currency_settings`/`lookup_exchange_rate`, Terraform `auto_rates`/`rate_basis`/`effective_to`.

**Two surfaces label a converted figure, and they are not interchangeable.** `describeCostConversion` (`client-core/src/currency.ts`) is the one-liner every compact surface prints — graph-card footnote, mobile card, chart aria-label, CLI. `ui/src/cost/CostConversionNotice.tsx` is the long form and the only place the _rates and their effective dates_ appear, plus the mid-period rate-change flag and the amber block naming a currency that is missing from the headline total; it is mounted above the widgets in `CostsPanel`, beside `CostCollectionNotice`. The panel gets the `conversion` block from the overview card's own response via `CostGraphCard`'s `onConversion` callback (held in a ref inside the card, so an inline arrow from the page does not re-run the query) rather than issuing the same `/costs/query` twice. `UnitCostCard` never fires it — a ratio has no currency to convert.

**Cost query language** (`client-core/src/cost-query-language.ts`, pure) compiles text to the existing `CostFilter[]` and nothing else — inexpressible input is a parse error, not a new code path, and `"query"` is in the `Omit<>` on the reader so text is type-level barred from SQL. Round-trips both ways (property-tested over generated inputs). `OR` is rejected naming the fix. The CLI compiles locally and posts `filters`, never `query` — an older server would ignore the field and return _unfiltered_ spend.

**Cost exports** (`cost_exports`, migration `0077`) stream rows via `ResultSet.stream()` into an S3-compatible or HTTPS sink, re-chunked into 8 MiB multipart parts; steady-state memory is one part, and back-pressure throttles the query. Restatement is handled twice: a trailing re-export window rewrites overlapping periods in full at the same key, _and_ every row carries `exported_at` + `collection_watermark` (the minimum newest-collected-day across accounts). Object keys are deterministic per period so re-export overwrites. Writes are `org:settings:write`, not `costs:write` — creating one is standing authorisation to ship the whole billing history to a destination the creator chose.

**FOCUS 1.3 / 1.4** (`cost_exports.output_schema`, migration `0127_cost_export_output_schema`; API `schema: native | focus-1.4 | focus-1.3`, 1.4 added in API `1.74.0` with no migration since the column is text). Orthogonal to `format`, so a FOCUS export can be CSV or NDJSON. The value is versioned so a later spec is a new option, never a silent header change; `FOCUS_COLUMNS_BY_VERSION` (`FOCUS_1_3_COLUMNS`, `FOCUS_1_4_COLUMNS`) / `FOCUS_CUSTOM_COLUMNS` in client-core are the headers and only change alongside a new schema value. Read a schema's version with `focusVersionOfSchema` rather than comparing strings. (Not to be confused with `FOCUS_COLUMNS` in `custom-costs.ts`, which is the _import_ side's column map and already reads 1.0 through 1.4.)

- **Adding a FOCUS version** is: a column list + `FOCUS_VERSIONS` entry + schema value + label in client-core, version branches in `toFocusRow` (`server-core/src/cost-exports/focus.ts` lists what differs per version at the top), the two OpenAPI enums (`CostExportSchema`, `FocusExportRequest.version`) plus an `API_VERSION` minor bump, the Terraform `schema` validator and description (regenerate `docs/`), and the docs page's "1.4 or 1.3" section. Diff the spec between tags (`git diff v1.3 v1.4 -- specification` in `FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec`) and check the Cost and Usage column files' feature levels and the ServiceCategory/Subcategory tables; `plugin-base/src/focus.ts` holds one category list on the basis that 1.3 and 1.4 share it.
- **1.3 vs 1.4 in our output**: 1.4 drops `ProviderName`/`PublisherName` and forces `EffectiveCost = BilledCost` on Tax (1.3 wanted tax derived from the taxed charges' effective cost, so 1.3 keeps the provider's figure). 1.4's new Conditional `InvoiceDetailId` and `CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails` are left out: the latter must list _every_ eligible public program, and a partial list is non-conformant. The new Billing Period / Contract Commitment / Invoice Detail datasets are not written.
- **The ad-hoc download defaults to 1.3** (`FOCUS_DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_VERSION`) because 1.4 removes columns an existing script may read; our clients send `version: FOCUS_LATEST_VERSION` through `focusExportRequestForConfig` (UI) or the CLI's `--focus-version`. The response carries `X-Focus-Version`. The mapping lives once in `server-core/src/cost-exports/focus.ts` and serves both the scheduled run and the ad-hoc `POST /costs/focus-export` (`costs:read`, 366-day cap, streamed; validation runs before the first byte so errors are still a 400). Decisions worth knowing before touching it:

- **Full row grain, always.** `ResourceId` must be set on any charge tied to a resource, which an aggregated row cannot honour, so `query.dimensions`/`tagKeys`/`costBasis` are ignored for FOCUS while `filters`/`chargeTypes` still apply (`costExportScope` in `rows.ts` is the shared WHERE). A PUT that omits `schema` keeps the stored value, so older clients cannot flip a FOCUS export back.
- **BilledCost = cash, EffectiveCost = `amortizedAmountExpr()`**, the same expression the graphs use. Credit/Adjustment rows force effective = billed (spec MUST). List/ContractedCost = effective for Usage, billed otherwise: no collector reads a price list, and understating commitment savings beats inventing a list price.
- **`PricingQuantity`/`ConsumedQuantity` must be null without `SkuPriceId`**, which no provider API we use supplies, so the usage quantity rides as `x_UsageQuantity`/`x_UsageUnit`. Don't "fix" this by filling PricingQuantity; it makes every file non-conformant.
- **Charge categories:** usage, covered usage and `commitment_discount` → Usage; `commitment_fee`, `support` → Purchase; `credit`, `refund` → Credit; `tax` → Tax; `adjustment`, `other` → Adjustment. A purchase row with a commitment id gets the id as its `ResourceId` (discount-handling MUST).
- **Service classification is plugin-owned**: `manifest.costs.focus` (`services` substring rules, first match wins, plus an optional `default`), validated by the manifest schema against the spec's category→subcategory tree in `plugin-base/src/focus.ts`. An invalid pair would make the loader drop the whole plugin, which `cost-export-focus.test.ts` guards. Undeclared services fall back to a generic English keyword classifier, then `Other`. Broad clouds (aws, azure, gcp, cloudflare, digitalocean, scaleway, ovh) ship `focus-services.ts` rule tables; single-purpose providers set `default`.
- **Names come from Postgres, once per run** (`loadFocusLookups`): account display names, the commitment inventory (category `Spend` for savings plans, `Usage` otherwise; ids not in the inventory fall back to an ARN heuristic because the column may not be null), and resource names/types matched on `(account_id, external_id)`, deleted resources included.

**Warehouse destinations** (`kind: "warehouse"`, API `1.51.0`, no migration: the creds columns were already nullable) load an export into a Snowflake or Databricks table through a _connected account_, with no credential of its own. The base is generic: a plugin declares `manifest.warehouseSink` (target fields: key, label, `dependsOn`, `optional`, `allowCustom`) and implements `PluginClient.listWarehouseTargetOptions` / `loadWarehouseRows` / `describeWarehouseSetup` (`plugin-base/src/warehouse-sink.ts`). The destination stores `{pluginId, accountId, target: Record<string,string>}`; hosts never interpret `target`, and `server-core/src/cost-exports/warehouse.ts` only validates it against the declared fields (unknown keys are _refused_, not dropped, or Terraform would see a diff it cannot fix), types columns in a portable vocabulary (`string|date|timestamp|decimal|boolean|json`; native names by table, FOCUS names by convention: `*Cost`/`*Quantity` decimal, `*PeriodStart/End` timestamp, `Tags` json, so the FOCUS layout maps when it lands), and hands rows over one period at a time. Every row gains `export_id` + `period_start`; each period is replaced atomically on `export_id = id AND day BETWEEN from AND to`, so the destination tolerates redelivery like S3 (no in-flight marker) and several exports can share a table. Routes: `GET /cost-exports/warehouse-sinks`, `POST /cost-exports/warehouse-options`, `POST /cost-exports/warehouse-setup` (all `org:settings:write`; provider refusals are 400 with the message, and the form falls back to typing). Desktop needs no allowlist change (the `cost-exports` prefix already covers subpaths). CLI: `exports warehouses|create|setup`; Terraform: `plugin_id`/`account_id`/`target` on the destination block.

- **Snowflake** cannot `PUT` over the SQL API (documented limitation), and binding is not allowed in multi-statement requests, while `BEGIN…COMMIT` needs one (each SQL API request is its own session, so temp tables are out too). Hence: bound multi-row `INSERT`s (1,000 rows / ~768 KB of binds; the VALUES cap is 16,384 rows, text guidance 1 MB) into a `TRANSIENT` `<TABLE>__IW_STAGE_<rand>`, then one literal-only 4-statement `BEGIN; DELETE; INSERT…SELECT; COMMIT`, then drop. MERGE was rejected because it cannot remove rows that vanished from a restated day. Only idempotent statements are retried at the sink layer; `runSql` already retries throttling with the same `requestId` (deduplicated server-side). Unquoted-style names are upper-cased so users can query them unquoted. `runSql` grew `bindings` and `multiStatementCount`.
- **Databricks** uses the Statement Execution API on a picked SQL warehouse. Named parameters cap at **256 per statement** (undocumented, enforced), so values go in as literals with **backslash** escaping: Databricks SQL does not read `''` as an escaped quote (adjacent literals concatenate), so ANSI escaping would silently corrupt apostrophes. Staging Delta table in 2 MiB statements, then `INSERT INTO t REPLACE WHERE … SELECT` (single atomic commit). `REPLACE WHERE` takes no column list before DBR 19.3, so the SELECT is built in the target's column order from the UC tables API, `CAST(NULL AS <type>)` for columns the export does not write. Only HTTP 429 is re-sent. A UC volume + `COPY INTO` was rejected: extra grants and a picker, and `COPY INTO` dedupes by file name, which fights restatement.
- **Native layout only.** The loader replaces each period by `day` and maps the native columns; FOCUS rows carry `ChargePeriodStart` instead, so `normalizeInputFor` refuses any `focus-*` schema with a warehouse destination (400) and the run refuses a stored row that has both. The FOCUS names in `COLUMN_TYPES` are groundwork for lifting that, which needs a day column derived from `ChargePeriodStart` and FOCUS cells in `warehouseCells`.

## Cost display options (measure, bins, chart types; API 1.58.0)

Saved reports and `cost_graph` widgets share one `CostGraphConfig`, so every option below lives there (jsonb, **no migration**) and every surface that renders a config honours it. All new fields are optional and never defaulted, and `costQueryForConfig` omits them at their defaults, so a config written before them issues byte-identical requests.

- **Measure** (`measure: cost | usage | count`, absent = cost). `usage` sums `cost_daily.usage_amount` over rows with `usage_unit = usageUnit` and **folds currencies in JS** (the scan stays the spend query's, grouped by currency; `queryCosts` merges on `""`), so series carry `currency: ""`. `count` goes through `queryCostCounts`: an inner per-(bin, value, currency) sum and an outer `uniqExact` of values whose sum `!= 0`, plus a second statement without the bin for the range total, because a value billed every day is one value. Empty group values are excluded. The service answers count on its own path (`runCostCountQuery`: one series labelled "Service count", no top-N, `totals[""]`). Responses carry `measure` (absent for cost) and `usageUnit`; every renderer formats through `formatCostMeasureValue` and keys totals by the response's currencies, so watch for `""` being falsy (the PDF's `primary ?` checks had to become `!== undefined`).
- **Rules live in one function**, `costDisplayProblem` (client-core): usage needs a unit, a unit is refused on any other measure, count needs a group-by and cannot be cumulative, non-cost measures refuse forecast/scenario/adjusted/unit cost, and a unit-cost chart refuses the cumulative _toggle_ (the legacy `cumulative` bin stays valid there). The server (`runCostQuery`), the stored-config zod schema (`costGraphConfigSchema` is now `costGraphConfigObjectSchema.superRefine(...)`, so reports, widgets, org config as code and the MCP write tools all refuse a config that could only render an error), both editors and the CLI call it. `costQueryRequestSchema` deliberately stays a plain object because the MCP tools spread its `.shape`.
- **Bins**: `quarterly` is `toStartOfQuarter` server-side and `costBucketStart`/`formatBucketLabel` client-side (unit costs pick it up through the same helper). `hourly` is in `COST_BINNINGS` but **every provider's rows are daily** (`CostRow.date` is a day, `cost_daily` is keyed by day), so `COST_STORE_GRANULARITY = "daily"` in `cost-readers.ts`, `bucketExpr` throws for it, `runCostQuery`/`runUnitCostQuery`/the custom-graph dispatcher refuse it with `HOURLY_BINNING_UNAVAILABLE_REASON`, `GET /costs/status` reports `granularity` per account, and the editors show it disabled via `hourlyCostBinningAvailable(statuses)`. Enabling it means an hourly store plus plugin support and flipping that constant (or making it per account); Terraform's `binning` validator omits `hourly` until then.
- **Cumulative** is now a toggle (`cumulative: true`) at any bin; `binning: "cumulative"` remains the legacy spelling of daily + toggle. Read both through `effectiveCostBinning(q)`; totals use `costSeriesTotal(points, cumulative)` (last point, not sum). The editors normalise a legacy config to daily + toggle on open and save the new spelling. `binForecast` gained a `cumulative` parameter (bins first, then runs the sum from the last actual).
- **Chart types** gained `donut` (pie now draws as a full pie; donut is the ring with the total in its hole) and `table` (rows per bin, a column per series, bin total, previous-period column; no forecast rows; real `<table>` semantics instead of `role="img"`). `isCostTotalsChart` is the pie/donut test, typed as a guard. Count is one series, so editors don't offer pie/donut for it.
- **Usage units** come from `GET /costs/dimensions?dimension=usage-units` (`getCostUsageUnits`, most-used first), riding the existing route and desktop IPC passthrough, so no new channel.
- **One-off run overrides**: `POST /cost-reports/:id/run` takes an optional body `{measure, usageUnit, binning, cumulative}` (`costReportRunOverridesSchema`, applied by client-core `applyCostReportRunOverrides`, which drops the money-only overlays when switching to usage/count). Used by CLI `reports <name> --measure/--bin/--unit/--cumulative` and the `run_cost_report` MCP parameters; never saved.
- **Surfaces**: shared `CostGraphConfigModal`/`CostGraphCard` (web + desktop), mobile `CostGraphSheet` (chips; hourly omitted with a hint since a chip cannot be disabled) and `CostChart` (pie/donut/table; takes a `format` function instead of a currency), CLI `costs`/`reports` flags with `--json` echoes, PDF (`costResponseBlocks`: table view, pie for donut, unit/count formats, distinct-count note), Terraform `measure`/`usage_unit`/`cumulative` on `infrawrench_cost_report`. **Deliberate omission:** scheduled report delivery still summarises _spend_ in the report's scope whatever its measure (it is a spend digest; the PDF/dashboard path renders the measure).

## Cost visibility scopes & per-object sharing (cloud-only)

Two controls that narrow the role model rather than adding to it. Migration `0125_cost_visibility_and_sharing` (two tables + `visibility_user_id` on `budgets`, `cost_alerts`, `report_notifications`); API `1.43.0`.

**Scopes are applied where cost queries are built, through an ambient store.** `server-core/src/cost/visibility-context.ts` is an `AsyncLocalStorage<CostVisibility>`; `clickhouse/cost-readers.ts` `costDailyOrgCondition(orgId)` is the **only** place a `cost_daily` org predicate is built (cost readers, `commitment-readers.ts`, the export row stream), and it ANDs on the scope's layers. `network-flow-readers.ts` narrows to `strictlyVisibleAccountIds`. A parameter threaded through every service would have been a silent-failure diff (a missed call site reads the whole org and looks fine); the store makes a cost route added later scoped without knowing scopes exist. `server-core/src/__tests__/cost-visibility-sql.test.ts` calls every reader under a scope and asserts the predicate reaches the emitted SQL, and fails on any raw `eq(costDaily.organization_id` outside the helper (`cost-reconcile.ts` is the allowed write-path exception). **No store means unrestricted**: the poller's evaluators, exports and the digest. **Every request path establishes one**: `costVisibilityMiddleware` (`web/src/auth/cost-visibility.ts`) runs last in the `orgScoped` chain for sessions, keys and agents; `runToolHandler` (`tools/permissions.ts`) wraps every MCP/chat dispatch (`api/__tests__/cost-visibility-routes.test.ts` enumerates route files that import cost data and asserts each is on the org tree or self-scoped, and that no dispatch site calls `tool.handler` directly); Slack `/infrawrench costs` wraps per linked member. A store for org A reading org B throws.

**Model.** `cost_visibility_scopes` (one per `role | member | api_key` principal; no FKs on purpose, so a deleted centre/account/principal narrows rather than cascading the restriction away). A layer matches `(account IN … OR showback multiIf IN centres+descendants) AND savedFilter`; an empty layer or an unresolvable saved filter matches nothing. All applicable layers **intersect** (role ∩ member ∩ key), the same rule as key scopes ∩ owner role. Owners are never scoped (resolver ignores role/member rows; the route refuses). Claimed agents resolve through their claimer; non-members get an empty visibility (match nothing). Saved-filter delete refuses while a scope references it (`cost_visibility_scope` referent kind).

**Postgres-side halves** live in `web/src/services/cost-visibility-filter.ts`. Per-account figures (credits, commitments, network flows) need an explicit account grant (`strictlyVisibleAccountIds`; a centre-only or filtered layer contributes none). Stored org-wide findings (anomalies, efficiency alerts incl. unit-cost regressions, the Moment anomaly feed) are withheld from scoped callers; they cannot be narrowed after detection. `/costs/status` lists accounts with a visible row or an explicit grant.

**Unattended objects evaluate as their scoped creator.** `visibility_user_id` is set to the creator only when they were scoped (null = org-wide); `budget-eval`, `change-eval` and report delivery (scheduled and "Send now") resolve that user's scope live and run inside it. No FK: a departed user must make the object see nothing, not widen to the org. Scoped callers list only objects with `visibility_user_id = them` (their stored crossings are over their own slice); objects created by unrestricted members are hidden from them. Cost-figure pushes (`COST_FIGURE_TRIGGERS` in client-core) exclude scoped members except the object's own `costVisibilityUserId` (`AlertEvent` → `sendPushToOrg` opts). Slack/Teams channels are org-chosen and unaffected.

**Refused outright for scoped callers** (`COST_SCOPE_DENY_RULES`, 403 `cost_scope_restricted`): `/cost-exports`, `/custom-cost-sources` (upload totals are org-wide money and an upload delete tombstones org-wide rows), `/invoices`, `/managed-accounts`, `/digest`, `/config`, writes to `/cost-visibility` and `/team/roles`, `POST /team/invitations`, `PATCH|PUT /team/members`. The team rules are the escalation guard: any role change could widen someone's visibility (including the caller's alt account). Break-glass elevations add permissions, never lift a scope.

**Sharing** (`object_access_grants`; one table, `principal_kind = 'org'` row is the org default, absent = `editor` so nothing changes until someone shares). `web/src/services/object-sharing.ts` holds the resolver and its own ALS principal (established by the same middleware and `runToolHandler`; no store = system caller with full access). Level = max(org default, member grant, role grant, report creator = implicit owner, **explicit** sharing of every ancestor folder). A folder at the default contributes nothing, or "No access" on a report would be undone by its folder. `sharing:override` (new permission, offered as an API key scope, Admin/Owner via catalog) bypasses. Delete = owner, or editor when nobody owns the object (legacy rows). Below viewer is a 404 (mapped in `api/index.ts` `onError`), visible-but-insufficient a 403. Enforced in the report/folder services (shared with the MCP report tools), every dashboard route, `validate-tabs`, `/sync/pull` (dashboards + pins), and report cards on dashboards (filtered when the report is not viewable). Creating a dashboard or folder grants the creator `owner`; reports use `created_by_user_id`, surfaced as an `implicit: true` grant the dialog and Terraform never send back. `PUT` replaces the document and requires an owner to remain; `DELETE` resets to the default.

**Surfaces.** Settings → Cost Visibility (`ui/src/settings/CostVisibilitySection.tsx`, registry key `cost-visibility`, pickers over centres/accounts/saved filters/roles/members/keys); `ShareDialog` + `createSharingClient` (`ui/src/sharing/`) on the reports panel (rows, folders, detail) and both `DashboardView`s; desktop reaches both through `cloud_settings_request` (`cost-visibility|sharing` + `GET saved-cost-filters` on the allowlist). `/team/me` returns `costVisibility`; mobile shows `CostVisibilityNotice` on the Costs tab (no editors on the phone, the anomaly-tuning precedent). CLI `infrawrench cost-visibility [me]` (`--json`). Terraform `infrawrench_cost_visibility_scope` (import `<kind>/<principal_id>`) and `infrawrench_object_sharing` (authoritative, set of grants, destroy resets). Docs: `team-and-billing/cost-visibility.md`.

**Known limits.** Cost annotations are human-written notes and stay visible to everyone with `costs:read`. Client-side caches (react-query, desktop) are per principal; a scope change shows on the next refetch. There is no server-side cost-result cache to poison.

## Cost canvases (cloud-only)

A natural-language report builder on top of the chat agent (migration `0127_cost_canvases`, API `1.47.0`). A user describes a report; the agent writes a **canvas**: a saved `CostCanvasSpec` (`client-core/src/cost-canvases.ts`) of blocks: `text`, `kpi` (spend / unit_cost / forecast / budget / anomaly_count), `chart` (a full `CostGraphConfig`), `table` (grouped spend, one column per bucket), `budgets`, `anomalies`, `cost_report`, `custom_graph` (the deterministic way to carry other connected tools' data).

**The spec stores queries, never numbers.** `runCostCanvasSpec` (`web/src/services/cost-canvases.ts`) re-answers every block through the service its standalone card uses (`runCostQuery`, `runUnitCostQuery`, `listBudgetsWithStatus`, `listRecentCostAnomalies`, `getCostReport`, `renderOrgCustomGraph`), inside the request's cost visibility store and sharing principal, so refresh, PDF, delivery, CLI and MCP never call a model and a canvas can never show more than its reader could query. Narrative quotes figures only as `{{kpiId}}` / `{{kpiId.change}}` tokens filled at run time (`renderCostCanvasText`); a typed number in text would freeze, and the system prompt says so. A failing block renders its error in place. Budgets need `budgets:read` and custom graphs `dashboards:read` (passed as `granted`; null = system caller). The live UI passes `includeChartData: false` because chart blocks draw through `CostGraphCard`, which queries for itself; CLI/MCP/PDF ask for the series.

**Strict validation, no SQL.** `costCanvasSpecSchema` in `ui/src/cost/config.ts` (`Exact`-asserted against the client-core types) is `.strict()` at every level, so an unknown key from the model is a 400 / tool error, never carried along. Filters are the structured `CostFilter[]`; no field takes a query string. `superRefine` checks unique ids, that text tokens name kpi blocks, tag keys, and scenario-needs-forecast. `formatCostCanvasSpecIssues` renders the failure as `path: message` so the model can fix it from the tool result alone. A `6m` relative preset was added to `COST_RANGE_PRESETS` for "the last six months".

**Reuse of the chat backend, not a parallel stack.** Creation is `POST /cost-canvases/draft`: an empty canvas (with `prompt` stored) plus a `chat_conversations` row whose new `cost_canvas_id` points at it. The canvas page embeds the ordinary `ConversationView` (new optional props `initialMessage`, sent once when the conversation loads empty, so a reload still delivers the prompt; `onActivity`; `placeholder`). `chat/agent.ts` appends `canvasAgentContext(conversationId)` to the system prompt for linked conversations (read once per turn; the agent is told to `get_cost_canvas` before editing). The link is conversation → canvas, not the reverse, because chat history is per user: an editor the canvas is shared with gets their own conversation (`POST /cost-canvases/:id/conversation`), and the `CostCanvas.conversationId` on the wire is the _caller's_ latest one.
