**Edits are chat approvals with a diff.** `write_cost_canvas` is `risk: "write"` with `requiresApproval` true when it replaces a canvas that already has blocks (creating, or filling the empty draft, auto-runs). The generic new `ToolDefinition.approvalSummary(input, auth)` hook returns plain lines (`describeCostCanvasChanges(diffCostCanvasSpecs(...))`, block-level by id, with moves computed from a longest-increasing-subsequence so one insertion doesn't read as everything moving); `agent.ts` runs it through `runToolHandler` (so it sees the caller's scope and sharing, and the dispatch-site test stays green) and stores it on the new `chat_pending_actions.summary`. `ConversationView`, mobile's chat screen and the canvas page's banner render it. The canvas page also finds the pending `write_cost_canvas` for its canvas and offers **Preview proposed** (`POST /cost-canvases/preview`), outlining changed blocks; approve/reject stay in the chat card so the resume path is the one chat already has.

**Composition.** Sharing is a fourth `ShareableObjectType`, `cost_canvas`, with the creator as implicit owner like reports and no folder chain (`hasImplicitCreatorOwner` / `inFolderTree` in `object-sharing.ts`; the Terraform `object_type` validator and OpenAPI enum moved too). Pinning is a `cost_canvas` dashboard widget kind (`{version, canvasId}`), filtered by sharing in `visibleWidgets` and checked on create; deleting a canvas soft-deletes its cards, parks its schedules and drops its grants, the report rule. PDFs reuse the dashboard mappers (`costConfigCard`, `unitCostResponseBlocks`, `customChartBlocks`, now exported) in `services/cost-canvas-pdf.ts`; a canvas card on a dashboard PDF folds its blocks into one section. Delivery is `report_notifications.cost_canvas_id` (the one-target check now counts three columns) with logic in `server-core/report-delivery/canvas.ts`, sharing `deliverDashboardNotification` (new `noun` param) and `recordAttempt`; rows are claimed by the web delivery loop after the dashboard pass. Unlike dashboard schedules, canvas schedules record `visibility_user_id` for scoped creators and `renderCanvasForDelivery` runs inside that scope.

**Surfaces.** Workspace tab `{kind: "cost-canvases", canvasId?}` (single tab, canvas compared; web `/cost-canvases/$canvasId`, desktop `?canvas=`), shared `CostCanvasesPanel` / `CostCanvasView` / `CostCanvasWidgetCard` in `ui/src/cost-canvases/`, web `lib/cost-canvases-client.ts`, desktop `lib/cost-canvases-client.ts` over the `cloud_cost_canvas*` IPC channels (`electron/cloud-data/cost-canvases.ts`; sharing rides the existing settings proxy). Manual edits without the agent: move/remove blocks, edit a chart in `CostGraphConfigModal`, rename. Mobile: read-only list/detail under Costs, `CanvasBlocks` native renderer, dashboard card, read-only schedules. CLI `infrawrench canvas list|show|refresh` (`--json`, `--format pdf`). MCP/chat tools in `web/src/tools/cost-canvases.ts`. Terraform `infrawrench_cost_canvas` (spec as JSON) and `infrawrench_cost_canvas_notification`. Not in org config as code, like cost reports (a `cost_canvas` card exports its raw `canvasId`). Docs: `features/ai-canvas.md`.

## Custom cost sources (uploaded CSV / FOCUS spend)

A named source (`custom_cost_sources`, migration `0133_custom_cost_sources`) that files are uploaded into; each source is **its own value in the provider dimension**, `plugin_id = custom:<sourceId>`, labelled with the source's current name by `providerNames(orgId)` in `web/src/services/cost-query.ts` (so a rename relabels history and no row is rewritten). Accounts are synthetic: `custom:<id>` or `custom:<id>/<file's account label>`, labelled "<label> (<source>)". Ids live db-free in `server-core/src/cost/custom-cost-ids.ts`.

- **Parsing is client-side and shared.** `client-core/src/custom-costs.ts` owns CSV parsing (delimiter sniffing, quotes, BOM), header auto-mapping (`detectCsvMapping`), the CLI's `--map field=Column` overrides, FOCUS detection and mapping (`FOCUS_COLUMNS`, checked against the v1.4 spec; `ChargeCategory` + `CommitmentDiscountId` → charge type, `EffectiveCost` → amortized), value parsing (dates incl. ambiguous slash-date detection, locale money formats), and **daily aggregation on exactly `cost_daily`'s dedupe key** (account, day, service, region, resource, tags + charge type + commitment, currency). Skipping the aggregation would make two lines of one file replace each other on insert. The Settings section (`ui/src/settings/CustomCostSourcesSection.tsx`, web route + desktop panel via the `cloud_settings_request` allowlist) and `infrawrench costs push --format csv|focus` both call it, so a file maps identically from either.
- **Upload sequence**: `POST …/uploads` (declares range + mode) → `…/rows` chunks of ≤5,000 through the shared ingest validator (`validateCostRows` in `cost-ingest.ts`, now with `subAccountId`, `allowAttribution` and `dateRange` options; the API push and workflow paths leave them off and behave exactly as before) → `…/complete`. Every row carries the reserved tag `infrawrench:upload=<uploadId>`, which is what makes "delete this upload" exact and keeps two uploads from replacing each other. The tag key is filtered out of `getCostTagKeys`.
- **Overlap is explicit**: creating an upload whose range overlaps a live upload without `mode` is a 409 listing them. `replace` is applied at **complete**, never at create, so an interrupted upload never removes what it meant to replace; it zeroes every row of the source in the range except its own, then `refreshHoldings` recomputes the affected uploads' row counts/totals/range from ClickHouse (`replaced` when nothing is left).
- **Removal is tombstones** (`clickhouse/custom-cost-store.ts`), the `cost-reconcile.ts` idiom: zero-amount rows at the stored keys, copying `tags`/`tags_hash`/`charge_type`/`commitment_id` verbatim, paged by day. Deleting a source zeroes all its rows before dropping the Postgres row (nothing could find them afterwards).
- Permissions: reads `costs:read`, everything else `costs:write` (same as `POST /costs/rows`). Terraform manages the source (`infrawrench_custom_cost_source`), not uploads; destroying it deletes its spend, which the schema description says. **Mobile is a deliberate omission** for uploading (no file picker + mapping UI worth having on a phone); its spend still shows in every mobile cost view because labelling is server-side. MCP needs nothing new: the cost tools already see these rows as providers.

## Jira integration

`jira_integrations` + `jira_issue_links` (migration `0074`), org-scoped, credentials encrypted like Twilio/Teams. Findings (cost anomaly, orphan, oversized, posture, expiring, probe) become issues; the link row is unique on (org, kind, source, key) so the UI shows "already filed" rather than offering a duplicate. Descriptions convert to **ADF server-side** — passing a plain string to the v3 API does not error, it writes the raw characters, so the failure would be invisible. Project and issue type are API-backed pickers, never typed keys. The site host is checked against an Atlassian suffix allowlist in `jira.ts`: **the bastion registry is not the right control** (it is keyed by plugin id for a connected cloud account; this is an org integration with no account row and no bastion in the path), and without it a member-supplied URL is an SSRF primitive. Members get `jira:read` but not `jira:write`.

## Issue filing (Jira + Linear)

Two parallel integrations (`jira_*` / `linear_*` tables — deliberately not generalized, so either is removable alone) behind one tracker-neutral affordance in `ui/src/issue-filing/` (the old Jira-named compat re-exports — `ui/src/jira/`, `JiraFilingProvider`, `FileJiraIssueButton`/`Modal` — were removed once no host imported them). The button labels itself by what is configured and the caller's per-tracker write permission; a tracker radio appears only when both are connected. Jira: per-org site URL guarded by an Atlassian suffix allowlist (member-supplied host = SSRF primitive), descriptions converted to ADF server-side (a plain string writes raw characters without erroring). Linear: fixed `api.linear.app` GraphQL host so no allowlist (commented where jira.ts has its guard); personal API keys go **bare** in `Authorization` (Bearer is the OAuth form and silently fails); descriptions are markdown; GraphQL errors arrive inside HTTP 200 and rate limits inside HTTP 400 — parse the body, don't trust status. Both: member gets `:read` not `:write`; link tables unique on org+kind+source+key so a finding can't be double-filed.

**Host wiring is load-bearing and was wrong on web for a while**: the provider has to sit above the workspace-tab viewport, because every findings list is a tab. Web mounts it in `components/OrgProviders.tsx` from `__root.tsx`, desktop inside `DesktopWorkspaceTabsViewport` — see "Workspace tabs and React context" for why the org layout route is not an option.

## GitHub issue filing and IaC pull requests (cloud-only)

The third tracker, but not a third copy of Jira/Linear: it runs on the org's existing **GitHub App** installation (`github_installations`, installation tokens from `server-core/github/app.ts`), so there is no stored credential, and it adds three things the other two lack. Tables `github_issue_settings` (one row per org; routes and Terraform sources inline as jsonb, PUT is whole-document because route order is meaning), `github_issue_links`, `savings_finding_states`, `savings_finding_scans`.

- **Permissions are GitHub-side state, not ours.** The app needs `issues: write` (and `contents` + `pull_requests: write` for PRs). GitHub applies a GitHub App's new permissions to an existing installation only after an owner of that account approves them, so old installs keep serving workflows/agents and answer 403 "Resource not accessible by integration" to issue writes. `issues-api.ts` turns that into `GithubApiError.missingPermission`, the route into the structured 409 `github_permission_required` (`client-core/api-errors.ts`, thrown by both web `apiFetch` and desktop `settings-client.ts`), and the UI into `GithubPermissionPrompt` with the installation's `html_url`. `GET /github-issues` also reports each installation's _accepted_ permissions (`GET /app/installations/{id}`) so the prompt shows before a failed submit. A permission 403 calls `forgetInstallationToken`: a cached token keeps the old permissions for up to an hour after approval.
- **Dedupe is a fingerprint, twice.** `findingFingerprint` = sha256(org, kind, sourceId), org-scoped so two orgs filing into one repo never comment on each other's issues. A partial unique index allows one _open_ link per org+fingerprint (the race guard), and every body carries `<!-- infrawrench-finding:<fp> -->`, searched (`/search/issues`) as the fallback when our link is lost. Refiling comments; a link whose issue was closed on GitHub is marked closed and a new issue opens. `indexGithubLinks` prefers an open link; rows treat a closed link as unfiled.
- **"New" needs memory.** Orphans and rightsizing are recomputed on read, so the poller's savings scan (`github-issues/savings-scan.ts`, six-hourly claim on `savings_finding_scans`) diffs against `savings_finding_states`: new findings raise the **`savingsFindings`** trigger (one alert per finding, `amountCents` = monthly cost or saving, cap 25 per scan biggest-first, the overflow forgotten so it re-raises), vanished ones call `resolveFindingIssues` (close+comment / comment / none per settings, once per link via `resolvedAt`). The **first scan baselines silently**; a feed that threw neither raises nor resolves its kind ("could not tell" is not "went away"). Anomalies resolve on first acknowledgement (`web/services/cost-anomalies.ts`); idle commitments key on account+commitment so next month comments on the same issue. To make the scan possible `listOrphans`/`listRightsizing` moved from web services to `server-core/savings/` (web files are re-exports).
- **Auto-filing is alert routing, not a second rule engine.** `AlertDestination` gained `{kind: "github-issues"}` (no id: the repository comes from the settings' routes); `AlertEvent.finding` carries what to file and `route.ts` lazily imports the filer. Alerts without a finding skip the destination (neither attempted nor failed). `savingsFindings` is excluded from `defaultAlertRule` and push-muted by default, exactly like drift, so shipping it changes nothing for an org that never writes a rule.
- **Routing** is first-match over routes by cost centre (the first allocation rule by priority matching account/plugin/tag; rules with a `service` condition are skipped because a resource has no service) or tag (null value = any), then the default repo; pure `resolveGithubIssueRoute` in client-core.
- **IaC pull requests derive the attribute, never hard-code it.** `pull-request.ts` runs the plugin's `terraformExport.mapResource` on the resource and on a copy with the rightsizing size field set to the recommendation; exactly one changed top-level literal attribute or it refuses. The address comes from `getIacResourceStatus`; the repo/directory from `iacSources`, keyed by IaC state _scope_ (account id or null) rather than state id, because re-uploads mint new ids and old ones are pruned. `hcl.ts` is a splice editor, not a parser: one scan marks code vs string/heredoc/comment and brace depth, and edits replace only the value bytes so the PR diff is one line. Refusals: module or indexed addresses, expression values, missing attribute, duplicate blocks, an orphan still referenced in the module. The recommendation is re-checked against the live (cached) rightsizing/orphan feed, so a forged size never becomes a PR. Gated by `pullRequestsEnabled` (settings need `org:settings:write`) + `github-issues:write` + a click; no auto-merge anywhere.
- **Surfaces.** Shared `GithubIssuesSection` (settings registry key `github-issues`; desktop allowlist gained `github-issues`, `github/(status|repos|install-url)` and `iac/states`), GitHub as a third tracker in `FileIssueModal` (repo/labels/assignees pickers in `issue-filing/github.tsx`), `OpenPullRequestButton` on Savings/Oversized rows, the routing `DestinationPicker`, CLI `infrawrench github-issues [settings]`, five MCP tools, `infrawrench_github_issue_settings` in the Terraform provider, and mobile filing into the routed repo (no settings, no PRs). Permissions `github-issues:read` (members) / `:write`.

## Provider cost coverage (Aug 2026 sweep)

**devin** (Oct 2026) estimates cost from ACU consumption at a user-editable price per ACU, by product, with sessions as resources and user/playbook/session tag as tags; see the Devin section for why there is no billed-cost path.

Cost collection added for **deepgram** (real USD daily), **elevenlabs** (money; successor endpoint is POST with an array `group_by`, so product type and region arrive together — on the deprecated fallback only _one_ breakdown is requested, since each is a complete decomposition and emitting both double-counts), **cartesia** (credits → money at the lowest published tier, `estimated`), **speechmatics** (hours → money; the endpoint returns a window aggregate with no buckets so daily rows are one request per day, `maxHistoryDays: 90` because history costs _requests_ here, `estimated`) and **hetzner** (inventory × `/v1/pricing`, `estimated`; emits rows **only for the day it runs** because a past month rebuilt from today's inventory omits everything deleted since — and traffic counters are _cumulative per billing period_, so those rows are dated to the period's first day and restated in place, `restatementDays: 31`; all money is scaled-integer, never float).

**newrelic** (Oct 2026) estimates cost from its usage events at user-editable rates (list prices by default) by product, with the consuming account and the ingest source or compute capability as tags; see the New Relic section for why there is no billed-cost path.
**grafana-cloud** (Oct 2026) reads billed usage per month by product, stack and region, period-native; see the Grafana Cloud section.
**elastic-cloud** (Oct 2026) reads the v2 Billing API per day, by deployment/project (resource), line-item category (service), SKU region and organization / instance / instance_type / component tags; prepaid ECUs feed credit burndown (see the Elastic Cloud section).
**sentry** (Oct 2026) estimates cost from `stats_v2` usage at user-editable rates (Team plan list prices by default) by data category, with the project as a tag; see the Sentry section for why there is no billed-cost path.
**coralogix** (Oct 2026) prices daily units by pillar and TCO priority at the account's editable unit price (published $1.50 default, `estimated`); see the Coralogix section.
**twilio** (Oct 2026) reads billed usage-record prices by leaf usage category, reconciled to `totalprice` daily, split per subaccount with the auth token (see the Twilio section); the account balance is a `credits` pot.
**fastly** (Oct 2026) reads invoices for closed months and the month-to-date invoice for the current one, monthly and dated to the 1st, by product, region and `productLine`/`productGroup` tags with charge types (see the Fastly section).
**datadog** (Oct 2026) reads Datadog's own contracted-rate cost: daily from estimated cost for the current and previous month, finalised monthly totals before that, by product, region, `org` and `pricing` tags; projected month-end cost and tag attribution are on the organization detail (see the Datadog section).

**baseten** (Oct 2026) reads billed spend from `/v1/billing/usage_summary`: dedicated inference per deployment and chainlet, training per job and Model APIs per model, daily, tagged by model/deployment/environment/instance type/team (see the Baseten section).

**Verified as having no usable billing API** (do not retry without new evidence): assemblyai, gladia, revai, cohere, deepseek, gemini (route via `gcp`), workos, groq, together, replicate, fly (GraphQL billing is undocumented), netlify. **Cloudinary was declined deliberately** — it is a flat subscription with an included allowance, so credits are not proportional to money and no rate makes the series correct. `mongodb`/`redis`/`kafka` are connection-string protocol plugins here, not SaaS clients, so they have no account to bill; Atlas spend comes from the separate `mongodb-atlas` plugin (billed invoice line items, Oct 2026).

**snowflake** (Oct 2026) reports billed amounts from organization usage when the role can read it and credits × user-editable prices otherwise, per service group and warehouse; see the Snowflake section.
**Verified as having no usable billing API** (do not retry without new evidence): assemblyai, gladia, revai, cohere, deepseek, gemini (route via `gcp`), workos, groq, together, replicate, fly (GraphQL billing is undocumented), netlify. **Cloudinary was declined deliberately** — it is a flat subscription with an included allowance, so credits are not proportional to money and no rate makes the series correct. `mongodb`/`redis`/`kafka` are connection-string protocol plugins here, not SaaS clients, so they have no account to bill; managed Redis Cloud is its own plugin (`redis-cloud`, below).

**redis-cloud** (Oct 2026) reads billed cost from the FOCUS cost report (`POST /cost-report` → task → `GET /cost-report/{id}`, ≤40 days per report), spreading each line's `BilledCost` over its charge period by UTC-day overlap; when the user key's role cannot generate reports it falls back to a list-price estimate of today's inventory only, tagged `costBasis: list-price-estimate` and returned `degraded: true` (see the Redis Cloud section).
**github** (Oct 2026) reads real billed amounts from the enhanced billing platform's usage report: daily, gross as usage plus discount as credit, by product, SKU, repository, organization and cost centre; see the GitHub section.

**modal** (Oct 2026) reads the workspace billing report over Modal's gRPC API: daily cost per app/sandbox/volume by resource type (each GPU type, CPU, memory) with user tags, plus each cycle's credits and plan adjustments as charge-typed rows on the 1st, so months sum to the invoice (Team/Enterprise plans; see the Modal section).
**oracle-cloud** (Oct 2026) reads billed `computedAmount` from the OCI Usage API, daily, by service, SKU (tag), region and resource, with each resource's compartment path as a tag; Universal Credits commitments feed credit burndown (see the Oracle Cloud section).

## Commitments & the savings planner

Plugins declare `commitments?: { kinds }` and implement `fetchCommitments(accountId)` (throw-rather-than-partial). `CommitmentRecord` lives in `plugin-base/src/cost.ts` beside `CostRow`, joined by `CostRow.commitmentId`. The load-bearing split is `hourlyCommitmentAmount` XOR `unitCommitments` — it decides which utilization question is even askable. **Omit, never substitute**: GCP CUDs carry units and no money at all; Azure's list carries no price but does return its own utilization, passed through verbatim and never blended with derived numbers. `termDays` comes from the provider, never from the dates (split/merged commitments have dates that no longer span the term).

Coverage is a **range** (broad = all uncovered usage, lower bound; narrow = only ever-covered `(plugin, service, region)` cells, upper bound) because there is no single honest denominator. Utilization's obligation counts only `active ∩ window ∩ days-with-data` — counting a day collection never ran reports a healthy plan as under-utilized. Unit-denominated → `null` with reason, never 0%. The planner recommends at nearest-rank **p10** of daily uncovered spend, gated PRESENCE → NOT-IN-DECLINE → FLOOR → MATERIALITY in that order (floor-before-trend misreports a 50% decline as "spiky"); break-even is exactly `1 − discount`. Until collectors stamp `commitmentId` onto rows, coverage reports unavailable with excluded accounts named. Collection is a poller pass on the credits-poll pattern (`account_commitments`, `account_commitment_polls`).

## Commitment attribution (what makes coverage non-zero)

Coverage was inert on ship: no collector stamped `commitmentId`, so it honestly reported "unavailable". Turning it on needed three model corrections, because the naive version reports a confident **0%** — strictly worse than unavailable.

**Coverage is computed on the amortized basis, never cash.** AWS prices RI/SP-covered usage at an unblended rate of **zero**, and Azure prices reservation-covered usage at an EffectivePrice of **zero** in ActualCost. Covered _cash_ spend is structurally zero on both, so a cash ratio reads 0% for every org that has ever committed to anything. `amortizedAmountExpr()` is exported from `cost-readers.ts` and shared by `commitment-readers.ts` and `cost-exports/rows.ts` so the three cannot drift — a restated copy in the exporter already had.

**`commitment_covered_usage` exists because AWS cannot supply a commitment id.** `SAVINGS_PLAN_ARN` / `RESERVATION_ID` are filter-only dimensions in Cost Explorer, never groupable. Azure can (`BenefitId`, EA/MCA only). So the coverage numerator is "charge type is covered-usage **or** a commitment id is present", not the id alone. Every `chargeType === "usage"` site was audited: the coverage and delivered denominators widened; the `hashTags` fold, the ingest default and the `charge_type DEFAULT 'usage'` did **not** — the back catalogue genuinely is usage, and widening the fold would collide a covered row with the plain usage row of the same cell.

**`amortized_reported UInt8` distinguishes absent from zero.** A commitment purchase's honest amortized amount _is_ 0, and the old `if(amortized_amount != 0, …)` fell back to full cash — rendering every purchase at cash **and** its amortized slices. Pre-existing rows default the flag to 0 and land on the `OR amortized_amount != 0` arm, i.e. bit-for-bit the old expression.

**Two-GroupBy limits shape both collectors.** Cost Explorer and Azure Cost Management both cap grouping at two, so each runs multiple passes per chunk. AWS's passes are literal complements (`Not` of the usage record-type union), so spend is conserved even if a record-type token is misspelled. Azure's second pass is deliberately **unfiltered** because the API has no `NotIn` — a filtered complement would silently drop any charge type Azure adds later. Azure derives covered usage as the per-cell gap between ActualCost and AmortizedCost, gated on both being non-negative: Azure emits negative corrections, and an ungated subtraction _fabricates_ coverage.

**Accumulate before emitting.** Any pass whose normalizers are many-to-one must aggregate into a keyed map first. Two provider rows that normalize to the same `(date, service, region, currency, chargeType, commitmentId)` are one host key, and `ReplacingMergeTree` keeps whichever arrived last — silently losing the other. Azure shipped this bug; its test suite had encoded it.

## Blended commitment discounts (the third cost basis)

`CostBasis` is `cash | amortized | blended`. Blended is amortized with each commitment's discount spread evenly across all the usage it was eligible to cover, so every eligible row in a pool carries the same effective rate: `rate = Σ effective / Σ on-demand-equivalent`, `blended_i = onDemand_i × rate`. It exists for chargeback: on amortized, which team "got" a shared Savings Plan or CUD is an accident of the provider's application order.

**Computed in the plugins at collection time, stored, never derived in SQL.** Only the plugin knows a row's on-demand equivalent and which rows share a commitment's scope, so each cloud plugin stamps `CostRow.blendedAmount` and declares `costs.blending`. The arithmetic is shared in plugin-base `cost-blending.ts` (`blendCommitmentPools`, `allocateProportionally`): the last weighted member absorbs the floating-point remainder so a pool's blended sum equals its amortized sum, and a pool with any unknown weight, negative amount, or no covered member is left unblended rather than guessed. Query-time blending was rejected: it would need an org-wide window per pool under every filter and visibility scope, so a cost-centre view would compute its own (wrong) rate.

**Storage mirrors amortized.** `cost_daily.blended_amount Float64` + `blended_reported UInt8` (additive columns; absent vs reported zero kept apart). `blendedAmountExpr()` in `cost-readers.ts` falls back to `amortizedAmountExpr()` per row, and `costBasisAmountExpr(basis)` is the single resolver every reader and the export stream use. Because unblended rows read as amortized and pools sum exactly, every day's blended total equals its amortized total for any provider mix and for history written before the columns. Tests prove it at each layer: `plugin-base` property test, per-plugin day sums, `server-core/src/__tests__/cost-blended-basis.test.ts`, and the ClickHouse integration test.

**Per provider (pools and weights):**

- **AWS**: pool `(day, currency, service)`; Cost Explorer has no instance-family grouping and Compute SPs span regions, so a regional RI's discount moving between regions of one service is the accepted approximation. On-demand rows weigh `UnblendedCost`; SP-covered usage's `UnblendedCost` _is_ its on-demand cost (`AmortizedCost` = `SavingsPlanEffectiveCost`). RI-covered (`DiscountedUsage`) unblended is 0, so the weight comes from `GetReservationUtilization` daily `OnDemandCostOfRIHoursUsed` per service (single-value `SERVICE` filter, so one request per reserved service), spread over regions by RI effective cost. SP and RI halves of pass 1b are separated by one extra `SavingsPlanCoveredUsage` request. Only chunks with covered usage pay for any of it. An RI ratio outside [1, 20] means the member account is reading utilization for reservations it does not own, and leaves the pool unblended. Needs `ce:GetReservationUtilization` (in the preflight policy); refusal is not an error.
- **Azure**: pool `(day, currency, service)` per subscription. Two extra `AmortizedCost` queries when covered usage exists: `[ServiceName, MeterId]` filtered `PricingModel In (Reservation, SavingsPlan)` with `UsageQuantity`, and `[MeterId]` for `OnDemand` to get the subscription's own per-meter rate; meters never run on demand are priced from the public Retail Prices API (same unit of measure, no conversion). Ratio outside [1, 20] or an unpriced meter leaves the service-day unblended.
- **GCP**: from the billing export, `credits.type` `COMMITTED_USAGE_DISCOUNT` pools per `(day, currency, region)`, `COMMITTED_USAGE_DISCOUNT_DOLLAR_BASE` per `(day, currency)`; eligible usage is every line of a SKU that got that credit type that day, weighted by `cost` (pre-credit). A fully covered row (net 0) is kept now because it takes part in blending. The richer query falls back to the original on a 400 so an old export table cannot lose spend. New-model spend CUDs (discount in the consumption-model price, `FEE_UTILIZATION_OFFSET` on the fee) are left as billed.

**Surfaces.** Every basis enum in the OpenAPI paths (costs, budgets, reports, cost canvases, exports, invoices/managed accounts, showback/cost-centre and tag-policy `?basis=`, change impact, unit costs), API 1.68.0, plus optional `blending` on `/costs/status`. Postgres `cost_basis` columns are free text, so no migration. UI: `CostBasisField` offers Blended only when `useCostBasisChoice` sees a blending account (or the saved value is blended) and shows a per-basis hint as both the select's `title` tooltip and a line under it (`COST_BASIS_HINTS`); invoices' customer modal has its own select. Mobile `CostBasisChips` mirrors it with the hint text (no hover on a phone), from `COST_BASIS_DESCRIPTIONS` in client-core. CLI `--basis blended` on `costs` and `unit-costs`. MCP `query_costs`/`get_cost_status` descriptions. Terraform `cost_basis` on budget, cost report, cost export and managed account accepts `blended`. Commitment coverage, utilization and the planner stay amortized on purpose: they describe what the provider did, not how to split it.

## Unit costs, scenarios, billing rules & invoicing

**Business metrics** (`business_metrics` + `business_metric_values`, Postgres both halves) divide spend to give cost-per-unit and margin. The series lives in Postgres, not ClickHouse, because the join is _not_ per-point: ClickHouse sums the numerator to the requested buckets, Postgres sums the denominator to the same buckets, and they meet once in application code — the shape `currency-convert.ts` already uses. **A missing denominator renders as a gap, never 0 or ∞** (`value: null` + a typed reason); a genuine zero stays `0`, and the two must stay distinguishable. Ratios are computed at the requested bucket — a daily unit cost summed over a month is not the monthly unit cost. `kind: "count" | "currency"` is a DB check constraint in both directions, and margin is offered only for `currency` metrics. Note `infra.metrics` was already taken by workflow key/value metrics (and is a Proxy returning `null` for unknown keys, so `infra.metrics.write` would have silently been `null`) — the binding is `infra.businessMetrics.write`, mapped to `costs:write` in `workflows/authorize.ts`.

**Business-metric importers** pull a metric's values on a schedule instead of waiting for a push. The provider half is a plugin capability, `manifest.businessMetricSource` (the importer form: fields typed `select`/`sql`/`text`/`number`, `dependsOn` for cascading pickers, `readOnly: "enforced" | "validated"`, `supportsDryRun`) plus three optional client methods, `listBusinessMetricSourceOptions`, `runBusinessMetricSource`, `dryRunBusinessMetricSource`; the contract and its helpers (`businessMetricSqlProblem`, `bindBusinessMetricSqlRange`, `rowsToBusinessMetricPoints`, `zonedDayStartMs`/`localDayOf`, `withBusinessMetricTimeout`) are `plugin-base/src/business-metric-source.ts`. Implemented by aws (CloudWatch GetMetricStatistics, hourly periods summed into local days within the 455-day retention, daily beyond), gcp (BigQuery; every run dry-runs first and refuses unless `statementType` is `SELECT`, 100 GiB `maximumBytesBilled`), snowflake (`multi_statement_count: 1`, session timezone set; read-only is only _validated_, there is no session setting that refuses writes), clickhouse (`readonly=1` plus result/time limits, the account's one configured service; the Cloud API key cannot run SQL so there is no service picker), postgres/mysql (through the new optional `SqlHostServices.queryReadOnly`, which the server injects only when the driver implements it, and which the plugins never fall back from), and the new metronome plugin (usage via `POST /v1/usage`, revenue via invoice breakdowns, optional per-customer labels). The datadog plugin was not on main when this landed; adding it is one capability on that plugin. The host half is `server-core/cost/metric-importers.ts` (validation against the form, the window, aggregation, storage, history) and `metric-import-pass.ts` (poller claim, the query-monitor `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` protocol that pushes `next_run_at` forward before running). Rules that are easy to break: a scheduled run restates **closed days ending yesterday** in the importer's timezone (never today); `restateImportedDays` deletes every label of each returned day and inserts the new rows in one transaction, but leaves days the source returned nothing for alone (a gap stays a gap), and points outside the window are dropped; the SQL guard is re-run on every execution, not just on save; failures back off from 1 h doubling to the schedule interval; and configuring/previewing/running needs `resources:execute` on top of `costs:write`, the query monitors' permission, because the query runs with the account's credentials. One importer per metric (`metric_id` unique). `business_metric_values` gained `label text NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` and the unique key is now `(metric_id, day, label)`; empty string rather than NULL because a NULL never collides in a unique index, so unlabeled restatement would append. Readers that divide (`getMetricValues`) sum labels per day, and coverage counts distinct days. CSV upload is client-only (`parseCsv`/`csvRowsToMetricValues` in client-core) and writes through the ordinary values endpoint in 5,000-value batches. Desktop reaches all of it over `cloud_*business_metric*` IPC channels; mobile shows only the importer status line on each card; the CLI verb is `unit-costs sources` / `unit-costs importer <key> [show|runs|run|set|enable|disable|delete]` (params as `--set key=value`, `@file` reads a value); Terraform has `infrawrench_business_metric_importer`, imported by metric id, whose GET wrapper synthesises a 404 from `{"importer": null}`. `generate:plugin-strings` now extracts importer form labels too.
**Calculations and labels.** `UnitCostMode` is `unit_cost | margin | usage_unit_cost | raw_metric`, each with a `scale` (per 1/100/1K/1M/1B; applied to the quotient only, `cost`/`metricValue` stay literal sums, and margin ignores it). The engine is `server-core/cost/unit-cost-run.ts`, **not** the web service, because the poller's threshold evaluator must judge exactly the number the chart draws and the poller cannot import `@infrawrench/web`; `web/src/services/unit-cost-query.ts` is now only the error vocabulary around it (and still resolves the metric through `getBusinessMetric`, which is the seam its tests mock). `usage_unit_cost` needs no metric: numerator and denominator are both `cost_daily` rows filtered to one `usage_unit` (the server-only `CostQuery.usageUnit`), so "cost per GB-month" divides exactly the spend that bought those GB-months; its route is `POST /business-metrics/usage-unit-costs` and `UnitCostQueryResponse.metric` is null there (the only case). `raw_metric` divides nothing, so zero/negative values are points, not gaps. Margin points carry `absoluteMargin`.
Values carry **labels** (`labels jsonb`, canonical) plus a scalar `label text NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` that is the restatement key `(metric_id, day, label)`: `''` for none, the bare value for a set holding only the `label` key, canonical JSON otherwise (`businessMetricLabelsKey`). That column, its default and its unique index name are the business-metric importers' single breakdown label, unchanged. `restateImportedDays` writes an importer's label as the label set `{label: <value>}` (jsonb and key both), the same row a pushed `{ label: "acme" }` makes, and `storedLabels` still reads any row with `labels = '{}'` from its key. The API keeps the single `label` on `BusinessMetricValue` (derived: the `label` key of `labels`) and accepts it on writes, since it shipped first. CSV upload is one flow, `MetricCsvImportModal`: `MetricCsvColumnMapping.labelColumns` maps header-named columns to labels (`guessCsvMapping` ticks every other valid header), beside the unnamed `label` column for headerless files. Rows partition the metric: `getMetricValues` sums a day's rows in SQL so every pre-label reader keeps its series, and `buildDenominators` sums duplicates instead of last-write-wins. A ratio split or filter by label needs a **label mapping** (`business_metrics.label_mappings`: a cost dimension + tag key, or `cost_centre`), because a per-value ratio needs a per-value numerator; the engine groups the numerator by that dimension (or by the allocation `multiIf` via the server-only `CostQuery.groupByAllocation`, shared with showback through `allocationExpr`) in the same single scan and refuses unmapped labels in ratio modes. At most one cost-centre-mapped label per query (a row belongs to one centre). Splits keep the 25 largest values by metric total and fold the rest into "Other", whose numerator is restricted to the folded values so it never absorbs spend with no denominator. **Thresholds** (`business_metrics.thresholds` jsonb; events in `unit_cost_threshold_events`) reuse the regression's insert-then-cooldown protocol with a 7-day cooldown, are keyed by a hash of the threshold's own fields (no ids in jsonb; an edit is a new threshold), skip windows with fewer than half their days reported and never judge "Other", and route under the existing `unitCostRegressionAlerts` trigger (relabelled "Unit-cost alerts") with a new `unit_cost_threshold` push type and efficiency-alert kind. Metric keys `usage-units` and `usage-unit-costs` are reserved because they are static routes beside `/:id`.

**Scenario models** are the half forecasting cannot see: known future cost. Rate changes apply first as _deltas against the untouched baseline of their own scope_, so overlapping rates compose additively (+10% and −20% is −10%, not ×1.1×0.8) and their order provably cannot matter; absolute amounts are added afterwards. `response.forecast` stays the unadjusted trend and `response.scenario` is a **second** field, never a replacement. **Budgets keep the raw trend unless a budget opts in** via `budgets.scenario_model_id` — a hypothesis someone typed must not silently change when a real person is paged.

**Billing rules** adjust spend **at query time and never write `cost_daily`** — collected spend is the audit trail. Percentages compile to a _product of conditional factors_ (`amount * if(c1,1.1,1) * if(c2,0.85,1)`), because markups genuinely compose; reallocation is first-match-wins in a `multiIf` and rewrites only the _group expression_, so conservation is structural rather than arithmetic. `adjustment.rawTotals` is returned whenever `adjusted` is set — even for an org with no rules, so the field's absence has one meaning. Exports, unit costs, anomalies, change alerts and the digest stay **raw**: they either page a human or feed a unit-economics figure. Writes are `org:settings:write`, like currency and exports.

**Invoicing**: `draft` recomputes on every read; **approval is the freeze** — lines, totals, exchange rates _and the day they were read_ are written to the row, and a frozen invoice never touches ClickHouse again (the test asserts `getShowbackSpend` was not called, not merely that the number matched). Void, never edit or delete; corrective invoices link both ways. Permissions are a three-way family (`invoices:read|write|issue`) because approve/send/void are irreversible and `write` is not — that split is what makes maker-checker expressible.

**Managed-account (MSP) pricing** sits on top of billing rules and keeps the same invariant: applied when an invoice is computed, never written to `cost_daily`. Four controls: re-rating to public list price and discount treatment live on the customer (`managed_accounts.pricing` jsonb, null = neutral), `tiered` and `expression` are new billing-rule kinds that are **invoice-only** (`BILLING_RULE_INVOICE_KINDS`; `compileBillingRules` and `summarizeBillingRules` skip them, so graphs, budgets and showback never move and their caption never names them) and can be scoped by `cost_billing_rules.managed_account_ids`. Invoices with any money-moving rule or non-neutral pricing take the **priced path**: `getPricingLines` scans with the same allocation `multiIf` + cost-centre reallocation as showback but grouped by month/account/provider/service/region/charge type/unit plus one column per tag key a rule reads (`'='||value` vs `''` so key-presence survives), and the pure engine `client-core/msp-pricing.ts` applies re-rate → discount treatment → percentage/tiered/expression rules in priority order, keeping a per-line ledger. The ledger is what makes "which rule changed what" exact (`line.effects`, `derivation.effects`) and makes `collected + Σeffects = adjusted` hold by construction. Percentage rules give the same totals on both paths (product of factors = sequential multiplication). Neutral customers keep the classic `getShowbackSpend` path byte-for-byte. Pricing is part of the approval compare-and-swap inputs.

**List prices** are an additive `cost_daily.list_amount` + `list_reported` pair (zero is an answer: free tier). Only set where the provider says so: GCP `cost_at_list` (only when every export row in the group had it; a 400 naming the column retries without it, keeping the blending columns, and any other 400 drops blending instead, so the chain ends at the original query and either feature survives the other's column being absent), AWS pass-1a `Usage` lines (unblended is the public rate because EDP/PPA/bundled discounts are separate `Discount` records; Spot re-rates at its Spot price; covered usage has no list in CE), and every `estimated` plugin (host fills `listAmount = amount` in `collect.ts`). Everything else falls back to collected + uplift, and invoices report the split as coverage. Azure's Query API has no list price.

**The expression language** (`client-core/pricing-expression.ts`) is a hand-written lexer, Pratt-ish parser, type checker and tree-walking evaluator over a closed field/function set. It never reaches SQL: expressions are evaluated in application code on the grouped lines, which is also why they are invoice-only. Hostile-input bounds (length, tokens, depth checked during parsing, nodes, list and string length) are tested; tag and field lookups go through `Map`s so `__proto__` is just an unknown name. A runtime failure (division by zero, non-finite, > 1e12) leaves the line at its previous cost and is reported, never zeroed. `POST /billing-rules/preview` prices one month without the rule (`ruleId` excluded) and with the candidate, through the same engine; the CLI's `billing-rules preview` and MCP's `preview_billing_rule` are thin wrappers. `POST /billing-rules/reorder` rewrites priorities to 10, 20, 30… in one transaction. `PUT /billing-rules/{id}` and `PUT /managed-accounts/{id}` leave `managedAccountIds` / `pricing` as saved when absent, so older clients cannot silently widen or reset them; the Terraform provider always sends both.

**Nested cost centres**: `parent_id` on the existing table rather than a second "segment" noun, so there is one allocation model and one rule list. `totals` keeps its exact old meaning (directly-allocated spend) and `subtreeTotals` is new, so a consumer summing centres still gets the org total and cannot be made to double count. The `multiIf` still resolves a row to one centre in one scan; the tree is assembled in application code afterwards.

## Network flow attribution

Egress and cross-zone transfer are billed as a total with no cause attached. The answer is a **pair** — who talked to what, across which boundary — which no existing cost dimension expresses.

**Raw flows never move.** The `GROUP BY` runs inside the provider's log query service; only the grouped result crosses the wire. A second low-cardinality totals query exists so the truncated tail is an exact subtraction rather than an estimate — that second scan is the price of having a denominator. Addresses, ports and protocols are resolved to resource refs _before_ storage and never persisted: a churning address would mint a new row per day for the same workload, which is the cardinality bomb here.

**`network_flow_daily` is its own table, deliberately not `cost_daily`.** Merging would stack a derived second opinion of data transfer on top of the provider's own billed `DataTransfer` line and double-count it into every budget, anomaly, export and invoice. The key is `(scope, direction, attribution, src/dst ref, zone, service)` folded into a `pair_hash`, capped at ~518 rows per account-day, TTL 90 days — this explains a bill rather than being a record of one.

Collection is **forward-only** behind a watermark: flow logs do not restate, so re-querying a settled day charges the customer again for a byte-identical answer. A day missed during an outage stays missed, and that is stated rather than papered over.

Amounts are **unconditionally `estimated`** with no off switch, because no configuration makes them reconcile: the free monthly allowance is consumed by services these records cannot see, and volume tiers and negotiated rates are invisible. All errors run in known directions, so the _ranking_ holds even where the absolute figure does not. Cross-zone is priced **per direction** on purpose — AWS captures at both ENIs and bills both ends. GB is 10^9; GiB would under-report by 7.4%, small enough to read as drift.

Enabling collection is `org:settings:write`, not `costs:write`: it authorizes daily queries **billed to the customer's own cloud account per GB scanned**, in perpetuity. The claim predicate joins on the switch so a collector bug cannot run a billable query for an org that never opted in.

## AI request attribution (AI spend by caller, cloud-only)

Splits billed AI spend by caller (team, user, feature, customer, any request-metadata key) by joining per-request logs to the bill. Migration `0127`, API `1.47.0`, docs `features/ai-attribution.md`.

**Two halves, one contract (`plugin-base/src/ai-requests.ts`).** (1) AI-billing plugins stamp normalized tags on their `CostRow`s via `withAiCostTags`/`aiCostTags`: `ai:provider` always, `ai:model` and `ai:token_type` where the billing API says (Anthropic cost report `model`/`token_type`, OpenAI `line_item` "model, type", Cursor events, Bedrock Marketplace "… (Amazon Bedrock Edition)" service names, Fireworks/OpenRouter model). Plain tags, so model and token type work in every report, filter, budget and allocation rule with no new dimension plumbing; the tag change re-keys rows, which host reconciliation (`cost-reconcile.ts`) already zeroes on re-written days. Cloudflare's own rows are deliberately **not** tagged (its file header explains why tag changes on that collector are risky). (2) Plugins that can read request logs declare `aiRequestLogs.sourceKinds` and implement `listAiRequestLogLocations` (the picker; Bedrock's `GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration` marks the recommended bucket/log group) and `fetchAiRequestLogs` (one closed UTC day, **already aggregated** through `AiRequestAccumulator`, which keeps only mapped metadata keys and caps distinct combinations at 2,000 with an `(other)` overflow row). AWS: `bedrock-s3`, `bedrock-cloudwatch` (Logs Insights `stats`, `queriesBillable`), `jsonl-s3`. Cloudflare: `ai-gateway` (logs API, 50/page, cached hits skipped, 4,000-page cap → degraded). The custom JSONL format is parsed by `parseAiRequestJsonLine` in plugin-base, so every storage-owning plugin reads the same documented schema. `fetchSigned` gained `binary` because the host-routed HTTP path decodes UTF-8 by default and would corrupt `.json.gz`.

**LiteLLM is host-owned, not a plugin** (`server-core/ai-attribution/litellm.ts`): nobody holds an account with it and it has no bill of its own, it is a gateway the org runs. `/spend/logs/v2` paged at 1,000, admin key encrypted on the source row (AAD `ai_request_source:<id>:api_key`), URL through the cost-exports egress guard (`destinationFetch`: https, no private/reserved addresses, no redirects). The proxy's Postgres is deliberately not read directly.

**The arithmetic (`ai-attribution/attribute.ts`, pure, tested).** Group the bill by (provider, normalized model, token type, currency) at whatever grain it has. Match each aggregate: exact normalized model, else a unique prefix match, else _ambiguous_ (several billed models; split by billed amount), else the provider-level line, else _unmatched_ (counted, never forced). Weigh: typed lines weigh only that token type; untyped lines weigh all types; list cost from a plugin `aiModelRates` card (Anthropic declares one, verified 2026-10-04) or the gateway's reported cost, else `DEFAULT_TOKEN_WEIGHTS`. Scale: fully priced line → callers get `listCost × min(1, billed/listCost)` and the rest is `(unattributed)`; unpriced line → whole bill by weight; no requests → all unattributed; non-positive (credits) → by weight. Every billed row in a group is split by the same fractions, so splits sum to rows and **billed totals cannot move**. `normalizeAiModel` is lossy on purpose (dates, `-v1:0`, inference-profile and vendor prefixes, dots → dashes), which is why ambiguity is reported rather than guessed; rate-card keys use the normalized (dashed) form.

**Storage.** Postgres: `ai_request_sources` (row is also the claim lease and the forward-only `collected_through` watermark), `ai_attribution_dimensions` (key → ordered metadata keys, ≤6 per org), `ai_attribution_days` (one row per org-day: per-source match stats, per-provider coverage, per-source collection flags; overwritten each run). ClickHouse: `ai_request_daily` (aggregates, 400-day TTL, **plain MergeTree + `collected_at`**: a remapped re-collection writes _different_ metadata keys, so ReplacingMergeTree would leave the old ones; readers take the latest `collected_at` per source-day) and `ai_cost_attributed` (cost_daily's columns + `run_at`, 3-year TTL; readers take the latest run per day, so a run is atomic and needs no tombstones). Both are in `ORG_SCOPED_CLICKHOUSE_TABLES`. Inserts use `wait_for_async_insert: 1` because a run reads what a collection just wrote. Old runs are not pruned (a few runs per day over a day's life; cheap under the `(org, day, run_at)` sort key).

**The attributed view (`cost-readers.ts attributedCostSource`).** When a query names a `caller:` tag key (group-by or filter in `queryCosts`, a rule in `getShowbackSpend`, the value/key pickers), the readers swap `FROM cost_daily FINAL` for a subquery aliased `cost_daily`: billed rows minus AI rows on days that have a run, `UNION ALL` the latest run's splits. Column refs, filters and visibility layers resolve against the alias unchanged. The splits table has no list or blended columns, so the split half projects zeros for them (`BILLED_ONLY_COLUMNS`): a split reads as amortized on the blended basis and as unlisted for re-rating, and a new `cost_daily` column a reader may touch under a `caller:` key goes in one of the two lists or that query fails as an unknown identifier. Every other query is byte-identical to before, so budgets/anomalies/exports that do not name a caller key read the bill as it was. `getCostTagKeys` adds `caller:*` keys from the attributed table, which is what puts them in every picker.

**When it runs.** Poller pass `runAiAttributionPass` (2 sources/tick, cost-exports claim protocol, 30-min lease, ≤7 days/pass, a day only after it has settled 3h, 6h cadence, setup failures back off 12h with the plugin's help URL). Each collected day is re-split immediately; `reattributeAfterCostCollection` (from `poller/cost-poll.ts`, rate-limited 30 min/org, no-op without sources) re-splits the trailing 4 days after any cost collection so restatements flow through. `POST /ai-attribution/reattribute` (≤92 days) does it on demand. Mapping changes reach history only via **Re-collect** (aggregates keep only mapped keys), clamped to the kind's `maxHistoryDays`.

**Permissions.** Reads `costs:read`; sources and the locations picker `org:settings:write` (authorizes reads of the org's logs, sometimes billed to its cloud account; audit-logged as `ai_request_source.*`); dimensions and reattribute `costs:write` (relabels spend, like cost centres).

**Surfaces.** One shared settings section (`ui/src/settings/AiAttributionSection.tsx`, key `ai-attribution`) for sources, dimensions, match-rate/coverage and a spend-by-caller bar list; desktop reaches it through the `cloud_settings_request` allowlist (`ai-attribution` added). CLI `infrawrench ai-spend [dim]` / `ai-spend sources` (`--json`). MCP `query_ai_spend_by_caller`, `list_ai_request_sources`. Terraform `infrawrench_ai_request_source` (LiteLLM `api_key` write-only) and `infrawrench_ai_attribution_dimension`. **Mobile deliberately has no dedicated screen**: configuration is org-wide settings (the anomaly-tuning line), and the read half reaches the phone already, because a dashboard cost graph grouped by tag `caller:team` renders on mobile like any other.

## Kubernetes cost beyond node compute

Volumes follow their mounting pod to a workload; a claim mounted by several goes to the **namespace** rather than being split N ways, because dividing a shared disk is an invention. Load-balancer Services match through `spec.selector`, which is equality-only, so the match is an exact subset test rather than a partial selector engine.

Two buckets join `idle` and `systemReserved` as nobody's cost: the **control plane** (a flat per-cluster fee with no per-workload quantity to divide by — correctly absent for self-managed clusters, whose control-plane nodes are already in `/api/v1/nodes`) and **unattached volumes** (bound and billing, mounted by nothing; the usual cause is StatefulSet `volumeClaimTemplates` defaulting to `Retain`).

**Egress is not attributable from the Kubernetes API itself** (`metrics.k8s.io` is CPU and memory only). It is attributed through the network-flow path instead; see "Kubernetes network costs" below.

The efficiency report **could not reuse `cost_reports`**: that config column is validated against a closed graph schema, `runCostReport` is hard-wired to the cost warehouse with no data-source indirection, and the numbers this report is about — requested, used, wasted — are computed live and never written there. It lives on the cluster's own surfaces instead.

It also **stops at the argument and names no target size**. The existing right-sizing is a discrete priced-SKU matcher over stored p95 quantiles; a pod request is continuous, two-dimensional per container, applied by patching a manifest, and the cluster metrics API is an instant with no history. None of those four pieces transfers.

## Kubernetes GPU cost

`plugin-kubernetes/src/gpu.ts` (pure) reads a node's accelerators off its extended-resource capacity and labels and expresses everything in **GPU-equivalents** (1.0 = one physical device), the only unit in which a whole card, a MIG slice and a time-sliced replica add up. MIG `mixed` resources are `nvidia.com/mig-<g>g.<mem>gb`, and the device plugin turns a profile's `+` into `.` (`1g.10gb+me` is advertised as `nvidia.com/mig-1g.10gb.me`); `single` strategy and GKE partitioning keep `nvidia.com/gpu` and say "slice" only in labels (`nvidia.com/mig.strategy`, the `-MIG-…` product suffix, `cloud.google.com/gke-gpu-partition-size`). Time-slicing/MPS advertise `replicas` units per card, so one unit is 1/replicas. Physical count comes from `nvidia.com/gpu.count` (or GKE/Karpenter/EKS Auto Mode count labels), never from capacity, which is inflated by replicas and MIG. **A MIG slice is priced by compute slices (g/7, g/4 on A30)**: it partitions the card exactly for every valid layout; memory-weighted pricing double-counts mixed layouts past 1.0.

The GPU pool comes **off the top** of a GPU node's rate before the 65/35 split, so a CPU-only pod on a GPU node pays for CPU and memory only, and unrequested GPUs are a `gpuIdle` bucket (`kubernetes-gpu-idle`, one row per node, tagged `gpu_model`). Workload GPU share is its own service (`kubernetes-gpu`), so `kubernetes-workload` now means CPU+memory only and the services still partition. Pool size, in order: an explicit per-GPU price (`gpuHourly` from the GCP plugin, which reads GPU SKUs out of the Cloud Billing catalog, or `gpu/<model>=` typed on the account), capped at the node rate; else a **ratio** against Compute Engine's published per-GPU and N2 component prices (scale-invariant, so it holds at billed or negotiated prices); else, for a model with no reference, the **remainder** after pricing vCPU and GiB at the component rates in absolute terms. A fixed "default GPU price" was rejected: it under-weights 8-GPU H200 boxes and over-weights a single A10G.

Utilization (`gpu-metrics.ts`) is DCGM / AMD exporter data through the API server proxy, Prometheus first (auto-discovered or the `gpuMetricsSource` credential; `none` disables), the exporter pods' `/metrics` second. Prometheus without `honorLabels` renames the exporter's `pod`/`namespace` to `exported_pod`/`exported_namespace`, which must win, or every GPU reads as the exporter pod's. MIG instances need `DCGM_FI_PROF_GR_ENGINE_ACTIVE` (GPU_UTIL is not reported there). **Time-sliced and MPS pods are always `null`**: DCGM cannot associate a shared device with one container. Nothing is fetched unless some pod requests a GPU.

GPU right-sizing is the deliberate exception to "Kubernetes names no target size": a MIG profile is a discrete catalog, a GPU request is one integer, and Prometheus has the history. It fires only from a seven-day p95 (never the exporter's instant sample), only when **every** GPU pod of the workload holds whole unshared NVIDIA devices on a MIG-capable model and is ≥24h old, and picks the smallest profile covering p95 busy and peak framebuffer with 25% headroom. Non-MIG models under 30% p95 get a "share it" finding with no money attached.

The CLI reaches the new dimension through `infrawrench costs --group-by tag:<key>` (the API already had `groupBy: "tag"`); MCP through `query_costs` and the plugin's stats/metrics tools.

## Kubernetes node and PVC labels as cost dimensions

Node and claim labels ride on the Kubernetes cost rows **as tags**, not as new `CostDimensionId`s, so group-by, filters, saved filters, budgets, allocation rules, billing rules, MCP and the CLI got them without a server change. Raw labels use reserved tag-key prefixes `k8s_node_label:` and `k8s_pvc_label:`; `client-core/src/cost-tag-keys.ts` is the only place outside the plugin that knows them (picker grouping via `TagKeyOptions`, the query-language shorthand `k8s_node_label['team']`, which compiles to `tag['k8s_node_label:team']` and formats back to the shorthand so round-trip holds, and the CLI's `--group-by k8s_node_label:<key>`). The plugin also always writes normalised node tags (`node_pool`, `capacity_type` = spot/on-demand/reserved, `instance_type`, `zone`) read from every provider's own labels (`plugin-kubernetes/src/cost-labels.ts`), and `storage_class` on volume rows.

**Node labels split rows; that is the cardinality risk.** (Merged over GPU allocation: a pod row carries `dailyCost - gpuDailyCost`, the GPU part staying on the per-workload `Kubernetes GPU` rows, and idle-GPU node rows carry the node tags too.) With a label context, `allocationToCostRows` writes a workload's compute **per pod**, keyed by `(service, resourceId, canonical tags)`, so one workload on spot and on-demand nodes is two rows under the same `resourceId` (`tags_hash` keeps them apart in ClickHouse). Idle and system-reserved are written per node-tag set too. The sum is unchanged; tests assert it. Per-node keys (`kubernetes.io/hostname`, anything ending `node-id`/`instance-id`) are refused, and each allowlist (`costNodeLabelKeys`/`costPvcLabelKeys` credential fields, multi-pick `providerOptions` filled from the live cluster) caps at 20 keys; blank means a small default list, `none` means no raw labels. PVC labels do not split rows (each claim is already a row) but still widen the tags map, hence the same cap.

Labels travel beside the allocation (`ClusterCostResult.nodeLabels`/`claimLabels`, `CostIndex.nodeAttributes`), never inside it: `cost-model.ts` stays label-free, which also keeps it out of the way of the GPU and network work on the same model. The efficiency report gains `nodeGroups` (pool x capacity type: nodes, node cost, idle, unused requests), cluster-scoped only.

## Kubernetes network costs

Pod-level network attribution rides the existing network-flow pipeline: the kubernetes plugin declares `manifest.networkFlows` and implements `fetchNetworkFlows` (`plugin-kubernetes/src/network-flows.ts`, sources in `network-sources.ts`), so a cluster's traffic lands in `network_flow_daily` behind the same org opt-in and forward-only watermark as VPC flow logs. Rows are workload-level (`namespace/Kind/name` as `src_ref`), never pod names, because Deployment pods churn and would mint a new pair every day.

**Three sources, strongest per pod wins:** (1) the cloud account's own VPC flow rows for the node, borrowed through the new host lookup `NetworkFlowFetchRange.observedEgress(refs)` (node `spec.providerID` → instance id → that day's egress by scope from _other_ accounts, `readObservedEgress`), split across the node's pods by their kubelet counters, with any excess left on a `k8s:node/<name>` row; (2) Cilium Hubble `hubble_flows_processed_total` with `labelsContext` workload labels, scraped per agent pod through the API server pod proxy on 9965. **Hubble counts flows, not bytes**, so its counts only weight the kubelet byte counter; the boundary follows from where the peer's replicas run, and Hubble's "world" is `unknown`, not internet (it includes in-VPC managed services); (3) kubelet `/api/v1/nodes/{n}/proxy/stats/summary` alone, `scope: unknown`, unpriced. Counters are cumulative since pod start and the plugin is stateless, so a day is lifetime-average rate × overlap with the day; pods gone by collection time are invisible. Host-network pods are never attributed (their counter is the node's). `maxHistoryDays: 1`. Each record carries `method` (`flow_log` | `in_cluster_flows` | `counter_estimate`), stored in a new `network_flow_daily.method` column (additive, DEFAULT ''); folding keeps the **weakest** method.

**Pricing is per account, not per plugin.** `NetworkFlowFetchResult.ratesFromPlugin` names the cloud whose card applies (from providerID scheme) and `rateOverrides` carries per-cluster `network/<scope>=rate` keys from the existing `nodeHourlyRates` field (parsed in the network module so `node-rates.ts` stays untouched). The host resolves it in `resolveFlowRates` (`collect.ts`): named plugin's new `manifest.transferRates` ?? its `networkFlows.rates` ?? the declaring plugin's own (empty) card, then `applyNetworkRateOverrides`. GCP and DigitalOcean publish per **GiB**; their cards are converted to per GB. Azure cross-zone is 0 (not billed since May 2024).

**`networkFlows.recut: true` keeps cluster rows out of every cross-account total**: pod bytes also leave through node ENIs an AWS flow log already counts. The org feed passes `excludePluginIds` unless asked for that account by id, skips recut rate cards, and exposes `recut` on account status so the UI can find clusters without naming a plugin.

**Billed allocation happens on read and is never written.** `kubernetes_network_settings` (per account, Postgres) stores a cost-query-language `billed_query` (text, compiled on each read; an empty-filter query is refused). `getKubernetesNetworkReport` (`server-core/src/network-flow/kubernetes.ts`) apportions per **day** with `apportionBilledDay` (`client-core/src/network-flows.ts`): factor `min(1, billed/estimate)` on priced rows, remainder explicit as unallocated; bytes basis only when nothing in the day was priced (labelled weakest). The sum handed out never exceeds billed; a day with no billed rows yet allocates nothing. Not in `cost_daily` because it would be a second opinion of the cloud's own data-transfer line. Currency mismatch between billed rows and the rate card yields an error, never a mix.

Surfaces: `GET /network-flows/kubernetes/:accountId` (+ `GET|PUT …/settings`, `costs:write`, audit-logged), shared `ui/src/cost/KubernetesNetworkSection.tsx` under the network section (billed source uses `CostFilterEditor`, so values are pickers), desktop cloud IPC (`cloud_network_flows`, `cloud_network_flow_settings_update`, `cloud_kubernetes_network`, `cloud_kubernetes_network_settings_update`; this also gave desktop the org network section it was missing), CLI `infrawrench k8s-network [cluster]`, MCP `get_kubernetes_network_costs` / `set_kubernetes_network_billed_source`, Terraform `infrawrench_kubernetes_network_settings`. **Mobile is a deliberate omission**, like the org network section it would sit under.

## Anomaly acknowledgement

Acknowledging writes the explanation onto the anomaly _and_ creates an org-wide annotation on its day, in one transaction — a failure between them orphans a note and a retry mints a second. Linked by one FK with a partial unique index, resolved backwards by a join rather than stored twice: two columns for one fact is how the two disagree.

An explained anomaly is **marked, not hidden or deleted**; the heading count becomes "N unexplained". **Detection never reads the acknowledgement columns**, so a later spike on the same key fires normally — an acknowledged spike is explained, not exempt, and a repeat of something you believed you understood is the finding you most want. Suppression lives in anomaly feedback (below), as exactly that: a separate, time-boxed, scoped object with an expiry, created by a verdict rather than by explaining.

Re-acknowledging rewords the note **text-only** (its date and scope may have been edited deliberately since). Deleting the note nulls the link but leaves the anomaly explained — removing a marker is not a retraction of the work.

## Budget alert notes (migration `0138`, API `1.64.0`)

A note on a fired budget alert is the anomaly-acknowledgement arrangement applied to `budget_alert_events`: `note`/`noted_at`/`noted_by_user_id` on the event (the record, restamped on a rewrite) and `annotation_id` → an org-wide cost annotation dated to the UTC day the alert fired (the artifact), written in one transaction by `web/src/services/budget-alert-notes.ts`. The four rules are the anomaly ones, stated once in `server-core/cost/anomaly-acknowledge.ts` and planned by `server-core/cost/budget-alert-note.ts` (`planBudgetAlertNote`, pure): mint once, reword text-only, a deleted marker stays deleted, and evaluation never reads the note (a noted budget is explained, not silenced). The link is one FK plus a partial unique index; `GET /cost-annotations` resolves it backwards by a left join into `CostAnnotation.budgetAlert` (`{budgetId, eventId}`), which the Terraform provider surfaces read-only as `budget_id`/`budget_alert_event_id` on `infrawrench_cost_annotation` (the same treatment as `cost_anomaly_id`).

**The follow-up is why this needed new columns.** A note goes back to where the alert went, so `budget-eval.ts` now routes with `{ track: true }` and stores `slack_messages` (`{installationId, channelId, ts}`) and `ms_teams_webhook_ids` on the event (`budgetAlertDeliveredTo`). `routeAlert` grew an optional `msTeamsWebhookIds` on its result, filled only when tracked; optional so the dozen hand-built results in tests did not all have to change. Slack gets a thread reply (`postSlackThreadReply`, plain `chat.postMessage` with `thread_ts`, no extra scope); Teams incoming webhooks return no message id and cannot thread, so it gets a follow-up card to the same webhooks. Budget alerts are never emailed, so there is no email leg. `postBudgetAlertNoteFollowUp` never throws and runs after the commit: by then the note exists, and failing the request would invite a retry that re-posts to every channel that did work. Gaps, by construction: alerts that fired before `0127`, and quiet-hours holds (delivered later by `alerts/pass.ts`, which does not write back to the event), have no recorded messages, so their notes reach the budget and the charts only. The response carries `followUp: {slack, msTeams}` and the composer says where it posted.

**Permissions:** `POST /budgets/:id/events/:eventId/note` needs `budgets:read` (to address the budget, which also applies the cost-visibility scope via `visibilityOwnerCondition`) and `costs:write` (the annotation's permission, as for anomaly explanations). Audit action `budget_alert.note` on the budget. Surfaces: `BudgetCard` lists this month's firings with notes and an **Explain/Edit note** action when the host wires `annotateBudgetAlert` (Costs panel only; dashboard cards show notes but no composer); desktop IPC `cloud_budget_alert_events`/`cloud_budget_alert_note`; CLI `budgets`, `budgets <name>`, `budgets annotate --note [--event]` (all `--json`); MCP `annotate_budget_alert`. **Mobile shows notes on its budget cards but deliberately has no composer**, the same line as anomaly explanations: it writes shared org state onto every chart.

## Anomaly feedback

A **verdict** (`expected` | `unexpected`, optional reason category and note) is a judgement of the detector and sits on `cost_anomalies` beside the acknowledgement, never instead of it: the acknowledgement is a fact about the spend that lands on charts, the verdict tunes detection. `explain: true` with a note runs the acknowledgement too, through the same service function. Migration `0127_anomaly_feedback` (renumbered at merge) adds the `feedback_*` columns, `suppressed_by_id`, `org_cost_anomaly_settings.feedback_tuning` (default true) and `cost_anomaly_suppressions`.

**Suppressions set spend aside; they do not mute keys.** Detection (`server-core/cost/anomaly-feedback.ts`, read once per pass by `loadAnomalyFeedbackContext`, never throws, degrades to "no suppressions") subtracts the scope's spend on covered days and judges the day twice: the full day must clear the bar (or nothing is stored) and the remainder must not (or the finding stands and alerts). A suppressed finding keeps its full amounts and gets `suppressed_by_id`; it is never routed, never texted, and never stamps `notifiedAt`, so it starts no cooldown. The link is (re)written only while a row is undelivered, which is what makes deleting or editing a suppression un-suppress a finding whose day is still in the 3-day re-judged window. A scope equal to the breakdown (a service suppression on the service breakdown) is an in-memory `Infinity` set-aside; every other scope (account, tag, cost centre, or a provider seen from the service breakdown) is one grouped `queryCosts` over the covered days per breakdown, capped at `MAX_SLICE_READS_PER_PASS`. Cost centres reuse the **cost visibility layer** (`runWithCostVisibility` with a synthetic one-centre layer) because that is already "rows the allocation rules give this centre", subtree included; there is no cost-centre dimension in ClickHouse. Recurrence coverage (`suppressionCoversDay`: one-off window, weekly weekday, monthly day-of-month with month-end clamp and ±1 day, seasonal date ±3 days) is pure in client-core and shared by the evaluator and the editor's "next covered" preview.

**One suppression per verdict.** `feedback_suppression_id` is the one a verdict owns: re-sending `expected` with `suppress` updates it, `unexpected` or withdrawing the verdict deletes it, and hand-made suppressions are never touched by feedback. Default lifetimes count from the later of the anomaly's day and today, or an old finding's one-off week would already have expired. Max 100 active per org (409), max 1096 days long.

**Sensitivity nudge** (`costAnomalySigmaNudge`, client-core): +0.5σ per `expected` verdict after the first on a (dimension, key) within 90 days, capped at +2σ and the 10σ ceiling; any `unexpected` verdict in the window cancels it. Spikes only. Derived on every pass from the verdicts (no stored state), so changing or clearing a verdict moves it back, and `feedback_tuning=false` switches it off without losing anything. `GET /costs/anomaly-sensitivity` explains each key; the web/desktop panels compose their own translated sentence from the counts, and the API's English `explanation` is for CLI/MCP.

**`feedbackTuning` is optional on `PUT /costs/anomaly-settings`** (omitted keeps the stored value), unlike `smsAlerts`, because whole-object clients (older desktop builds, the Terraform provider before this, config-as-code documents) already ship; config-as-code's apply falls back to the current value for the same reason, so an older exported document plans clean.

**Surfaces.** Slack: `infrawrench_anomaly_expected` / `_unexpected` buttons on every anomaly alert (`slackButtons`), handled in `slack-inbound.ts` behind the linked-member + `costs:write` gate inside `withPrincipalCostVisibility`; the verdict only (a recurrence needs choices a button cannot ask), answered `in_channel` so the channel sees who answered. Teams: incoming webhooks are one-way, so `AlertEvent.teamsActions` adds `Action.OpenUrl` links to `GET /api/anomaly-feedback?o&a&v` (`routes/anomaly-feedback-link.ts`), a session-authed page that only renders; the write is a CSRF double-submit POST like the Slack link page, because unfurlers follow URLs. Web/desktop: `CostAnomaliesSection` row actions + `CostAnomalyFeedbackModal`, `Suppressions` and `Precision` panels, sensitivity list and switch in Tune detection (desktop via `cloud_costs_*anomaly*` IPC channels). Mobile: verdict badges and an Expected/Unexpected sheet scoped to the row's own key; suppression editing, sensitivity and precision stay web/desktop. CLI: `costs --anomalies feedback|suppressions|precision|sensitivity`. MCP: `give_cost_anomaly_feedback`, `list_cost_anomaly_suppressions`, `get_cost_anomaly_precision`. Terraform: `infrawrench_anomaly_suppression` and `feedback_tuning` on `infrawrench_anomaly_settings`.

## Period-native plugins must date to the period _start_

Mistral dated an in-progress month's running total to a clamped month-end — a date that moved every collection, so each pass wrote a new `cost_daily` key instead of replacing the last. The month summed to the sum of its own prefixes: an inflation factor of **(N+1)/2**, roughly 16x over a full month, and permanent, because incremental collection never revisits days outside the restatement window.

**A `periodNative` row is dated to the period start**, which is stable across the period — the discipline Cloudflare, PlanetScale, Scaleway, Turso and OVH already followed. `restatementDays` must then be wide enough to _contain_ that start: a 3-day window straddles the 1st on three days a month and misses it on the rest, so the running month simply stops being collected. Mistral uses 62 — the smallest constant always containing the 1st of both the current and previous month.

Reconciliation's day-scoped guard is what let this rot: a monthly-native plugin files a whole month on one day, so "only days the plugin wrote" never covers the rest. `cost/period-scope.ts` widens the restated _unit_ — for a `periodNative` plugin a row on the 1st restates that calendar month. Deliberately only the 1st: Cloudflare anchors on arbitrary days, Turso on a due date, OVH on an issue date, and widening to "any written day's month" would let one flaky invoice page zero a sibling row.

## Invoice approval is a compare-and-swap

`computeInvoiceFigures` reads ClickHouse, so it cannot run inside the Postgres transaction without holding a row lock across an analytics query. Approval snapshots its inputs, computes, then re-reads the invoice **and** the customer under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and refuses with a 409 if anything feeding the figures moved — period, managed account, the customer's cost centres, accounts, cost basis, billing-rules flag, currency, name, or the customer being soft-deleted. The lock closes both orderings. Without it, a draft edited mid-approval froze the new period against the old period's numbers.

Void-with-supersede is one transaction covering the void, the corrective draft and **both** link directions; a half-applied supersede leaves an irreversibly void invoice with no path forward. The invoice-number retry loop wraps the transaction rather than sitting inside it, because a unique violation poisons a transaction.

Delivery attaches the breakdown rather than linking it — a link has to keep resolving and would serve a customer's spend to whoever holds it. Retry versus resend is drawn on whether anything landed: a failure with no delivered recipient retries freely, anything partly or wholly successful needs an explicit resend, and an attempt whose outcome was never recorded is treated as unknown rather than as failure.

## Efficiency alerts, and the null that must never become zero

Three trigger kinds — commitment expiry, idle commitment, unit-cost regression — routed through `alerts/route.ts` like every other kind. One `ALERT_TRIGGERS` entry in `client-core/src/alert-routing.ts` derives the rules picker, mute lists, push defaults and the OpenAPI enum. The **one axis that is not derived** is `PushNotificationData`, whose mobile `pushDataToPath`/`parsePushData` switches have no `never` guard — a missing arm compiles and silently drops the deep link.

**Idle detection returns an explicit skip before any arithmetic when utilization is `null`**, never `?? 0`. Unattributed accounts, unit-denominated commitments, missing data days and zero obligation all report null deliberately; treating any of them as zero pages someone about a commitment that is fine. Unit-cost regression applies the same rule to gaps: a day with no reported metric contributes to neither window, so flat spend across gap days reads as _improved_, not as a fabricated regression. Below the minimum reported days a window returns a distinct insufficient-history reason rather than a quiet "no regression".

Idle is `info`, not `warning`: nothing is breaking, the money is already spent, and the finding restates monthly.

## Cost per change / cost per deploy

"What did this change cost?", answered by joining the two halves that already existed: `resource_changes` / `deployment_runs` on one side, collected `cost_daily` on the other. For a change on day `T`, the resource's **per-day** spend over `[T-w, T-1]` is compared against `[T+1, T+w]` and the difference reported as a **run-rate delta** (money per day). A total would describe two spans of time; only a rate describes what the estate now costs to own, which is what the edit actually altered. `cost/change-impact.ts` is the arithmetic (pure, db-free, `__tests__/change-impact.test.ts`), `cost/change-impact-load.ts` the gathering, `client-core/src/change-cost-impact.ts` the wire contract plus every surface's phrasing. **Name collision to keep straight**: `cost/change-detect.ts` is _cost change alerts_ ("spend on this scope moved >X% vs the prior period"); this is a _resource change event's_ cost.

**Computed lazily on read.
